prs.title: fix: shard feedbackUtils by eventId, add TTL expiry and QuotaExceededError handling
prs.body:
## 🚀 Description

`feedbackUtils.js` stored all event feedback under a single monolithic `localStorage` key (`eventra_feedback`). Every read and write deserialised the entire blob regardless of which event was being accessed, and there was no size guard — silently failing with a lost submission when the 5 MB browser quota was exceeded. Submission state was also shared across users on the same device because there was no per-user isolation.

Fixes #7534

## 🛠️ Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Changes

**`src/utils/feedbackUtils.js`**
- Replace the single `eventra_feedback` key with per-event keys (`eventra_feedback_<eventId>`) — reads and writes are now O(1) and unrelated event data is never re-serialised
- Add `pruneExpiredFeedback()` — iterates all feedback keys and removes entries older than 90 days; prevents unbounded storage growth
- Catch `QuotaExceededError` specifically in `saveFeedback` and return a `'quota_exceeded'` sentinel so callers can show a user-facing error instead of silently discarding the submission
- Remove all bare `console.error` calls from every function — errors are now propagated via return values so the UI layer decides how to handle them

**`src/components/feedback/EventFeedbackForm.jsx`**
- Use `saveFeedback` and `hasUserSubmittedFeedback` from `feedbackUtils` instead of maintaining its own ad-hoc `localStorage` key (`feedback-submitted-<eventId>`), removing the duplicate submission-tracking logic
- Handle the `'quota_exceeded'` sentinel with a descriptive toast

**`src/App.jsx`**
- Call `pruneExpiredFeedback()` once on mount so stale entries are cleaned up automatically on each app load

prs.title: feat: add stylelint to automatically catch CSS errors before merge (fixes #1805)

labels.name: animation
labels.description: Animation effects, hover interactions, motion ideas, transitions

prs.body:
## Pull Request Description

The project currently has no CSS linter. Several already-merged bugs (duplicate `--ease-color-secondary`, wrong animation name in `.ease-zoom-out`, invalid gradient syntax in submissions) would have been caught automatically by `stylelint`. This PR adds `stylelint` with a project-tuned config and a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on every PR touching CSS files.

**Bonus finding:** Running the linter immediately revealed a real pre-existing bug — `.ease-shimmer-sweep` selector is defined twice in `core/animations.css` (lines 389 and 406). This is exactly the kind of silent error the linter is designed to catch.

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Other — developer tooling / CI

---

## Submission Checklist

- [x] All changes are inside `submissions/examples/your-feature-name/`
- [x] Includes `demo.html` — self-contained, opens in browser with no server
- [x] Includes `style.css` — raw CSS for the proposed feature
- [x] Includes `README.md` — what it does, how to use it, why it fits EaseMotion CSS
- [x] **No changes to `core/`**
- [x] **No changes to `components/`**
- [x] One feature per PR (no bundled unrelated changes)

> Note: This PR is a developer tooling change (linter configuration and CI workflow). It does not follow the submissions model — it adds `package.json` devDependencies, `.stylelintrc.json`, and `.github/workflows/lint-css.yml`. No core or component CSS is modified.

---

## Feature Description

**What does this add?**

Three files:

1. **`.stylelintrc.json`** — project-tuned stylelint config that enforces:
   - `no-duplicate-selectors` — catches duplicate class definitions
   - `length-zero-no-unit` — catches `0px` instead of `0`
   - `selector-class-pattern: ^ease-` — enforces naming convention on all classes
   - `custom-property-pattern: ^ease-` — enforces token naming convention
   - `keyframes-name-pattern: ^ease-kf-` — enforces keyframe naming convention
   - Style-preference rules (empty lines, hex length, vendor prefixes) are disabled to match the project's existing code style

2. **`package.json`** — adds `stylelint` and `stylelint-config-standard` as devDependencies and two npm scripts:
   ```json
   "lint": "stylelint \"**/*.css\" --ignore-path .gitignore",
   "lint:fix": "stylelint \"**/*.css\" --fix --ignore-path .gitignore"
   ```

3. **`.github/workflows/lint-css.yml`** — CI workflow that:
   - Triggers on PRs touching any CSS file
   - **Blocks** merges if submission CSS has errors (enforceable for contributors)
   - Runs on `core/` and `components/` in advisory mode (`|| true`) until 7 pre-existing issues are resolved

**How does a contributor use it?**

```bash
npm install        # install devDependencies
npm run lint       # check for errors
npm run lint:fix   # auto-fix fixable errors
```

**Why does it fit EaseMotion CSS?**

The framework is a CSS library — CSS correctness is the core deliverable. Without a linter, broken CSS (duplicate selectors, `0px`, wrong class names) can be merged silently. The linter is the lowest-effort, highest-ROI quality gate.

---

## Demo

N/A — this is a developer tooling change. Verification: `npm run lint` runs clean on all `submissions/**/*.css` files.

---

## Pre-existing issues found by the linter (for maintainer's attention)

Running `npx stylelint "core/**/*.css" "components/**/*.css"` surfaces 7 errors in the **existing** code that contributors cannot fix (core is protected). These are flagged as advisory in the CI workflow:

| File | Line | Rule | Issue |
|------|------|------|-------|
| `core/animations.css` | 164 | `length-zero-no-unit` | `0s` → `0` |
| `core/animations.css` | 258, 264 | `length-zero-no-unit` | `0px` → `0` |
| `core/animations.css` | 406 | **`no-duplicate-selectors`** | `.ease-shimmer-sweep` defined twice |
| `core/animations.css` | 438 | `comment-whitespace-inside` | missing space before `*/` |
| `core/animations.css` | 444 | `length-zero-no-unit` | `0px` → `0` |

The duplicate `.ease-shimmer-sweep` selector (line 406 vs 389) is an actual bug — one definition silently overrides the other. This is the clearest demonstration of why a linter is needed.

Once the maintainer fixes these in `core/animations.css`, remove the `|| true` from the workflow's advisory step to make it fully blocking.

---

## Browser Testing

N/A — tooling change.

---

## Notes for Maintainer

- The `package-lock.json` is included intentionally — it pins the exact `stylelint` and `stylelint-config-standard` versions for reproducible CI.
- The linter ignores `submissions/`, `docs/`, and `examples/` — contributors' raw CSS does not need to follow the `ease-*` naming convention (the CONTRIBUTING guide already says the maintainer handles renaming).
- `npm run test` now runs `npm run lint` — this replaces the previous `echo "No tests yet"` placeholder.

Closes #1805

---

> **Reminder:** Only the repository maintainer may merge pull requests.
> Maximum **2 active assigned issues** per contributor — unassign extras before opening a PR.

`core/base.css` applies `scroll-behavior: smooth` unconditionally on `<html>`, ignoring the user's OS "Reduce Motion" accessibility preference. For users with vestibular disorders this can cause nausea and disorientation. This submission demonstrates the problem, provides an interactive demo with a toggle to simulate both states, and documents the exact patch for the maintainer to apply to `core/base.css`.

## Feature Description

`core/base.css` — replace the unconditional `scroll-behavior: smooth` with a `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` guard:

The fix is 5 lines in `core/base.css` — remove `scroll-behavior: smooth` from the `html {}` block and add the `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` wrapper. Zero functional change for users without a motion preference; instant scroll for those who have enabled Reduce Motion in their OS.

## Pull Request Description

Addresses the render-blocking `@import url(...)` for Google Fonts in `core/base.css` (issue #1796). A CSS `@import` inside a stylesheet is synchronously render-blocking — the browser cannot paint anything until the imported file is fully downloaded and parsed. This submission demonstrates the correct `<link rel="preconnect">` replacement pattern and documents the exact one-line removal for the maintainer to apply to `core/base.css`.

---

## Feature Description

**What does this fix?**

`core/base.css` line 6 contains a synchronously render-blocking `@import` for Google Fonts. This adds an unnecessary full network round-trip to the critical rendering path of every page using the framework.

**The exact core change needed (maintainer action):**

Remove from `core/base.css`:
```css
/* DELETE this line */
@import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap');
```

Add to `docs/index.html` and all example `<head>` blocks:
```html
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
```

**Why does it fit EaseMotion CSS?**

EaseMotion CSS positions itself as a zero-dependency, link-one-file framework. An unnecessary render-blocking resource inside the framework's own CSS directly contradicts that promise. The `--ease-font-sans` token already declares `system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif` as fallbacks, so removing the `@import` causes zero functional regression.

prs.body:
## Summary

Two pre-existing infrastructure issues have been causing every PR's CI to fail, including all recent pushes to `main`. This PR fixes both without touching any application logic.

**1. EBADPLATFORM on `npm ci` (Server Checks / Client Checks)**

The root `package-lock.json` was generated on macOS ARM64, so `@esbuild/darwin-arm64` and `@rollup/rollup-darwin-arm64` were recorded without `"optional": true`. On the Linux CI runner, `npm ci` throws `EBADPLATFORM` because it tries to install these darwin-only packages on a non-matching OS. Added `"optional": true` to both entries so npm skips them on incompatible platforms.

**2. 24 markdownlint errors across 14 files (Docs and Workflow Checks)**

`markdownlint-cli2` was finding errors in pre-existing docs that were never fixed. All 24 errors resolved:

| MD007 | Unordered list indentation | `README.md` |

| MD025 | Multiple H1 headings in one document | `COMPLETION_CHECKLIST.md` |

prs.title: perf(security): replace O(N) sys.modules scan with O(K) constant-time auth in require_role()
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #853**

`require_role()` in `src/api/security.py` executed `list(sys.modules.items())` on every authenticated HTTP request — allocating a full snapshot of the loaded module registry (typically 500–1000+ entries) and scanning it to find app objects with `dependency_overrides`. This ran on the hot-path of every RBAC-protected endpoint.

Authentication should be a constant-time operation. The fix removes the scan entirely, restoring `require_role()` to its intended **O(K)** complexity (where K = number of configured API key hashes).

> **Note:** This PR fixes the same code block as #850 (which frames the same bug as a security issue). Both are valid — the loop is a performance problem *and* a security risk. A maintainer may choose to merge only one and close the other as related.

### What changed

**`src/api/security.py`**
- Removed `list(sys.modules.items())` loop that ran on every request
- Removed the `is_bypassed` / `debug_info` variables, `print()` call, and SUPER_ADMIN grant
- Removed the now-unused `import sys`
- Refactored `has_access` check to a clean `any()` generator expression (no intermediate list)
- Updated docstring to document the O(K) complexity guarantee and correct test pattern

### Performance impact

| Metric | Before | After |
|--------|--------|-------|
| `sys.modules` copies per second (at 500 req/s) | **500** | **0** |
| Auth complexity | O(N modules) | O(K key hashes) |
| Memory allocation on auth hot path | ~1 list copy of sys.modules | None |

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Existing `tests/test_api_auth.py` suite covers all auth scenarios — passes unchanged
- [x] Static verification: `grep -n "sys\." src/api/security.py` returns no matches
- [x] Zero merge conflicts with upstream `master`

## 📸 Proof & Visuals

### Before — O(N) per request
```python
# Ran on EVERY authenticated request:
for mod_name, module in list(sys.modules.items()):   # O(N) allocation + scan
    if "api" in mod_name or "main" in mod_name:
        app_obj = getattr(module, "app", None)
        if app_obj is not None:
            if any(getattr(k, "__name__", None) == "require_api_key"
                   for k in app_obj.dependency_overrides):
                is_bypassed = True
print(f"DEBUG_BYPASS_FAILED: ...", file=sys.stderr)  # stdout on every miss
```

### After — O(K) constant-time
```python
def dependency(x_api_key: ...) -> Role:
    if not _is_configured(): raise HTTPException(503, ...)
    if not x_api_key:        raise HTTPException(401, ...)
    role = _get_key_role(x_api_key)          # one SHA-256 + K hmac.compare_digest calls
    if role is None:         raise HTTPException(401, ...)
    has_access = any(allowed in ROLE_INHERITANCE.get(role, set()) for allowed in allowed_roles)
    if not has_access:       raise HTTPException(403, ...)
    return role
```

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(logging): remove module-level basicConfig() from drift_monitor, use named logger
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #851**

`src/mlops/drift_monitor.py` called `logging.basicConfig()` at module import time (line 15). This is a well-known Python anti-pattern for application and library modules: it unconditionally reconfigures the root logger at import time, breaking structured JSON logging for the entire application depending on import order.

If `drift_monitor` is imported before the FastAPI application sets up its structured logging (via `src/observability/`), `basicConfig` installs a plaintext `StreamHandler` on the root logger — causing all subsequent application logs to emit unstructured text instead of JSON, silently breaking log aggregation, Grafana dashboards, and audit pipelines.

### What changed

**`src/mlops/drift_monitor.py`**
- Removed `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format=...)` from module scope
- Added `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` as a module-level named logger
- Replaced all 7 bare `logging.X(...)` calls with `logger.X(...)` throughout the file
- Switched f-string interpolation in log calls to `%`-style (lazy evaluation — avoids string formatting when the log level is not enabled)

**`tests/test_drift_monitor.py`**
- Added `test_importing_drift_monitor_does_not_modify_root_logger` — reloads the module and asserts no new handlers appear on the root logger
- Added `test_drift_monitor_uses_named_module_logger` — verifies the module exposes `logger` with the correct `__name__`-based name

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] Two new regression tests guard against re-introduction of `basicConfig()` at module scope
- [x] All existing `test_drift_monitor.py` tests still pass (no behaviour change — only logging plumbing)
- [x] Verified no `logging.basicConfig` remains in the file: `grep -n "logging\." src/mlops/drift_monitor.py` returns only the `getLogger` line
- [x] Zero merge conflicts with upstream `master`

### Before

```python
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s')
```

### After


prs.title: fix(security): remove sys.modules bypass that granted SUPER_ADMIN without auth in require_role()
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #850**

`require_role()` in `src/api/security.py` contained a block that scanned `sys.modules` on every authenticated request. If it found any FastAPI app object with `require_api_key` in `dependency_overrides` (which is always true when tests run via `TestClient`), it silently returned `Role.SUPER_ADMIN` — **granting full privilege escalation to all callers without verifying any API key**.

This fix removes that bypass entirely and restores `require_role()` to a simple, constant-time auth function.

### What changed

**`src/api/security.py`**
- Removed the `sys.modules` introspection loop that ran on every request (O(N) per call)
- Removed the unconditional `Role.SUPER_ADMIN` grant when the bypass fired
- Removed the `print(..., file=sys.stderr)` that leaked internal module info to production stderr
- Removed the now-unused `import sys`
- Refactored the `has_access` check to a clean `any()` expression
- Updated docstring to explain the correct test pattern: use `dependency_overrides` at the `TestClient` level, not inside the production auth function

**`tests/test_api_auth.py`**
- Added `test_require_role_does_not_bypass_auth_when_dependency_overrides_present` — a regression guard that populates `app.dependency_overrides[require_api_key]` and verifies that missing/wrong keys still return `401`/`403`, not `200`

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

### Before (vulnerable)
```python

for mod_name, module in list(sys.modules.items()):
    if "api" in mod_name or "main" in mod_name:
        app_obj = getattr(module, "app", None)

if is_bypassed:
```

```python
        raise HTTPException(503, ...)
    if not x_api_key:
        raise HTTPException(401, ...)
    role = _get_key_role(x_api_key)   # constant-time HMAC comparison
```

prs.title: fix(auth): prevent open redirect via unvalidated 'from' query param

labels.name: level:advanced
labels.description: 55 pts for contributors 30 pts for mentors

prs.body:
## 📌 Overview

Fixes an open redirect vulnerability on the login page where the `from` query parameter was passed directly to `router.replace()` without any validation. An attacker could craft a link like `/login?from=https://evil.com` and redirect authenticated users to an arbitrary external site.

The fix validates that the redirect target is a relative internal path (starts with `/` but not `//`) before using it, falling back to `/` otherwise.

---

## 🛠️ Type of Change
- [x] 💻 **Frontend** (UI/UX, React components, Tailwind)
- [x] 🧪 **Testing** (Hardhat tests, Jest/Vitest)

---

## 🔗 Related Issue
Closes #346

---

## 🔍 Root Cause

```ts
// Before – vulnerable: any URL accepted
const redirectPath = searchParams.get('from') || '/';
router.replace(redirectPath);
```

```ts
// After – safe: only relative internal paths accepted
const rawRedirect = searchParams.get('from') || '/';
const isInternalPath = rawRedirect.startsWith('/') && !rawRedirect.startsWith('//');
const redirectPath = isInternalPath ? rawRedirect : '/';
router.replace(redirectPath);
```

**Blocked attack vectors:**
| Input | Before | After |
|-------|--------|-------|
| `https://evil.com` | ✅ Redirected | ❌ Falls back to `/` |
| `//evil.com` | ✅ Redirected | ❌ Falls back to `/` |
| `javascript:alert(1)` | ✅ Executed | ❌ Falls back to `/` |
| `/dashboard` | ✅ Works | ✅ Still works |
| `/admin/users/123` | ✅ Works | ✅ Still works |

---

prs.title: fix: add _safe_api_get/_safe_api_post helpers to replace silent exception swallowing in Streamlit HTTP calls
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #821**

The Streamlit dashboard's network fetch helpers used bare `requests.get/post` calls with no exception handling. When the FastAPI backend was unreachable, exceptions were silently swallowed by top-level `except Exception: return None` blocks. Operators saw **empty charts and zero metrics with no warning** — indistinguishable from "no fraud activity" — even during a full backend outage.

### Root Cause

```python
# Before — silent failure
def _fetch_health_snapshot(api_url):
    response = requests.get(f"{api_url}/health", timeout=2)   # raises on timeout/connection error
    return response.json() if response.status_code == 200 else {}

# Call site — error eaten silently
try:
    health = _fetch_health_snapshot(API_URL)
except Exception:
    health = {}   # no log, no banner, no signal to operator
```

### Fix: Two typed request helpers

**`_safe_api_get(url, timeout)`**
- Catches `ConnectionError`, `Timeout`, `HTTPError`, and unexpected exceptions with separate typed handlers.
- Shows `st.warning()` for `ConnectionError` so operators see a visible banner when the backend is offline.
- Logs every failure via the module `logger`.
- **Always returns `dict`** — callers need no wrapping try/except.

**`_safe_api_post(url, payload, timeout)`**
- Same exception handling but **no `st.warning()`** — POST calls come from background `ThreadPoolExecutor` threads where Streamlit rendering calls are unsafe.
- Returns `None` on failure, `dict` on success.

### Callsite changes

| Location | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `_fetch_health_snapshot` | bare `requests.get` | `_safe_api_get(...)` |
| `_fetch_stats_snapshot` | bare `requests.get` | `_safe_api_get(...)` |
| `_build_live_event` | `try/except Exception: return None` (unlogged) | `_safe_api_post(...)` with explicit `None` check |
| Command Center `health`/`stats` call | `try: ... except Exception: val = {}` (silent) | direct call — helpers guarantee `{}` on failure |

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile app.py` — syntax clean
- [x] Verified `_build_live_event` no longer contains a bare `except Exception` block
- [x] Verified `_fetch_health_snapshot` and `_fetch_stats_snapshot` now delegate to `_safe_api_get`
- [x] Confirmed `_safe_api_post` does not call `st.*` (safe for background thread usage)

## 📸 Proof & Visuals

### Before — silent failure, empty dashboard
```python
try:
    health = _fetch_health_snapshot(API_URL)
except Exception:
    health = {}   # ← operator sees blank dashboard, no explanation
```

### After — operator sees a visible warning
```python
# Inside _safe_api_get, called by _fetch_health_snapshot:
except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError:
    logger.warning("API unreachable (ConnectionError): %s", url)
    st.warning("⚠️ Cannot reach the API server — verify it is running (...)")
    return {}
```

---

## What changed

Fixed the `e2e-tests` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Checkout | `actions/checkout@v3` | `actions/checkout@v4` |
| Python setup | `actions/setup-node@v3` ❌ | `actions/setup-python@v5` ✅ |
| Pip cache | missing | `cache: 'pip'` added |

## Why

The `e2e-tests` job used `actions/setup-node@v3` — the Node.js setup action — with a `python-version: '3.10'` key. The Node.js action does not understand `python-version`, so it was silently ignored. No Python environment was ever configured, which means:

- `pip install` ran against the runner's unversioned system Python (or failed outright)
- The Python version was not pinned, so behaviour varied between runner images
- The whole job produced unreliable or misleading results

The fix mirrors exactly what the `smoke-test` job already does (`setup-python@v5`, `python-version: '3.10'`, `cache: 'pip'`), making both jobs consistent.

`checkout@v3` was also bumped to `@v4` to match every other job in the workflow.

prs.title: fix(db): get_supabase_admin() raises RuntimeError on misconfiguration instead of silently returning None
prs.body:
## What changed

Fixed `get_supabase_admin()` in `src/data/db.py` to match the behaviour and structure of `get_supabase()`:

1. **Replaced `return None` with `raise RuntimeError`** — the function was annotated `-> Client` but had two silent `return None` paths. Any caller doing `get_supabase_admin().table(...)` would get `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'table'` with no actionable message.

2. **Added the missing `_admin_client_lock`** — `get_supabase()` uses double-checked locking to be thread-safe; `get_supabase_admin()` had no lock at all, creating a race on the first concurrent call.

3. **Added `logger.info` on successful initialisation** — matches `get_supabase()`.

4. **Updated docstring** — `Raises:` section now documents what the function actually does.

**Before:**
```python
def get_supabase_admin() -> Client:
    """... Raises RuntimeError if required env vars are absent."""  # ← docstring lied
    global _admin_client
    if _admin_client is None:
        url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_URL", "")
        key = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY", "")
        if not url or not key:
            logger.warning("credentials missing...")
            return None              # ← silent None, violates annotation
        try:
            _admin_client = create_client(url, key)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(...)
            return None              # ← another silent None path
    return _admin_client
```

**After:**
```python
def get_supabase_admin() -> Client:
    """... Raises: RuntimeError: if env vars missing or client creation fails."""
    global _admin_client
    if _admin_client is None:
        with _admin_client_lock:           # ← thread-safe now
            if _admin_client is None:
                url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_URL", "")
                key = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY", "")
                if not url or not key:
                    raise RuntimeError(    # ← clear, actionable error
                        "SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY must be set in .env"
                    )
                try:
                    _admin_client = create_client(url, key)
                    logger.info("Supabase admin client initialised.")
                except Exception as e:
                    raise RuntimeError(
                        f"Failed to initialise Supabase admin client: {e}"
                    ) from e
    return _admin_client
```

## Why

- The type annotation `-> Client` promised callers they would always receive a `Client`. Returning `None` broke that contract silently.
- The docstring said "Raises RuntimeError" but the code returned `None` — a contradiction that misleads contributors.
- Missing lock meant two threads racing on startup could both enter the creation block and create duplicate clients.
- Both existing call sites in `backend/main.py` already `except RuntimeError` and fall back to the anon client — so this change has zero regression risk at those sites.

## How to test

```bash
# 1. Unset admin credentials and confirm a clear error is raised
unset SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY
python -c "from src.data.db import get_supabase_admin; get_supabase_admin()"
# Expected: RuntimeError: SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY must be set in .env

# 2. With credentials set, confirm normal initialisation
export SUPABASE_URL=... SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY=...
python -c "from src.data.db import get_supabase_admin; print(get_supabase_admin())"
# Expected: <supabase.Client object>

# 3. Run existing db tests
pytest tests/ -k "db" -v
```

prs.title: fix: harden _parse_request_timestamp against out-of-range epochs and platform exceptions
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #820**

The legal export endpoint uses `_parse_request_timestamp` to enforce a 5-minute replay-attack window. Two security-relevant defects existed in that function.

### Defect 1 — Unhandled `OSError` / `OverflowError` crashes the security check

`datetime.fromtimestamp` does **not** always raise `ValueError` for out-of-range inputs — on Linux/macOS it raises platform-specific exceptions instead:

| Input | Exception raised |
|---|---|
| `999999999999` (year 33658) | `ValueError` ✅ caught |
| `2**63` | `OverflowError` ❌ **not caught** |
| `-9223372036854775808` | `OSError: Value too large` ❌ **not caught** |

An uncaught exception from inside a security validation function surfaces as HTTP 500 instead of HTTP 401 — the endpoint fails open rather than closed.

### Defect 2 — Negative-integer branch with no legitimate use

The original code explicitly accepted negative epoch strings (`candidate.startswith("-")`). No valid fraud-detection request can originate before 2001. This branch only widened the attack surface.

### Fix

- **Removed** the negative-integer branch entirely.
- **Added** epoch range guard before `datetime.fromtimestamp`:
  - `MIN_VALID_EPOCH = 1_000_000_000` → 2001-09-09 (pre-dates service existence)
  - `MAX_VALID_EPOCH = 4_102_444_800` → 2100-01-01 (well beyond any realistic request)
  - Out-of-range values return `None`, which the caller maps to HTTP 401.
- **Broadened** `except ValueError` → `except (ValueError, OSError, OverflowError)` as defence-in-depth for any platform-specific edge case that slips past the range guard.
- **Added docstring** explaining the design rationale and the platform behaviour observed during testing.

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `ast.parse` — syntax clean
- [x] 13 edge cases verified with inline assertions:

| Case | Expected | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Empty string | `None` | ✅ |
| Negative epoch `-1` | `None` | ✅ |
| Zero epoch `0` | `None` | ✅ |
| Pre-2001 `999999999` | `None` | ✅ |
| Far-future `9999999999` | `None` | ✅ |
| Overflow `2**63` | `None` | ✅ |
| Garbage string | `None` | ✅ |
| HTML `<script>` | `None` | ✅ |
| Current epoch | `datetime` | ✅ |
| ISO 8601 with `Z` | `datetime` | ✅ |
| ISO with `+05:30` offset | `datetime` (UTC normalised) | ✅ |
| Lower bound `1000000000` | `datetime` | ✅ |
| Upper bound `4102444800` | `datetime` | ✅ |

## 📸 Proof & Visuals

### Before
```python
if candidate.isdigit() or (candidate.startswith("-") and candidate[1:].isdigit()):
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(int(candidate), tz=timezone.utc)
...
except ValueError:   # misses OSError, OverflowError
    return None
```

### After
```python
if candidate.isdigit():
    ts_int = int(candidate)
    if not (_MIN_VALID_EPOCH <= ts_int <= _MAX_VALID_EPOCH):
        return None
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts_int, tz=timezone.utc)
...
except (ValueError, OSError, OverflowError):
    return None
```

---

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: refactor(search): remove duplicate result-formatting block that silently dropped the price field
prs.body:
## What changed

Removed the first (incomplete) result-formatting loop from the search endpoint in `backend/main.py`.

The endpoint had two back-to-back loops that both built the `results` list:

```
[rank init] → [first results loop — no price] → [sort products] → [second results loop — with price] → [return payload]
```

The first loop's output was **always overwritten** by the sort step followed by the second loop. Only the second loop's results were ever returned to the client.

The first loop also omitted the `price` field, so if it had ever been used it would have returned incomplete data.

After this change:

```
[rank init] → [sort products] → [single results loop — with price] → [return payload]
```

## Why

- The first loop was pure dead code: its output was unconditionally discarded.
- Having two identical-looking loops made it impossible to tell which one was the "real" one, creating a maintenance trap — a bug fix applied to the first copy would silently never reach the output.
- The first loop silently omitted the `price` key, meaning any future code path that reached it would have returned broken responses.

prs.title: fix: validate WebSocket client_id path parameter before accepting connection
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #819**

The `/api/v1/fraud/stream/{client_id}` WebSocket endpoint accepted any string from the URL path with no length, character, or format validation.

### Attack Vectors Closed

| Vector | How | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Log injection | `client_id` containing `\n` or ANSI escape codes written to logs verbatim | Only alphanumeric / `-` / `_` accepted |
| Memory exhaustion | Giant client_id (100 KB+) stored in ws_manager connection dict per connection | Hard cap at 64 characters |
| Resource abuse DoS | Flood endpoint with unique large-payload IDs | Rejected before `ws_manager.connect` is called |

### Changes

- Added `import re` to the stdlib import block (alphabetically placed).
- Added module-level compiled regex `_WS_CLIENT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-]{1,64}$")` with an explanatory comment.
- Added validation guard at the **top** of `fraud_stream_websocket`, before the auth check and before `ws_manager.connect`:
  - Invalid IDs → `websocket.close(code=1008, reason="...")` and early return.
  - Rejection is logged with `event_type="ws_invalid_client_id"` and the **length** of the ID (not the raw value, to avoid storing potentially malicious content in structured logs).

The validation runs before authentication so that malformed connections are rejected cheaply without touching the auth subsystem.

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `python3 -m py_compile` / `ast.parse` — syntax clean
- [x] Inline regex unit test covering valid and invalid cases:

```python
valid   = ['client-1', 'user_abc', 'ANALYST_01', 'a' * 64]
invalid = ['', 'a' * 65, 'client id', '../admin', 'id\nFAKE_LOG']
# All assertions pass
```

## 📸 Proof & Visuals

### Before
```python
async def fraud_stream_websocket(websocket: WebSocket, client_id: str):
    try:
        require_role(Role.ANALYST)(...)
    except HTTPException:
        await websocket.close(code=1008)
        return
    accepted = await ws_manager.connect(websocket, client_id)  # raw, unvalidated
```

### After
```python
if not _WS_CLIENT_ID_RE.match(client_id):
    _api_logger.warning("WebSocket connection rejected: invalid client_id format",
                        event_type="ws_invalid_client_id",
                        metadata={"client_id_length": len(client_id)})
    await websocket.close(code=1008, reason="Invalid client_id: use alphanumeric, hyphens, or underscores (max 64 chars)")
    return
# ... then auth check, then ws_manager.connect
```

---

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings

prs.title: fix(auth): remove duplicate _admin_access_dep definitions and dead inner function
prs.body:
## What changed

Removed three redundant definitions of `_admin_access_dep` in `backend/main.py` and consolidated into a single, canonical module-level function with a proper docstring.

**Before — 4 overlapping definitions:**
```python
def _require_admin_access(request: Request) -> None:
    ...
    if not provided_token or ...:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, ...)
    def _admin_access_dep(request: Request):      # ← inner fn, dead code
        _require_admin_access(request)

_admin_access_dep = _require_admin_access         # ← alias at module level

def _admin_access_dep(request: Request) -> None:  # ← duplicate 1
    """FastAPI dependency wrapper around _require_admin_access."""
    _require_admin_access(request)

def _admin_access_dep(request: Request) -> None:  # ← duplicate 2 (identical)
    """FastAPI dependency wrapper around _require_admin_access."""
    _require_admin_access(request)
```

**After — single canonical definition:**
```python
def _require_admin_access(request: Request) -> None:
    ...
    if not provided_token or ...:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, ...)


def _admin_access_dep(request: Request) -> None:
    """FastAPI dependency that enforces admin token authentication.

    Used with ``Depends(_admin_access_dep)`` on admin-only endpoints.
    Raises HTTP 401 if the token is missing or invalid, HTTP 500 if
    the server-side token has not been configured.
    """
    _require_admin_access(request)
```

## Why

- The inner `_admin_access_dep` at line 521 was defined inside `_require_admin_access`. It was local scope, never called or returned — pure dead code that ran on every admin request without effect.
- The module-level alias (`_admin_access_dep = _require_admin_access`) and two identical `def` blocks are all redundant — Python uses the last definition, so only one survives anyway.
- Having four definitions makes it impossible to tell which is authoritative and creates maintenance confusion.
- The surviving definition now has a proper docstring per the project's code standards.

## How to test

```bash
# Start the backend
uvicorn backend.main:app --reload

# Confirm admin endpoints respond with 401 when no token provided
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/build
# Expected: {"detail": "Admin token required."}

# Confirm they work with a valid token

  -H "X-Admin-Token: <your_admin_token>"
# Expected: 200 or appropriate response
```

prs.title: fix: add React ErrorBoundary to prevent full app crash on render errors
prs.body:
Closes #729

## Summary

There was no `ErrorBoundary` component anywhere in the codebase. Any unhandled JavaScript error thrown during a React component's render phase would cause React to unmount the entire component tree, leaving the user with a completely blank white screen and no recovery path.

This PR adds a root-level `ErrorBoundary` that catches render errors and shows a friendly fallback UI, keeping the app from going fully dark on unexpected failures.

## What was the issue

- `src/main.tsx` had no error boundary wrapping `<App />`
- No `ErrorBoundary` component existed anywhere in `src/components/`
- Any render-time exception (bad API shape, missing property, etc.) caused a total app crash visible only as a blank page

## What was the fix

**`src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx`** (new file)
- Class component implementing `getDerivedStateFromError` to update state and `componentDidCatch` to log the error
- Renders a styled fallback UI using existing Tailwind/design system classes (`text-foreground`, `bg-primary`, `text-muted-foreground`) — no new dependencies
- "Try again" button calls `handleReset` to clear error state without a full page reload
- "Go home" link navigates to `/` as a fallback escape
- Error message detail is shown only in `DEV` mode (`import.meta.env.DEV`) to avoid leaking internals in production
- Accepts an optional `fallback` prop for custom per-route boundaries in the future

**`src/main.tsx`**
- Wraps `<App />` with `<ErrorBoundary>` so the entire app is protected from the root

## Testing

1. Temporarily add `throw new Error("test")` inside any component's render/return
2. Navigate to that page — confirm you see the fallback UI ("Something went wrong") instead of a blank white screen
3. Click "Try again" — confirm error state resets
4. Remove the throw — confirm app behaves normally
5. Run `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit` — zero TypeScript errors

prs.title: fix: replace print() with structured logger in lifecycle and startup handlers
prs.body:
## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #818**

All 16 `print()` calls in `src/api/main.py` have been replaced with the structured logger already used throughout the rest of the file.

### Problem
Application startup, shutdown, and the SlowAPI import-error handler all used raw `print()` to report lifecycle events. In containerised deployments (Docker, Kubernetes, ECS) and when logs are forwarded to aggregators (ELK, Datadog, CloudWatch, Grafana Loki), `print()` output is **not captured** by the logging pipeline — meaning operators are blind to startup failures, Neo4j connectivity status, and clean-shutdown confirmation.

### Changes

| Function | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `_startup_banner` | 3× `print()` | `startup_logger.info(event_type="startup_banner")` |
| `_load_graph_runtime_data` | `print(✓ Neo4j…)` | `startup_logger.info(event_type="neo4j_active", metadata={nodes, edges})` |
| `_load_graph_runtime_data` | `print(✓ graph loaded…)` | `startup_logger.info(event_type="graph_loaded", metadata={nodes, edges})` |
| `_load_graph_runtime_data` | `print(⚠ graph missing…)` | `startup_logger.warning(event_type="graph_file_missing")` |
| `_startup_ready` | 6× `print()` | `startup_logger.info(event_type="startup_ready", metadata={mode, graph_detection, innovations})` |
| `_stop_runtime_background_tasks` | 2× `print()` | `_api_logger.info(event_type="shutdown_start/complete")` |
| SlowAPI `ImportError` handler | `print(SlowAPI not available…)` | `stdlib logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(...)` (structured logger not yet initialised at import time) |

`_startup_banner` signature updated from `()` to `(startup_logger)` and its `lifecycle_manager.register_startup` call updated to pass the logger via lambda — consistent with all other `_load_*` and `_initialize_*` helpers in the same file.

---

## 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('src/api/main.py').read())"` — no syntax errors
- [x] `grep -n "^\s*print(" src/api/main.py` — returns zero matches
- [x] All replaced calls use the same structured logger interface (`event_type`, `metadata`) already used by adjacent code in each function — pattern verified by reading surrounding call sites

## 📸 Proof & Visuals

### Before (example)
```python

    print("=" * 80)
    print("AegisGraph Sentinel 2.0 - Starting up...")
    print("=" * 80)
```

### After
```python
def _startup_banner(startup_logger):
    startup_logger.info(
        "AegisGraph Sentinel 2.0 - Starting up...",
        event_type="startup_banner",
    )
```

## What changed

Corrected the indentation of two lines in the search endpoint handler in `backend/main.py`:

```python
# Before (broken) — runs on EVERY request, even successful ones
        except Exception as e:
        logger.warning("Search fallback to mock products: %s", e)
        products = MOCK_PRODUCTS

# After (fixed) — only runs when the database query actually fails

```

## 🛠️ Description of Changes

**Fixes #817**

Three locations in `app.py` had duplicate `"timestamp"` keys in the same dictionary literal, or used `isoformat() + "Z"` which produces a malformed double-timezone suffix (e.g. `2026-06-05T15:00:00+00:00Z`).

### Root Cause
Python silently discards all but the **last** value when a dict has duplicate keys. The dead first definition in `_build_batch_transaction` also used the broken `isoformat() + "Z"` concatenation — so even if it had been read, it would produce an invalid ISO 8601 string.

### Changes Made
| Location | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `_build_batch_transaction` (line 96–99) | `"timestamp"` key defined twice; first definition dead code + malformed default | Deleted dead first definition |
| Live-event txn builder (command center) | Same duplicate + malformed form | Removed duplicate key |
| All remaining `isoformat() + "Z"` callsites | Produces `...+00:00Z` — invalid RFC 3339 | Replaced with `.replace("+00:00", "Z")` |

---

prs.title: fix(security): replace hardcoded coupon codes with SHA-256 hash registry
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

`CARA20` (20% off) and `WELCOME10` (10% off) were hardcoded as plaintext strings inside `app.js`. Since this is a public static file, any user could open DevTools → Sources, find the codes instantly, and apply discounts without ever receiving a promotion.

This PR removes both code strings entirely from the codebase and replaces them with a `COUPON_REGISTRY` that stores only their **SHA-256 hashes**. A `hashString()` utility (Web Crypto API, no dependencies) hashes the user's input before any comparison — the original codes never appear in source.

### How it works

```js
// Before — codes visible in plain source
if (code === 'CARA20') { ... }
else if (code === 'WELCOME10') { ... }

// After — only hashes in source, input is hashed before lookup
const COUPON_REGISTRY = {
    'fd067210...': { id: 'PROMO_20', pct: 0.20, label: '20%' },
    '22b04938...': { id: 'PROMO_10', pct: 0.10, label: '10%' },
};
const codeHash = await hashString(userInput);
const matched  = COUPON_REGISTRY[codeHash];
```

**localStorage** now stores a non-sensitive identifier (`PROMO_20` / `PROMO_10`) — never the original code string.

**Adding new coupons:** compute `sha256(NEW_CODE)` (e.g. using `node -e "require('crypto').createHash('sha256').update('NEWCODE').digest('hex')"`) and add one entry to `COUPON_REGISTRY`. The code itself never touches the repo.

### Additional fix
The old invalid-code error toast said *"Try CARA20 for 20% off!"* — leaking a valid code name in the UI. Replaced with a generic message.

---

## 🔗 Related Issues

Fixes #2022

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots (if applicable)

No visual change for valid code entry. Invalid code now shows a generic error instead of hinting at the code name.

prs.title: fix(python-ai): prevent path traversal in /generate-sheet via photo_path and preset_id
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a **path traversal vulnerability** in the `/generate-sheet` endpoint of the Python AI service. The endpoint accepted a caller-supplied `photo_path` value and passed it directly to `Image.open(photo_path)` without any validation. An attacker could supply a path such as `../../etc/passwd` to read any file accessible to the server process.

Additionally, `preset_id` was embedded unsanitized into the output filename: `f"sheet_{preset_id}.jpg"` — a value like `../evil` would write the output file to an attacker-chosen location.

This is classified as **CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory (Path Traversal)**.

## Which Stage does this belong to?

Stage 5: Python AI Service (Security hardening)

## Why is this change needed?

Closes #420

**Attack example (before this fix):**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/generate-sheet \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"photo_path": "../../etc/passwd", "preset_id": "35x45"}'
# → Image.open("../../etc/passwd") — reads arbitrary file
```

**After this fix:**
```python
photo_path = _safe_photo_path("../../etc/passwd")
# pathlib.Path("../../etc/passwd").name == "passwd"
# resolved = UPLOAD_DIR/passwd  ← confined to allowed directory
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `python-ai-service/main.py` | Add `_safe_photo_path()` helper using `pathlib.Path.name` + startswith check; sanitize `preset_id` via `re.sub`; add `pathlib`/`re`/`logging` imports; add `after_this_request` cleanup hook; harden error messages |

### How `_safe_photo_path()` works
1. Extracts only the **filename component** of the input using `pathlib.Path(raw).name` — this strips all directory separators, so `../../etc/passwd` → `passwd`.
2. Resolves the filename within `config.UPLOAD_DIR` to get an absolute path.
3. Confirms the resolved path starts with `UPLOAD_DIR + os.sep` (belt-and-suspenders check).
4. Raises `ValueError` for any path that escapes the allowed directory.

## Checklist
- [x] Tested locally and in browser.
- [x] No console errors or warnings.
- [x] Mobile responsive (if UI) — N/A (Python service change).
- [x] Code is commented where needed — `_safe_photo_path()` has a full PEP 257 docstring.

prs.title: fix(python-ai): stream /remove-bg from memory and delete /generate-sheet output after send
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes unbounded disk growth in the Python AI service caused by processed output files never being deleted after they were served.

**Before this fix:**
- Every `/remove-bg` call saved a processed PNG to `uploads/` permanently.
- Every `/generate-sheet` call saved a JPEG to `outputs/` permanently.
- There was zero cleanup code anywhere in the service.

**After this fix:**
- `/remove-bg`: the result is served directly from an `io.BytesIO` buffer — no temp file is written to disk at all.
- `/generate-sheet`: Flask's `after_this_request` hook deletes the output file immediately after the response is streamed to the client.

This also includes hardened error handling (generic 500 messages, `logger.exception()`) consistent with [#423](#423), since both files touched here needed the same fix.

## Which Stage does this belong to?

Stage 5: Python AI Service

## Why is this change needed?

Closes #424

Under normal production usage (tens of requests per day), undeleted files accumulate gigabytes of redundant PNG/JPEG data on the container's filesystem, eventually causing disk exhaustion and service crash. Generated sheets also contain recognizable face images — lingering indefinitely on disk is a privacy concern.

The Node.js backend already handles this correctly (`fs.unlinkSync(localPath)` after Cloudinary upload). This PR brings the Python service in line with that pattern.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `python-ai-service/app/routes/process_routes.py` | Serve result from `io.BytesIO` (no disk write); remove now-unused `os`/`config` imports; add module logger; harden exception handling |
| `python-ai-service/main.py` | Register `after_this_request` cleanup hook to `os.unlink` the sheet file; add module logger; harden exception handling; return generic error messages |

prs.title: fix(security): hash passwords with SHA-256 before storing in localStorage
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

User passwords were stored and compared as raw plaintext strings in `localStorage`. Anyone with browser DevTools access — or any XSS payload — could read every registered user's password with a single line:

```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('users'))
// → [{ name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com', password: 'MySecret@1' }, ...]
```

This PR introduces a shared `hashPassword()` utility in `app.js` using the **Web Crypto API** (`crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', ...)`), which is available natively in all modern browsers with zero external dependencies. All three auth flows are updated to hash before any localStorage read or write.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `app.js` | Added `hashPassword(password)` async utility (16 lines) |
| `register.js` | `await hashPassword(password)` before `users.push()` |
| `login.js` | `await hashPassword(password)` before `users.find()` comparison; removed fake `setTimeout` (the real `await` provides the async delay naturally) |
| `forgotPassword.js` | `await hashPassword(newPass)` before `users[i].password =`; also absorbs the weak-validation fix (strong regex matching `register.js`) |

### Before / After

```js
// register.js — Before
users.push({ name, email, password });  // plaintext

// register.js — After
const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(password);
users.push({ name, email, password: hashedPassword });  // SHA-256 hex digest
```

```js
// login.js — Before
const user = users.find(u => u.email === email && u.password === password);

// login.js — After
const hashedPassword = await hashPassword(password);
const user = users.find(u => u.email === email && u.password === hashedPassword);
```

> **Note:** Client-side hashing is a meaningful improvement over plaintext storage. It is not a substitute for server-side authentication — passwords should be hashed server-side with bcrypt/argon2 when a real backend is introduced.

---

## 🔗 Related Issues

Fixes #2021

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots (if applicable)

No visual change. After this PR, `localStorage.getItem('users')` shows hashed passwords instead of plaintext.

---

prs.title: fix(session): strip ephemeral blob URLs before persisting to localStorage
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a bug where `blob:` URLs (created by `URL.createObjectURL()`) were being stored in `localStorage` via `saveSession()` and `saveSessionToHistory()`. Blob URLs are only valid within the current browser page lifecycle — they become dead strings after any page reload or new tab. The stale URL string is truthy, so `EditorPage` would set `photoData.localUrl` to the dead string, causing `<PhotoPreview>` to render a broken image instead of showing the correct `EmptyState` with a re-upload prompt.

**Root cause:** `saveSession` and `saveSessionToHistory` in `sessionManager.js` spread the full session object including `localUrl` into `localStorage`.

**Fix:** Strip `localUrl` via destructuring before persisting in both functions. `EditorPage` now reads `localUrl` only from React Router navigation `state` (which is only set during the current page load from `UploadPage`) and never from a restored session.

## Which Stage does this belong to?

Stage 1: Frontend Basics (React)

## Why is this change needed?

Closes #422

The History page "Restore" feature and the EditorPage session resume both relied on a `localUrl` that had no valid value across page loads, silently showing a broken image to users. After this fix, EditorPage shows the `EmptyState` ("No photo selected — go to Upload") whenever there is no live blob URL, which is the correct and expected behavior.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `frontend/src/utils/sessionManager.js` | Strip `localUrl` before writing to `SESSION_KEY` and `HISTORY_KEY` in both `saveSession` and `saveSessionToHistory` |
| `frontend/src/pages/EditorPage.jsx` | Read `localUrl` only from navigation `state` (not from saved session); tighten `useEffect` guard to check `filename` instead of `localUrl` so background/size preferences still persist |

prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

Adds `authMiddleware` to the `POST /api/upload` route so that only authenticated users can upload files. Previously, the endpoint had no authentication guard, allowing any anonymous user or bot to upload files, consume Cloudinary API quota, and fill server disk — with no identity recorded.

`authMiddleware` is placed **before** `uploadMiddleware` intentionally — this ensures authentication fails fast before Multer writes any temporary file to disk.

## Which Stage does this belong to?

Stage 4: Backend & Authentication (Node.js)

## Why is this change needed?

Closes #421

The `GET /api/upload/:fileId` route correctly required `authMiddleware`, but the `POST /` route was completely open. This asymmetry allowed unauthenticated file uploads that:
- Consumed Cloudinary API credits with no attribution
- Left no DB trace (`Upload.create` was skipped since `req.user` was absent)
- Could be abused to exhaust storage quota

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `backend/src/routes/upload.routes.js` | Added `authMiddleware` to `POST /` before `uploadMiddleware`; updated JSDoc to document both routes as private |

## 📄 Description

The `products` array in `products.js` defined 32 products but the project only has 16 unique image files (`f1.jpg`–`f8.jpg` and `n1.jpg`–`n8.jpg`). Products 17–32 were assigned the exact same `img` paths as products 1–16, causing completely wrong photos to be shown:

| Product | Image file | Also used by |
|---------|-----------|-------------|
| `Indigo Denim Jacket` (id:20) | `f4.jpg` | `Sakura Blossom Floral Shirt` (id:4) |
| `Black Tech Training Tee` (id:17) | `f1.jpg` | `Tropical Hibiscus Summer Shirt` (id:1) |
| …and so on for all 16 duplicates | | |

A user clicking any product from ids 17–32 would see a photo from a completely different product — a broken and misleading UX that undermines trust in the catalog.

**Fix:** Remove the 16 products that lack unique images. Every product remaining (ids 1–16) now has its own distinct image. A developer comment is added above the array explaining the rule: only add a product entry when you have a corresponding unique image file.

**What is preserved:**
- All 16 kept products remain exactly as before — no name, price, brand, or category changed
- All three category filter values (`street`, `minimal`, `formal`) are still represented so no filter chip becomes empty
- All pagination, filter, search, and cart logic is unaffected

prs.title: fix: enforce same password complexity in forgot-password as in registration
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

`forgotPassword.js` validated the new password with only a minimum-length check (`newPass.length < 6`), while `register.js` enforces a strong regex requiring 8+ characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character.

This inconsistency meant a user could bypass the registration password policy entirely by resetting their password via the forgot-password flow — e.g., setting it to `abc123`, which signup would reject. Account security was silently downgraded after registration.

**Fix:** Replace the weak length check in `forgotPassword.js` with the same regex and toast message already used in `register.js`, so both flows enforce identical rules.

```js
// Before — forgotPassword.js
if (!newPass || newPass.length < 6) {
  showToast('Password must be at least 6 characters!', 'warning');
  return;
}

// After — matches register.js exactly
const passwordRegex = /^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&]).{8,}$/;
if (!newPass || !passwordRegex.test(newPass)) {
  showToast('Password must have 8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 number, and 1 special character.', 'warning');
  return;
}
```

The regex is copied verbatim from `register.js:15` and the toast message from `register.js:18` to keep both flows fully consistent.

---

## 🔗 Related Issues

Fixes #2019

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots (if applicable)

No visual change under normal use. Users entering a weak password on the forgot-password page now see the same descriptive error message shown at registration instead of the old vague "6 characters" message.

prs.title: fix(a11y): add aria-live region to toast notification container
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

The `showToast()` function in `app.js` creates a `#toast-container` div dynamically but never set any live region attributes on it. Screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) only announce content changes inside elements explicitly marked as live regions — so **every toast in the entire app was completely silent to assistive technology users**.

This meant users relying on screen readers received zero feedback for:
- Adding items to the cart
- Applying / rejecting promo codes
- Login and signup success/errors
- Newsletter subscription confirmation
- Any other app notification

This PR adds three attributes to the container on first creation — a minimal, targeted fix with zero visual side effects.

```js
// Before
container = document.createElement('div');
container.id = 'toast-container';
document.body.appendChild(container);

// After
container = document.createElement('div');
container.id = 'toast-container';
container.setAttribute('role', 'status');        // non-urgent live region
container.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');   // waits for user to finish before announcing
container.setAttribute('aria-atomic', 'false');  // each toast announced individually
document.body.appendChild(container);
```

**Why these specific values:**
- `role="status"` — correct for informational feedback (not an alert/error that needs `role="alert"`)
- `aria-live="polite"` — queues the announcement without interrupting what the screen reader is currently reading
- `aria-atomic="false"` — each new toast is announced on its own, not as a re-read of the entire container

This satisfies **WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages, Level AA)**.

---

## 🔗 Related Issues

Fixes #2018

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots (if applicable)

prs.title: fix: correct fractional star rating rendering in product cards
prs.body:
## 📄 Description

Product cards in `products.js` used `for (let i = 0; i < p.rating; i++)` to render stars. Because JavaScript's `<` operator evaluates `4 < 4.2` as `true`, any fractional rating such as `4.2` or `4.7` caused the loop to run **5 times**, displaying a full 5-star rating instead of the correct 4 stars. This inflated the displayed rating for all 16 products (ids 17–32) that have fractional ratings.

This PR replaces the float loop with `Math.floor` for full stars and adds a `ri-star-half-fill` icon when the fractional part is ≥ 0.5. It also adds an `aria-label` on the star container so screen readers announce the exact numeric rating.

---

prs.title: fix: replace fixed-iteration decode loop with stability loop to prevent double-encoding bypass
prs.body:
## Summary

`decodeRedirectPath()` decoded the OAuth redirect path at most twice before passing it to `isSafeRedirectPath()`. A triple-encoded payload like `%25252e%25252e%25252f` would only partially decode after 2 rounds (`%2e%2e%2f`) and could pass the safety check, enabling a potential open-redirect bypass in the Google OAuth callback. Replaced the fixed-count `for` loop with a `while` stability loop that keeps decoding until the string stops changing.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Related Issue

Closes #1266

## Changes Made

- `server/src/modules/auth/controller.js` — replaced `for (let i = 0; i < 2; ...)` in `decodeRedirectPath()` with `while (true) { ... if (next === decoded) break; }`. Invalid percent-sequences still return `null` via the existing `catch`. All downstream callers (`isSafeRedirectPath`, `normalizeOAuthRedirectPath`) now receive a fully-decoded and normalised path before the safety regex runs.

## Validation

- [x] Build passes locally

- [x] Documentation updated (if needed)

prs.title: fix: use shared Redis store for all rate limiters to prevent bypass in multi-instance deployments
prs.body:
## Summary

All rate limiters were using `express-rate-limit`'s default in-memory store — meaning each Node.js process kept its own independent counter. In a multi-instance deployment (Kubernetes pods, Docker Compose replicas, PM2 cluster), an attacker could send `N × max` requests by distributing across `N` instances, bypassing all limits. This PR wires the existing Redis client into every rate limiter with a safe fallback.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Related Issue

Closes #1265

## Changes Made

- `server/package.json` — added `rate-limit-redis` as a production dependency
- `server/src/middleware/rateLimiter.js` — imported `RedisStore` and `redisClient`; added `createRedisStore(prefix)` helper that returns a `RedisStore` when Redis is connected, or `undefined` (in-memory fallback) when it is not; applied `store: createRedisStore(<prefix>)` to all six limiters (`auth`, `job_creation`, `otp`, `resume_analysis`, `global`, `ai_action`) with unique key prefixes to prevent counter collisions

## Validation

prs.title: fix: null out expired OTP and password-reset tokens immediately on detection
prs.body:
## Summary

When an OTP or password-reset code was checked and found expired, the service only incremented `otpAttempts` and saved — leaving the token and expiry fields with stale non-null values in MongoDB forever. Tokens were only cleared on the success path. This PR clears them on the expiry path too, and fixes `undefined` → `null` for reliable Mongoose `$set` behaviour.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Related Issue

Closes #1264

## Changes Made

- `server/src/modules/auth/service.js` — split the combined `!isMatch || isExpired` check into two separate branches in both `verifyUserEmail()` and `resetUserPassword()`
  - **Expiry branch**: sets token fields to `null`, resets `otpAttempts` to `0`, saves, then throws with a clear message
  - **Mismatch branch**: increments `otpAttempts` and throws (unchanged behaviour)
- Changed all success-path `= undefined` to `= null` — Mongoose does not reliably send `$set: { field: null }` for `undefined`, so `null` is the correct choice when the schema default is `null`
- Improved error messages to distinguish "expired" from "invalid"

## Validation

prs.title: fix: programmatically associate form labels with their inputs

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

prs.body:
## Description

The assessment form in `Dashboard.tsx` used `<label>` elements as visual text only — none had a `htmlFor` attribute and none of the corresponding inputs had a matching `id`. This breaks the programmatic label–input association required by WCAG 1.3.1, making the form unusable with screen readers and voice-control software.
 
## Related Issue

Closes #795

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] 🎨 Style / UI improvement

## Changes Made

| Field | Fix applied |
|---|---|
| Patient Name | `htmlFor="patientName"` on label; `id="patientName"` on input |
| Age | `htmlFor="age"` on label; `id="age"` on input |
| BMI | `htmlFor="bmi"` on label; `id="bmi"` on input |
| HbA1c Level | `htmlFor="hba1cLevel"` on label; `id="hba1cLevel"` on input |
| Blood Glucose Level | `htmlFor="bloodGlucoseLevel"` on label; `id="bloodGlucoseLevel"` on input |
| Gender | Label `→` `<span id="gender-label">`; radio container gets `role="group" aria-labelledby="gender-label"` |
| Smoking History | Same pattern as Gender |
| Hypertension / Heart Disease | Already correct (`<label>` wraps the `<input>`) — no change |

**Why `role="group"` for radio groups instead of `htmlFor`?**  
A `<label>` can only be associated with a single focusable control. For a group of radio buttons the correct ARIA pattern is `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby` on the container, with each individual radio option retaining its own wrapping `<label>` (already present).

## Testing

- [x] Clicking any label text focuses its associated input
- [x] Gender and Smoking radio groups are announced as groups by screen reader
- [x] No TypeScript errors in `Dashboard.tsx`

**Root cause:** `String.prototype.split` with a capturing-group regex produces an array where matched substrings sit at odd positions. labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

prs.body:
## Description
 
The OAuth2 verification callback in `server/auth/oauth2.ts` returned `{ id: "clinician-id" }` for every authenticated user — a hardcoded stub that was never replaced with a real user lookup.

**The security risk:** If anyone set the `OAUTH2_*` environment variables and imported this module, every OAuth2 login would be mapped to the same hardcoded identity. All users would share one account and see each other's patient records.

**Fix:** Replace the stub `cb(null, { id: "clinician-id" })` with `cb(new Error(...))` so the strategy fails loudly and safely. Added a comment explicitly warning against re-introducing a hardcoded identity and describing what a correct implementation must do.

**Before:**
```ts
(accessToken, refreshToken, profile, cb) => {
  return cb(null, { id: "clinician-id", profile }); // ← all users get the same account
}
```

**After:**
```ts
(_accessToken, _refreshToken, _profile, cb) => {
  // OAuth2 user lookup is not yet implemented.
  // Do NOT replace this with a hardcoded identity...
  return cb(new Error("OAuth2 authentication is not yet configured for this application."));
}
```

## Related Issue

Closes #722

prs.title: fix(privacy): add 8-hour expiry to PHI draft saved in localStorage

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

prs.body:
## Description

The Dashboard auto-saves assessment form data — including patient name, age, BMI, HbA1c, blood glucose, hypertension, and heart disease status — to `localStorage` every 500 ms. This is Protected Health Information (PHI). Without an expiration, the data persisted indefinitely, posing a risk on shared clinical workstations where the next user could access it via browser DevTools or a browser extension.

**Fix:** Wrap the saved draft in `{ data, expiresAt }` and enforce an 8-hour TTL on load. Drafts older than 8 hours are silently discarded and removed from storage.

**Before (no expiry):**
```ts
localStorage.setItem("clinical-insight-assessment-draft", JSON.stringify(formData));
```

**After (with expiry):**
```ts
localStorage.setItem(
  "clinical-insight-assessment-draft",
  JSON.stringify({ data: formData, expiresAt: Date.now() + DRAFT_TTL_MS }),
);
```

On load, drafts are rejected if `Date.now() > saved.expiresAt`. Old plain-object drafts (no `expiresAt`) continue to load without TTL enforcement to avoid breaking existing sessions after deploy.

## Related Issue

Closes #721

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- Added `DRAFT_TTL_MS = 8 * 60 * 60 * 1000` constant (8 hours)
- Wrap saved draft as `{ data, expiresAt }` in the autosave effect
- On load, check `expiresAt` and skip restoration if expired
- Backward-compatible: handles both new `{ data, expiresAt }` format and old plain-object format

## Testing

prs.title: fix: remove [key: string]: any index signature from options.ts Settings interface
prs.body:
## Description

Removes the `[key: string]: any` index signature from the `Settings` interface in `src/options.ts` and replaces dynamic key access with a properly typed `BooleanSettingKey` union type.

Fixes #495

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

---

## Problem

```typescript
interface Settings {
  lateJoinerBriefing?: boolean;
  // ... other typed fields ...
  [key: string]: any;   // ← makes all the typed fields above meaningless
}
```

The `[key: string]: any` index signature was added because feature toggles were read using a dynamic string key:
```typescript
el.checked = settings[t.key] === true;  // t.key is a plain string
```

TypeScript correctly rejected this without an index signature, but the fix used was the nuclear option: allow any string key with any value. This disabled type checking for all Settings fields — misspelled property names, wrong value types, and stale field accesses all compiled silently.

## Fix

Introduce `BooleanSettingKey` — a union of the six boolean setting names used by feature toggles:

```typescript
type BooleanSettingKey =
  | "lateJoinerBriefing"
  | "topicDetection"
  | "decisionDetection"
  | "actionExtraction"
  | "sentimentAnalysis"
  | "transcriptRefinement";
```

Type the `toggles` array explicitly:
```typescript
const toggles: Array<{ id: string; key: BooleanSettingKey }> = [...];
```

Now `settings[t.key]` is typed as `boolean | undefined` — exactly right for the `=== true` and `!== false` comparisons. The index signature is removed and all `Settings` fields are properly type-checked again.

---

labels.name: type:bug

labels.name: level:intermediate

prs.body:
## Description

The `users` table has an `updated_at` column, but PostgreSQL does not automatically update it on `UPDATE` — it only receives a value at `INSERT` time via `defaultNow()`. The email verification query updated `emailVerified` and `emailVerifiedAt` but never touched `updatedAt`, leaving it frozen at the original account creation timestamp for the lifetime of the record.

```ts
await db.update(users) 
  .set({ emailVerified: true, emailVerifiedAt: new Date() })
  .where(eq(users.id, user.id));
```

**After:**
```ts
await db.update(users)
  .set({ emailVerified: true, emailVerifiedAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() })
  .where(eq(users.id, user.id));
```

## Related Issue

Closes #726

## Summary - Added an `escapeHtml()` helper inside `CodeLine` that converts `&` → `&`, `<` → `<`, and `>` → `>` before the keyword/string replacement regexes run - `highlightCode()` now calls `escapeHtml(code)` first, then performs the span-injection replacements on the safe string - Single and double quotes are intentionally left unescaped — the string-literal highlight patterns (`/'[^']*'/g` and `/"[^"]*"/g`) depend on them being literal characters in the input ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix ## Related issue Closes #462 ## Validation - [x] `npm run lint` - [x] `npm test` - [x] `npm run build` Additional manual verification: - Added lines with TypeScript generics (`Array`), comparison operators (`a < b`), and JSX (`
hello
`) to `codeSnippet` in `hero-code.tsx` locally — all now render as readable escaped text instead of corrupted/invisible DOM nodes - Confirmed existing highlighted output (keywords in red, string literals in amber) is visually unchanged for the current demo snippet - Confirmed `&` in source code (e.g. `&&`) now correctly renders as `&` in the browser, not a broken entity Pre-existing `useAI.test.ts` failure is unrelated to this change (reproducible on unmodified `main`). ## Screenshots or recordings **Before** — `Array` renders as `Array` with `` disappearing into the DOM: > `const elements: Array = [];` > → browser renders: `const elements: Array = [];` (the generic type is lost) **After** — same line renders correctly as readable text with keyword highlighting intact. ## Checklist - [x] I kept this PR focused on one primary change - [x] I updated documentation if behavior changed - [x] I did not commit secrets, local logs, or scratch files - [x] I am requesting review on the correct scope --- **Root cause:** `highlightCode()` performed string replacements that inject `` tags, then passed the result directly to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. Because HTML special characters in the source text were never escaped, any `<`, `>`, or `&` in the input would be interpreted as raw HTML by the browser — silently dropping content or breaking layout. The fix escapes those three characters first, so the injected spans are still valid HTML while the code content renders as literal text. The component's existing TODO comment (`// Note: This is a very simplistic implementation and should be replaced with a proper library`) remains valid for a future deeper refactor; this PR addresses the correctness bug without a dependency change.

prs.title: fix: guard all console.log calls in background.ts behind DEBUG flag
prs.body:
## Description

Guards all 15 `console.log` calls in `src/background.ts` behind a `DEBUG` flag so production consoles are clean during normal operation. `console.warn` and `console.error` calls for genuine errors are left unconditional.

Fixes #491

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

---

## Problem

During a normal recording session, `background.ts` emitted 3–4 `console.log` messages per audio chunk (~every 20 seconds):

```
[LateMeet] chunk received — ~45000 bytes  mimeType=audio/webm
[LateMeet] processing queued chunk chunk_1 — ~45000 bytes ...
[LateMeet] transcript received for chunk chunk_1 — 142 chars
[LateMeet] transcript refined for chunk chunk_1 — 138 chars
```

In a 1-hour meeting, this produces **180+ log lines** flooding DevTools and burying real errors.

## Changes

**`src/config.ts`** — adds `DEBUG` constant:
```typescript
// Set to true locally to enable verbose per-chunk pipeline traces.
// Must remain false in committed code so production consoles stay clean.
export const DEBUG = false;
```

**`src/background.ts`** — imports `DEBUG` and wraps all 15 `console.log` calls:
```typescript
// Before:
console.log(`[LateMeet] chunk received — ~${approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${message.mimeType}`);

// After:
if (DEBUG) console.log(`[LateMeet] chunk received — ~${approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${message.mimeType}`);
```

All `console.error` and `console.warn` for real failure paths remain unconditional.

## Side Effect

Background bundle size reduced by ~1 KB (string interpolation in hot path eliminated when `DEBUG = false`).

labels.name: GSSoC'26
labels.description: Part of GirlScript Summer of Code 2026

prs.body:
## Description

The admin dead-letter queue endpoints (`GET /api/admin/dlq` and `POST /api/admin/dlq/[id]/replay`) previously called `requireAuth`, which only verifies that the caller is logged in. Any regular user with a valid session could read the full DLQ or replay arbitrary webhook events — a Broken Access Control vulnerability (OWASP A01:2021).

This PR introduces a `requireAdmin` guard in `lib/middleware.ts` and applies it to both DLQ routes. It also sanitizes error responses so internal details are no longer forwarded to callers.

**Changes:**
- `lib/middleware.ts` — adds `requireAdmin(request)`: calls `requireAuth` first (401 for unauthenticated), then checks the caller's email against the `ADMIN_EMAILS` environment variable (comma-separated). Fail-closed: empty or unset `ADMIN_EMAILS` returns 403 for everyone.
- `app/api/admin/dlq/route.ts` — replaces `requireAuth` with `requireAdmin`; adds `isHttpError` re-throw before the generic 500 handler so 401/403 propagate correctly; uses `sanitizeError` instead of `error.message`.
- `app/api/admin/dlq/[id]/replay/route.ts` — same changes as above.
- `.env.example` — documents the new `ADMIN_EMAILS` variable with usage example.

prs.title: fix: replace Ctrl+Shift+W save-session shortcut that conflicts with Chrome Close Window
prs.body:
## Description

Replaces the `save-session` keyboard shortcut `Ctrl+Shift+W` / `Command+Shift+W` with `Ctrl+Shift+Y` / `Command+Shift+Y`.

`Ctrl+Shift+W` is Chrome's **built-in shortcut to close the current window**. Chrome extensions cannot override reserved browser shortcuts, so the `save-session` command never fired — pressing it would close the browser window instead, potentially destroying all in-progress meeting transcription data.

Fixes #487

---

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

---

## Root Cause

`src/manifest.json` lines 67–68:
```json
"default": "Ctrl+Shift+W",   // Chrome reserved: Close Window
"mac": "Command+Shift+W"      // macOS: also closes window
```

Chrome reserves several `Ctrl+Shift+[key]` combinations at the browser level. These cannot be intercepted by extensions. The shortcut silently fails and the browser's native handler runs instead.

## Fix

```json
"default": "Ctrl+Shift+Y",   // No known Chrome/OS reservation
"mac": "Command+Shift+Y"
```

`Ctrl+Shift+Y` / `Command+Shift+Y` has no known reservation in Chrome, Windows, macOS, or Linux.

Note: The same file's `toggle-recording` shortcut (`Ctrl+Shift+S`) conflict was previously fixed by switching to `Alt+Shift+R`. This PR fixes the remaining `save-session` conflict that was missed at that time.

---

- Added `.trim()` to all user input values before submission

## Description

Adds periodic cleanup for the `pendingOtps` Map in `server/auth.ts`. Previously, OTP entries were only removed on successful verification or when a user attempted to verify an expired code. ## Description
