issues.body:
## Bug

Commit `9ab19325` (PR #871 — "perf(ml): vectorize batch predictions") introduced a broken `interpret_predictions_batch` function in `analyze.py`.

**Root cause:** The function was written with leftover code from the old single-record `interpret_prediction` at the top — it references `input_data` (undefined in this scope; the parameter is `input_data_list`) and uses `n_samples`/`n_features` before they are defined, causing an `UnboundLocalError` on every call.

**Affected line:** `analyze.py:338` — `cached = cache.get(input_data)`

**Fix:** Remove the stale preamble and initialize dimensions before the NumPy pre-allocation:
```python
n_samples = len(input_data_list)
n_features = len(features)
X_input = np.zeros((n_samples, n_features))
```

This fix has been applied to PRs #930 and #933 to unblock their CI. The bug exists on `main` and will affect any future branch that merges from `main`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Leaderboard page shows GitHub contributors instead of quiz leaderboard data from the backend API

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Indicates that the pull request or issue is currently under review.

issues.body:
### Bug Summary

The leaderboard page fetches GitHub contributor data and converts `contributions * 150` into a fake "score", completely ignoring the existing `GET /api/leaderboard` backend endpoint that computes real quiz rankings. When the GitHub request fails, the page falls back to hardcoded demo users.

### Bug Description

**What is happening:**
`src/pages/leaderboard/index.tsx` calls `https://api.github.com/repos/ajay-dhangar/algo/contributors` and maps each contributor's commit count into a synthetic score. If that request fails, it renders a hardcoded list of fictional users (`"Jane_DevOps"`, `"NeonNinja"`, `"StackOverlord"`) with Unsplash avatar URLs.

Meanwhile, `server/server.js` exposes `GET /api/leaderboard` which queries `QuizAttempt` records and returns real per-user scores and attempt counts — but nothing in the frontend consumes this endpoint.

**Why this matters:**
- Users who complete quizzes never see their results on the leaderboard; the backend scores are computed and saved but never displayed.
- The page misleads users: it looks like a quiz performance board but actually ranks GitHub committers.
- The fallback demo data (fictional usernames, stock photo avatars) is visible in production whenever the GitHub API is rate-limited or unavailable.

**Relevant files:**
- `src/pages/leaderboard/index.tsx` — lines 35–105
- `server/server.js` — line 282 (`GET /api/leaderboard`)
- `src/utils/api.ts` — `useApiBaseUrl` / `buildApiUrl` utilities already available

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the leaderboard page in the browser.
2. Observe that all listed users are GitHub contributors ranked by commit count, not quiz participants ranked by score.
3. To see the fallback: throttle the GitHub API (or exceed its rate limit) and reload — fictional users with Unsplash photos appear instead.
4. Submit a quiz attempt through the quiz flow and check the leaderboard — the user does not appear.

### Expected Behavior

The leaderboard page should call `GET /api/leaderboard` (using `useApiBaseUrl()` and `buildApiUrl`) and display real quiz rankings. If the API is unavailable, it should show an empty state or an error message — not fabricated users.

### Actual Behavior

The page calls the GitHub contributors API, ignores the quiz leaderboard API entirely, and renders hardcoded demo data as a fallback.

### Severity

Major - impacts significant functionality

### Environment

- [x] Local Development
- [x] Production

### Suggested Fix

1. Replace the `axios.get(github contributors URL)` call with a call to `buildApiUrl(apiBaseUrl, "/api/leaderboard")`.
2. Map the backend response fields (`userId`, `totalScore`, `attemptsCount`) into the existing `LeaderNode` interface.
3. Remove the hardcoded fallback array; replace it with an empty state or a clear error message.
4. If a GitHub contributor view is still desired, move it to a separate dedicated "Contributors" page.
5. The `useApiBaseUrl` hook is already present in `src/utils/api.ts` and used elsewhere — reuse it here.

issues.title: [Bug]: Backend tests duplicate route logic instead of testing the real Express app

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Indicates that the pull request or issue is currently under review.

issues.body:
### Bug Summary

`server/tests/api.test.js` creates a brand-new Express app inside the test file and reimplements the routes from `server/server.js`. This means tests can pass even when the production routes are broken.

### Bug Description

**What is happening:**
Inside `runTests()`, the test file imports `express`, `cors`, and the models, then manually reconstructs the same routes it is supposed to test — the comment in the file even says `// Test endpoints (identical logic to server.js)`. The real `server.js` is never imported or started.

As a result:
- Validation rules, middleware order, rate-limiting behaviour, and response shapes in `server.js` are completely untested.
- A contributor can change production logic in `server.js` while the copied test implementation stays green — the test suite gives false confidence.
- Edge cases such as invalid quiz IDs, malformed payloads, and leaderboard query accuracy are not covered.

**Relevant files:**
- `server/tests/api.test.js` — lines 82–100 (the duplicated route reconstruction)
- `server/server.js` — the actual production app that is never imported

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `server/tests/api.test.js` and find the comment `// 2. Start the Express App programmatically`.
2. Observe that it creates `const app = express()` and re-declares `app.post("/api/quiz-attempts", ...)` inline rather than importing `server.js`.
3. Introduce a deliberate breaking change in `server/server.js` (e.g. change the error response key or add a required validation field).
4. Run the test suite — tests still pass because they are running against the copied implementation, not the changed production file.

### Expected Behavior

Tests should import and start the real Express app from `server/server.js` (or a shared `app.js`) so that any regression in production logic is caught immediately.

### Actual Behavior

Tests run against a manually reconstructed copy of the routes. Production regressions go undetected.

### Severity

Major - impacts significant functionality

### Environment

- [x] Local Development

### Suggested Fix

1. Refactor `server/server.js` to export the configured Express `app`:
   ```js
   // app.js — exports configured app
   module.exports = app;

   // server.js — entry point only
   const app = require('./app');
   app.listen(PORT);
   ```
2. Update `server/tests/api.test.js` to import the real app:
   ```js
   const app = require('../app');
   const server = app.listen(TEST_PORT);
   ```
3. Add `supertest` for cleaner HTTP assertions without managing a real port.
4. Expand test coverage for:
   - Invalid/missing payload fields
   - Unknown quiz IDs (expect 404)
   - Real leaderboard aggregation results
   - Rate-limit enforcement on `/api/quiz-attempts`

issues.title: [Bug]: /api/execute-code runs untrusted code directly on the host without any sandbox or resource limits

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Indicates that the pull request or issue is currently under review.

issues.body:
### Bug Summary

The `/api/execute-code` endpoint executes arbitrary Python, C++, and Java code directly on the host server using `child_process.exec` with no sandbox, process isolation, CPU/memory limits, filesystem restrictions, or network restrictions.

### Bug Description

**What is happening:**
`server/server.js` accepts user-submitted code, writes it to `os.tmpdir()`, and runs it via shell commands like `python "${filename}"`, `g++ ... && ...`, or `cd "${tempDir}" && javac ... && java ...`. The only protection in place is a 10-second timeout and a 10MB output buffer.

There is no:
- Sandbox or container isolation (Docker, firejail, nsjail, etc.)
- Per-request CPU or memory limit
- Filesystem restriction (submitted code can read/write arbitrary paths)
- Network restriction (submitted code can open outbound connections)
- Request body size limit on `express.json()`
- Rate limiting specific to this endpoint (the `scoreSubmitLimiter` only covers `/api/quiz-attempts`)

**What should happen:**
Untrusted code should never run directly on the host. It must be executed inside an isolated environment with strict resource and filesystem boundaries.

**Relevant files:**
- `server/server.js` — lines 170–260 (the `/api/execute-code` route)
- `src/pages/playground/index.tsx` — the frontend that submits code

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a POST request to `/api/execute-code` with `language: "python"` and `code` set to any of the following:
   - `import os; print(os.listdir('/'))` — reads host filesystem
   - `import subprocess; subprocess.run(['curl', 'http://attacker.com'])` — outbound network call
   - `while True: pass` — CPU exhaustion (blocked only after 10s timeout, but many concurrent requests can exhaust the server)
   - A large recursive program to exhaust stack/memory before the timeout fires

### Expected Behavior

Code submitted by users should be executed inside an isolated sandbox with enforced CPU time, memory, wall-clock time, stdout/stderr size, and filesystem access limits. The host filesystem and network should be unreachable from submitted code.

### Actual Behavior

Submitted code runs directly on the host process with the same permissions as the Node.js server, with access to the filesystem, environment variables, and the network.

### Severity

Major - impacts significant functionality

### Environment

- [x] Local Development
- [x] Production

### System Information (Optional)

Node.js backend, `child_process.exec`, `os.tmpdir()`.

### Suggested Fix

- Wrap execution in Docker/firejail/nsjail or delegate to a remote code execution judge (e.g. Judge0, Piston API).
- Add `express.json({ limit: '10kb' })` to cap request body size.
- Add an endpoint-specific rate limiter for `/api/execute-code`.
- Use `execFile`/`spawn` with fixed argument arrays instead of shell command strings to prevent shell injection.
- Create a unique temp subdirectory per request and recursively delete it after execution.
- Return generic error messages to avoid leaking host paths in compiler output.

issues.title: [BUG] AI insights cached responses consume hourly rate-limit quota

labels.name: gssoc:assigned
labels.description: GSSoC: Issue assigned to a contributor

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The AI insights route consumes a user's hourly rate-limit quota before checking whether a fresh cached insight already exists.

Currently the route:

1. Looks up and increments the in-memory per-user rate limit.
2. Then checks Supabase for a non-expired `ai_insights` cache entry.
3. Returns the cached response if present.

As a result, repeated requests for already-cached insights can exhaust the user's hourly quota even though no expensive AI generation or metrics recomputation is needed.

**Files to look at**

- `src/app/api/ai-insights/route.ts`
  - rate limit map and increment
  - cached `ai_insights` lookup
  - fresh insight generation path

**Why this matters**

Rate limiting should protect expensive operations. Cached reads are cheap and are expected to be safe for dashboard refreshes or repeated visits.

**Potential impact**

- Users can hit `429 Rate limit exceeded` while only reading cached data.
- Dashboard refreshes may block access to otherwise available insights.
- The route behaves inconsistently with the purpose of its cache.

**Suggested fix**

- Check Supabase for a valid cached insight before incrementing the rate-limit counter.
- Only increment the quota when the route needs to generate a fresh insight.
- Keep `Retry-After` behavior for true fresh-generation rate-limit failures.
- Add tests covering:
  - cached response does not consume quota
  - fresh generation consumes quota
  - quota is enforced only after repeated fresh generations

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Valid cached AI insight responses do not increment the hourly quota.
- [ ] Fresh insight generation still respects the existing rate limit.
- [ ] Tests cover cached and uncached behavior.

issues.title: [BUG] Repo analytics chart expects timeline fields the API does not return

labels.name: gssoc:assigned
labels.description: GSSoC: Issue assigned to a contributor

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The repository analytics API and chart disagree on the timeline data shape.

The shared type and API response define timeline points as:

```ts
{ date: string; events: number }
```

But `RepoTimelineChart` renders Recharts series using these keys:

```tsx
dataKey="commits"
dataKey="prs"
dataKey="issues"
```

Because the API does not return `commits`, `prs`, or `issues`, the chart can render blank or misleading series even when the API request succeeds.

**Files to look at**

- `src/lib/repoAnalytics.ts`
- `src/app/api/metrics/repo-analytics/route.ts`
- `src/components/repo-analytics/RepoTimelineChart.tsx`
- `src/components/repo-analytics/RepoAnalyticsSheet.tsx`

**Why this matters**

The analytics drawer is user-facing, and the chart should reflect the actual data returned by the API. A mismatch between API contracts and component expectations makes the visualization unreliable and easy to regress.

**Potential impact**

- Empty or incorrect timeline chart
- Misleading repository analytics
- Weak type safety between API response and UI rendering

**Suggested fix**

Choose one consistent timeline contract:

1. Update the chart to use the existing `events` field and label it accordingly.
2. Or expand the API/type to return separate `commits`, `prs`, and `issues` values if those series are intended.

For the smaller fix, align `RepoTimelineChart` with `events`, update the legend/labels, and add a test or fixture that verifies the chart consumes the same shape exported by `RepoAnalyticsResponse`.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `RepoTimelineChart` uses data keys that exist in `RepoAnalyticsResponse.timeline`.
- [ ] The shared timeline type matches the API response and UI expectations.
- [ ] The chart renders meaningful data when the API returns valid timeline points.
- [ ] A test or typed fixture covers the data contract.

issues.title: [BUG] Repository analytics timeline mislabels GitHub commit activity

labels.name: gssoc:assigned
labels.description: GSSoC: Issue assigned to a contributor

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The repository analytics route uses GitHub's `/stats/commit_activity` response as if the final `days` array always represents the last seven calendar days ending today.

GitHub returns weekly buckets where each item contains a `week` Unix timestamp and a `days` array for that specific Sunday-through-Saturday week. The current implementation takes the last bucket's `days` array and labels it with dates generated from `today`, which can mislabel activity on most weekdays.

The route also only treats `200 OK` as valid. GitHub can return `202 Accepted` while repository statistics are being generated, but the current fallback turns that state into an all-zero timeline.

**Files to look at**

- `src/app/api/metrics/repo-analytics/route.ts`
  - `fetch(.../stats/commit_activity)`
  - timeline construction from `lastWeek.days`
  - fallback timeline generation

**Why this matters**

Repository activity is a core part of the analytics drawer. If dates are mislabeled or a temporary `202 Accepted` response becomes a zero-activity chart, the dashboard can present inaccurate repository health and activity information.

**Potential impact**

- Incorrect timeline labels
- False all-zero activity charts
- Downstream repository health scoring based on inaccurate activity totals

**Suggested fix**

- Use each GitHub stats bucket's `week` timestamp to derive the actual dates for the `days` array.
- Build the visible timeline from those real dates instead of generating labels from `today`.
- Handle `202 Accepted` explicitly, for example by returning a partial/loading status instead of zero activity.
- Add route tests for:
  - successful `200 OK` weekly stats
  - `202 Accepted` stats-building response
  - empty stats response

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Timeline dates are derived from GitHub's `week` timestamp.
- [ ] The route does not mislabel Sunday-through-Saturday activity as the last seven days ending today.
- [ ] `202 Accepted` is handled as a stats-building state, not as zero activity.
- [ ] Tests cover the corrected timeline behavior.

issues.title: [BUG] Friend comparison cache can leak token-scoped GitHub data across users

labels.name: gssoc:assigned
labels.description: GSSoC: Issue assigned to a contributor

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The friend comparison endpoint caches comparison data by target username and date only:

```ts
const cacheKey = `${normalizedUsername}::${today}`;
```

However, the GitHub API requests used to build that payload are made with the currently signed-in user's access token. GitHub search results can vary depending on the viewer's token and repository permissions, especially for private repositories or organization repositories.

This means one signed-in user can populate `comparison_cache` for a target username, and another signed-in user can later receive that cached payload even though their own token may not have access to the same GitHub data.

**Files to look at**

- `src/app/api/metrics/compare/route.ts`
  - cache key creation around the comparison cache lookup
  - GitHub API requests using `session.accessToken`
  - `comparison_cache` upsert at the end of the route

**Why this matters**

Cache entries for token-scoped data should include the viewer identity or be guaranteed to contain public-only data. Otherwise, comparison metrics may leak private or restricted GitHub activity across authenticated users.

**Potential impact**

- Privacy leak across users
- Incorrect comparison metrics
- Cache poisoning where one viewer's authorization context affects another viewer's response

**Suggested fix**

- Include the requesting viewer identity in the comparison cache key, for example:

```ts
const cacheKey = `${session.githubId ?? session.githubLogin}::${normalizedUsername}::${today}`;
```

- Alternatively, only cache data that is fetched through a public-only path and is guaranteed not to vary by viewer permissions.
- Add tests covering two different signed-in sessions querying the same target username and verify the second session does not reuse the first session's cached payload.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Comparison cache keys account for the requesting viewer or use public-only data.
- [ ] Cached comparison payloads cannot be shared across different viewer authorization contexts.
- [ ] Tests cover cache isolation between two authenticated users.

[Bug]: Two visible scroll-to-top buttons rendered simultaneously in App.jsx causing overlapping UI and duplicate DOM nodes
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`App.jsx` mounts **two separate visible scroll-to-top button components** at the same time — `<ScrollToTopButton />` (line 198) and `<BackToTop />` (line 202). Both are lazy-loaded and both render a floating button in the bottom-right corner of the screen. This causes them to visually overlap, creates duplicate DOM nodes, and means click handlers fire on two separate component instances.

**Affected file:** `src/App.jsx` (lines 196–205)

```jsx
{/* App.jsx — both rendered simultaneously */}
<Suspense fallback={null}>
  <ScrollToTopButton />   {/* ← renders BackToTopButton internally */}
</Suspense>
{/* Enhanced back-to-top with progress ring - appears at 400px */}
<Suspense fallback={null}>
  <BackToTop />           {/* ← full implementation with progress ring */}
</Suspense>
```

**Component chain:**
- `ScrollToTopButton` (`src/components/ScrollToTopButton.jsx`) is a thin wrapper that renders `<BackToTopButton threshold={50} />` from `src/components/common/BackToTopButton.jsx`
- `BackToTop` (`src/components/common/BackToTop.jsx`) is the full implementation with scroll progress ring
- Both `BackToTopButton` and `BackToTop` render a fixed-position button in the bottom-right corner

## To Reproduce

1. Open the app in a browser
2. Scroll down past 50px on any page
3. Observe two overlapping scroll-to-top buttons in the bottom-right corner
4. Open DevTools → Elements and search for the button nodes — two separate instances exist in the DOM
5. Both have `position: fixed` with similar `bottom`/`right` values, causing z-index stacking

## Expected behavior

Only one scroll-to-top button should be visible at any time. The `BackToTop` component (with the progress ring) is the more complete implementation and should be the only one rendered. `ScrollToTopButton` and its underlying `BackToTopButton` wrapper are redundant given `BackToTop` already exists.

## Additional context

There is also a third scroll component, `<ScrollToTop />` (line 183), which is invisible (renders `null`) and only handles route-change scroll resets via `useEffect`. This one is correct and should be kept.

**Suggested fix:**
1. Remove `<ScrollToTopButton />` from `App.jsx` (line 198) — it is entirely redundant
2. Remove the lazy import for `ScrollToTopButton` (line 40) from `App.jsx`
3. Consider deleting `src/components/ScrollToTopButton.jsx` as it is no longer used anywhere
4. Keep `<BackToTop />` as the sole scroll-to-top button and `<ScrollToTop />` as the invisible route-reset component

This also reduces the JavaScript bundle by eliminating one unnecessary lazy chunk.

issues.title: [Bug]: feedbackUtils stores all event feedback in a single localStorage key with no size limit, expiry, or per-user isolation
[Bug]: EventFeedbackForm uses simulated API delay instead of real backend — feedback is never persisted
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

`EventFeedbackForm` does not make any real API call when a user submits feedback. Instead it executes a fake `setTimeout` delay and then writes a single `localStorage` key to mark the event as submitted. There is no feedback endpoint in `/api/`. This means every piece of feedback submitted by users is silently discarded — it never reaches a server, event organizers never see it, and it disappears if the user clears browser storage or switches devices.

**Affected files:**
- `src/components/feedback/EventFeedbackForm.jsx` (lines 44–52)
- `src/utils/feedbackUtils.js` (localStorage-only storage, no API integration)

**Root cause in code:**
```js
// src/components/feedback/EventFeedbackForm.jsx
try {
  // Simulate API submit delay   ← mock, not a real request
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 800));

  localStorage.setItem(`feedback-submitted-${eventId}`, "true");
  setSubmitted(true);
  toast.success("Feedback submitted! Thank you for sharing your thoughts.");
```

There is also no feedback endpoint under `/api/` — only `auth/`, `send-email.js`, `leaderboard.js`, `ai-recommendations.js`, and `github-proxy.js` exist.

## To Reproduce

1. Navigate to any event detail page that renders `EventFeedbackForm`
2. Select a star rating and write a comment
3. Click **Submit**
4. Observe the success toast — "Feedback submitted!"
5. Open DevTools → Application → Local Storage
6. Note that only a key like `feedback-submitted-<eventId>` is stored — no feedback content, no server call in the Network tab
7. Clear `localStorage` and reload — the form resets as if feedback was never submitted
8. Event organizers have no way to access the submitted data

## Expected behavior

Submitting the feedback form should:
1. POST the rating, comment, tags, and `userId` to a real `/api/feedback` endpoint
2. Persist the data server-side so event organizers can retrieve aggregate ratings
3. Use the server response to confirm submission rather than a client-side `localStorage` flag
4. Show an error to the user if the server request fails (not swallow it silently)

## Additional context

- `src/utils/feedbackUtils.js` also stores all feedback data in `localStorage` under the key `eventra_feedback` as a secondary mechanism, but this is also purely client-side and does not sync with any backend
- The `FeedbackSystemDemo` page demonstrates the UI but confirms no real API integration exists
- Bypassing the "already submitted" guard is trivial: open DevTools → Application → Local Storage → delete the `feedback-submitted-<eventId>` key → refresh — the form resets

**Suggested fix:**
1. Create `/api/feedback.js` serverless route with POST (save feedback) and GET (retrieve by eventId) handlers
2. Replace the `setTimeout` mock in `EventFeedbackForm` with a `fetch('/api/feedback', { method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({eventId, rating, comment, userId}) })`
3. Include `userId` from the auth context in the payload so the server can enforce one-submission-per-user
4. Remove the client-side "already submitted" localStorage-only guard and rely on the server response

issues.title: [Bug] External Code Execution API URL Hardcoded in LiveCodeRunner — Not Environment-Configurable
issues.body:
## What

The Piston code execution API URL (`https://emkc.org/api/v2/piston/execute`) is hardcoded directly inside `src/components/studyroom/LiveCodeRunner.tsx`. It cannot be overridden via environment variable, making it impossible to swap the endpoint for a self-hosted instance, a staging mock, or a different provider without a code change and a full redeploy.

## Cause

In `src/components/studyroom/LiveCodeRunner.tsx`, the third-party API URL appears as a string literal in the fetch call:

```ts
const res = await fetch("https://emkc.org/api/v2/piston/execute", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ ... }),
});
```

All other external API calls in the codebase reference `API_BASE_URL` from `src/config/api.ts`, making them overridable per environment. This endpoint is the only external API URL that is not centralized.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `src/components/studyroom/LiveCodeRunner.tsx`.
2. Search for `emkc.org` — the URL is a string literal in the component body.
3. Verify `src/config/api.ts` — the Piston endpoint is absent.
4. Check `.env.example` — no `VITE_CODE_EXECUTOR_URL` variable exists.

## Expected Behavior

The code execution endpoint should be sourced from an environment variable (e.g., `VITE_CODE_EXECUTOR_URL`) with the public Piston API as a fallback. This would allow:
- Local development to point to a self-hosted Piston instance.
- CI/testing environments to use a mock.
- Production to switch providers without a code change.

## Actual Behavior

The URL is hardcoded. Any change to the endpoint (provider migration, self-hosting, outage workaround) requires modifying the source file and redeploying.

## Relevant Code References

- `src/components/studyroom/LiveCodeRunner.tsx` — hardcoded `https://emkc.org/api/v2/piston/execute`
- `src/config/api.ts` — existing centralized API configuration (reference for the correct pattern)
- `.env.example` — missing `VITE_CODE_EXECUTOR_URL` entry

## Suggested Fix

**Step 1** — Add to `.env.example`:
```
VITE_CODE_EXECUTOR_URL=https://emkc.org/api/v2/piston/execute
```

**Step 2** — Add to `src/config/api.ts`:
```ts
export const CODE_EXECUTOR_URL =
  import.meta.env.VITE_CODE_EXECUTOR_URL || "https://emkc.org/api/v2/piston/execute";
```

**Step 3** — Update `src/components/studyroom/LiveCodeRunner.tsx`:
```ts
import { CODE_EXECUTOR_URL } from "@/config/api";

// ...
const res = await fetch(CODE_EXECUTOR_URL, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ ... }),
});
```

## Additional Context

The `emkc.org` Piston API is a free, community-maintained service with no SLA. If it experiences downtime or rate-limits the app, there is currently no way to switch endpoints without a source-level change. Centralizing the URL in `config/api.ts` (consistent with how `API_BASE_URL` is handled everywhere else) resolves this and makes the codebase more maintainable. The change touches 3 files and requires no logic changes.

[Bug] "Connect with Peer" and "Start Learning" Buttons on Dashboard Have No onClick Handler
issues.body:
## What

Two prominent call-to-action buttons on the Dashboard are completely non-functional — clicking them produces no response, no navigation, and no feedback whatsoever. The \"+ Start Learning\" hero button and the \"Connect with Peer\" button inside the Recommended Peers section both lack `onClick` handlers.

## Cause

In `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`, neither button is wired to any action:

**\"+ Start Learning\" hero button:**
```tsx
<motion.button
  whileHover={{ scale: 1.05 }}
  whileTap={{ scale: 0.95 }}
  className="rounded-2xl bg-gradient-to-r from-cyan-400 to-blue-500 px-7 py-4 font-semibold text-black shadow-[0_0_35px_rgba(34,211,238,0.35)]"
>
  + Start Learning   {/* ← no onClick */}
</motion.button>
```

**\"Connect with Peer\" button in Recommended Peers loop:**
```tsx
<button className="mt-5 w-full rounded-2xl bg-gradient-to-r from-cyan-400 to-blue-500 px-4 py-3 font-semibold text-slate-900 transition hover:scale-[1.02]">
  Connect with Peer   {/* ← no onClick */}
</button>
```

For comparison, the `DiscoverPeerCard` in `src/pages/Discover.tsx` correctly receives an `onConnect` prop and handles the connection logic — the Dashboard's inline peer card was never wired up similarly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Log in to the application.
2. Navigate to the Dashboard (`/dashboard`).
3. Click the **\"+ Start Learning\"** button in the hero section.
4. Observe that nothing happens.
5. Scroll to the **\"Recommended Peers\"** section.
6. Click the **\"Connect with Peer\"** button on any peer card.
7. Observe that nothing happens.

## Expected Behavior

- **\"+ Start Learning\"** should navigate the user to the Sessions page (`/sessions`) or open a session creation dialog.
- **\"Connect with Peer\"** should initiate a connection request to the selected peer (POST to the `peer_connections` table) and provide feedback (success toast, button state change to \"Pending\").

## Actual Behavior

Both buttons are visually styled and animate on hover/tap (via Framer Motion), creating the impression they are interactive — but clicking either does nothing. Users are left confused.

## Relevant Code References

- `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` — hero section `<motion.button>` (\"+ Start Learning\")
- `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` — Recommended Peers map loop `<button>` (\"Connect with Peer\")
- `src/pages/Discover.tsx` — `DiscoverPeerCard` with working `onConnect` prop (reference implementation)

## Suggested Fix

**\"+ Start Learning\":**
```tsx
import { useNavigate } from "react-router-dom";
// ...
const navigate = useNavigate();
// ...
<motion.button
  onClick={() => navigate('/sessions')}
  ...
>
  + Start Learning
</motion.button>
```

**\"Connect with Peer\":**
```tsx
const handleConnect = async (peerId: string) => {
  const { error } = await supabase
    .from("peer_connections")
    .insert({ requester_id: user.id, receiver_id: peerId, status: "pending" });
  if (!error) toast({ title: "Request sent!", description: "Your connection request has been sent." });
};
// ...
<button onClick={() => handleConnect(p.id)} ...>
  Connect with Peer
</button>
```

## Additional Context

These are the two highest-visibility action buttons on the Dashboard. Dead CTAs are a significant UX regression — users who click them and get no response may assume the app is broken. The Discover page already has working peer connection logic that can be reused directly.

issues.title: [Bug] Dashboard Activity Feed Displays Hardcoded Fake Data Instead of Real User Activity
issues.body:
## What The \"Activity Feed\" panel on the Dashboard renders 4 static, hardcoded strings that never change regardless of who is logged in or what actions they have performed. Every user sees the same fabricated activity with a static \"2 mins ago\" timestamp. ## Cause In `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`, the Activity Feed section maps over a hardcoded array instead of fetching real data from the database: ```tsx {[ "Joined AI Session", "Completed React Quiz", "New Peer Request", "Earned 50 XP", ].map((activity, i) => (

{activity}

2 mins ago {/* static forever */}
✔
 ))} ``` This appears to be a placeholder left in from development that was never wired up to real data. ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Log in to the application. 2. Navigate to the Dashboard (`/dashboard`). 3. Observe the \"Activity Feed\" section on the right panel. 4. Log out and log in as a different user. 5. Observe that both users see the exact same 4 activity entries. ## Expected Behavior The Activity Feed should display the authenticated user's real recent activity — such as sessions joined, messages sent, XP awarded, or peer connection requests — pulled from the database and timestamped accurately. ## Actual Behavior All users see the same 4 hardcoded strings: \"Joined AI Session\", \"Completed React Quiz\", \"New Peer Request\", \"Earned 50 XP\", each with a static \"2 mins ago\" label that never updates. ## Relevant Code References - `src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` — Activity Feed section (lines ~280–310) ## Suggested Fix Replace the hardcoded array with a real Supabase query. For example, query the last 5 entries from `session_participants`, the XP award log, or a dedicated `activity_log` table filtered by the authenticated user's ID: ```tsx // Example approach const [recentActivity, setRecentActivity] = useState([]); useEffect(() => { if (!user) return; const fetchActivity = async () => { const { data } = await supabase .from("activity_log") // or session_participants, etc. .select("*") .eq("user_id", user.id) .order("created_at", { ascending: false }) .limit(5); if (data) setRecentActivity(data); }; fetchActivity(); }, [user]); ``` If a dedicated activity log table does not yet exist, this issue is also an opportunity to design one that aggregates events from sessions, XP awards, and peer connections. ## Additional Context This is one of the most visible sections on the Dashboard — every logged-in user sees it immediately. Displaying fabricated data breaks trust and gives users a false picture of their history. The fix scope is well-contained to the Dashboard component and does not require changes to routing, auth, or shared components.

## Feature Name

`stylelint` — CSS linter setup for automated quality enforcement

---

## Description

The project currently has no CSS linter. `package.json` only contains:

```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "echo \"No tests yet\" && exit 0"
}
```

Several already-filed issues (invalid gradient syntax, invalid `font-weight` unit, duplicate variable declarations, wrong animation names) are bugs that a standard CSS linter would have caught **before they were merged**. Without a linter:

- Contributors submit broken CSS that passes review silently
- Maintainers must manually spot CSS syntax errors during code review
- The CI submission validator (`submission-validator.yml`) cannot detect CSS-level mistakes

---

## Why is this useful for EaseMotion CSS?

The framework is a CSS library — CSS correctness is the core deliverable. A linter is the lowest-effort, highest-impact quality gate available. `stylelint` with `stylelint-config-standard` enforces W3C-compliant CSS, catches typos, duplicate properties, invalid values, and convention violations automatically on every PR.

---

## HTML Snippet

N/A — this is a tooling change, not a UI component.

---

## CSS Snippet

No CSS changes required. The linter validates existing files.

**Files to add/modify:**

`package.json`:
```json
{
  "devDependencies": {
    "stylelint": "^16.0.0",
    "stylelint-config-standard": "^36.0.0"
  },
  "scripts": {
    "lint": "stylelint \"**/*.css\" --ignore-path .gitignore",
    "lint:fix": "stylelint \"**/*.css\" --fix --ignore-path .gitignore",
    "test": "npm run lint"
  }
}
```

`.stylelintrc.json` (new file at repo root):

{
  "extends": ["stylelint-config-standard"],

    "custom-property-pattern": "^ease-",

`.github/workflows/lint.yml` (new CI job):

name: Lint CSS
on: [pull_request]

issues.body:
## Feature Name `ease-min-h-0` / `ease-min-w-0` — Flex and grid overflow fix utilities --- ## Description There is a well-known CSS behaviour: flex and grid items have an implicit `min-height: auto` and `min-width: auto`. This means a flex child that contains scrollable content (e.g., a `overflow-y: auto` inner div, a `
` block, or a long text truncation) **will not scroll or truncate** — it will instead expand the flex container beyond its bounds.

The fix is `min-height: 0` (or `min-width: 0` for the horizontal axis) on the flex/grid child. EaseMotion CSS has no utility for this, so developers hit a confusing layout bug with no in-framework escape hatch.

---

## Why is this useful for EaseMotion CSS?

This is one of the most frequently searched CSS problems for flexbox users. Any developer building a sidebar layout, a scrollable panel, a code block in a flex row, or a truncated text card will encounter this. Since EaseMotion CSS promotes utility-first composition via `.ease-flex` and `.ease-grid`, the framework should include the fix for the most common trap those classes create.

---

## HTML Snippet

```html



  
Header


  
  

    
Very long code content that should scroll...

  







  
  

    
Very long username that should truncate but won't without min-w-0

  



```

---

## CSS Snippet

```css
/* Add to core/utilities.css */

/* Flex/grid overflow fix — prevents implicit min-size from blocking scroll/truncate */
.ease-min-h-0 { min-height: 0; }
.ease-min-w-0 { min-width:  0; }
```

---

## Visual Reference (optional)

A well-known reference: [https://css-tricks.com/flexbox-truncated-text/](https://css-tricks.com/flexbox-truncated-text/) — the `.ease-truncate` class in EaseMotion CSS already exists, but it silently fails inside flex rows without `min-width: 0` on the parent.

---

## Checklist

- [x] This feature does not duplicate an existing EaseMotion CSS class
- [x] I understand my naming will be standardized by the maintainer
- [x] I will submit code inside `submissions/examples/` only — not in `core/` or `components/`

issues.body:
## Feature Name `--ease-space-7` — Missing spacing token between `1.5rem` and `2rem` --- ## Description The EaseMotion CSS spacing scale in `core/variables.css` currently reads: ```css --ease-space-6: 1.5rem; /* 24px */ /* space-7 is missing */ --ease-space-8: 2rem; /* 32px */ ``` There is an **8px gap** between `space-6` and `space-8` with no token to fill it. Every other adjacent pair in the scale is separated by 4px (`space-1`→`space-2`→`space-3`→`space-4`) or 8px (`space-4`→`space-5`→`space-6`). The jump from `space-6` to `space-8` skips `1.75rem` (28px), which is a commonly needed value for section spacing and component padding. Without this token, developers must hardcode `1.75rem` — breaking the principle that all spacing values should come from the design token system. --- ## Why is this useful for EaseMotion CSS? The framework explicitly positions itself as token-first and human-readable. A gap in the spacing scale forces magic number usage, which undermines that promise. `--ease-space-7` would: - Complete the natural numeric sequence (`space-1` through `space-8` without gaps) - Enable `.ease-gap-7`, `.ease-padding-7`, `.ease-margin-7` utility classes - Allow components and submissions to use `var(--ease-space-7)` instead of `1.75rem` --- ## HTML Snippet ```html

Section Title

Card 1
Card 2
Card 3
``` --- ## CSS Snippet ```css /* core/variables.css — add after --ease-space-6 */ --ease-space-7: 1.75rem; /* 28px */ /* core/utilities.css — add alongside other gap/padding/margin utilities */ .ease-gap-7 { gap: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-padding-7 { padding: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-margin-7 { margin: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-pt-7 { padding-top: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-pb-7 { padding-bottom: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-pl-7 { padding-left: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-pr-7 { padding-right: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-mt-7 { margin-top: var(--ease-space-7); } .ease-mb-7 { margin-bottom: var(--ease-space-7); } ``` --- ## Visual Reference (optional) The change is purely additive — one new token and its corresponding utility classes. No existing classes are modified. --- ## Checklist - [x] This feature does not duplicate an existing EaseMotion CSS class - [x] I understand my naming will be standardized by the maintainer - [x] I will submit code inside `submissions/examples/` only — not in `core/` or `components/`

## 🐛 What's broken? `.ease-sticky` hardcodes `top: 0`, which is **wrong for the most common real-world use case** — a page that already has a fixed navbar. Any sticky element on such a page will be obscured behind the navbar with no way to change the offset using the utility class system. --- ## 📋 Steps to Reproduce 1. Link EaseMotion CSS 2. Build a page with a fixed `64px` navbar and a sticky sidebar: ```html
Navbar
Sidebar
``` 3. Scroll the page — the sidebar sticks at `top: 0`, hidden under the navbar --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior `.ease-sticky` should either: - Default to `top: 0` but expose a CSS variable so the offset can be overridden per-element without writing a new class, or - Ship companion utilities for common offsets (`.ease-sticky-top-16`, etc.) --- ## ❌ Actual Behavior `core/utilities.css` line 161: ```css .ease-sticky { position: sticky; top: 0; } ``` `top: 0` is hardcoded. There is no CSS variable, no modifier class, and no documented override path. The only way to use a different offset is to write custom CSS that overrides the utility class, which defeats the purpose. --- ## 🔗 Reproduction ```html
Fixed Navbar (64px tall)
Sidebar
Long content
``` --- ## 🌍 Environment | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | EaseMotion CSS version | `1.0.0` | | Browser | All browsers | | OS | All platforms | --- ## 💡 Suggested Fix Introduce a CSS custom property with a `0` default so the offset is overridable inline or via a parent rule: ```css /* core/variables.css */ :root { --ease-sticky-top: 0; } /* core/utilities.css */ .ease-sticky { position: sticky; top: var(--ease-sticky-top); } ``` Usage then becomes: ```html
...
...
``` No extra classes needed — the token override pattern is already how EaseMotion CSS works throughout the rest of the framework.

## Feature Name `--ease-glow-warning` — Warning glow design token --- ## Description `core/variables.css` defines a consistent set of glow tokens for semantic colors: ```css --ease-glow-primary: 0 0 16px rgba(108, 99, 255, 0.45); --ease-glow-success: 0 0 16px rgba(34, 197, 94, 0.45); --ease-glow-danger: 0 0 16px rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.45); /* --ease-glow-warning ← missing */ ``` The `warning` semantic color (`--ease-color-warning: #f59e0b`) is fully defined with light, base, and dark variants — but has **no corresponding glow token**. This means developers cannot compose a consistent warning glow effect via the design system and are forced to hardcode `box-shadow` values, breaking the token-first philosophy of the framework. --- ## Why is this useful for EaseMotion CSS? The framework's entire value proposition is composability via human-readable tokens. Having three out of four semantic glow tokens is an incomplete set. Any component that needs a warning state glow (e.g., a warning card, an alert button, a form field with a caution state) must bypass the token system. Adding `--ease-glow-warning` closes this gap and makes the design system internally consistent. --- ## HTML Snippet ```html

This action requires your attention.

``` --- ## CSS Snippet ```css /* Add to core/variables.css alongside the existing glow tokens */ :root { --ease-glow-warning: 0 0 16px rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.45); } ``` The RGBA value is derived directly from `--ease-color-warning: #f59e0b` (`rgb(245, 158, 11)`), keeping it consistent with how all other glow tokens are constructed. --- ## Visual Reference (optional) The pattern mirrors the existing three tokens exactly — same spread, same opacity, just the warning amber color. --- ## Checklist - [x] This feature does not duplicate an existing EaseMotion CSS class - [x] I understand my naming will be standardized by the maintainer - [x] I will submit code inside `submissions/examples/` only — not in `core/` or `components/`

## 🐛 What's broken? `core/base.css` applies `scroll-behavior: smooth` unconditionally to the `` element. This means smooth scrolling is **always active**, even for users who have indicated via their OS accessibility settings that they prefer reduced motion. For users with vestibular disorders, unexpected smooth scrolling can cause nausea and disorientation. --- ## 📋 Steps to Reproduce 1. On macOS: System Settings → Accessibility → Display → enable "Reduce Motion" 2. On Windows: Settings → Ease of Access → Display → enable "Show animations in Windows" (off) 3. Link EaseMotion CSS on any page with anchor links or `scroll-into-view` calls 4. Click an anchor link — the page still scrolls smoothly instead of jumping instantly --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior When a user has `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` set, anchor navigation and programmatic scrolling should jump instantly, not animate. WCAG Success Criterion 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) and general best practice for vestibular accessibility require this. --- ## ❌ Actual Behavior `core/base.css` line 21: ```css html { font-size: 16px; scroll-behavior: smooth; /* ← no reduced-motion guard */ -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; } ``` `scroll-behavior: smooth` is applied to all users regardless of their accessibility preference. --- ## 🔗 Reproduction ```html Jump to section
Section content
``` With "Reduce Motion" enabled in OS settings, clicking the anchor still produces a smooth scroll instead of an instant jump. --- ## 🌍 Environment | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | EaseMotion CSS version | `1.0.0` | | Browser | All browsers that support `prefers-reduced-motion` | | OS | macOS (Reduce Motion), Windows (Reduce Animations), Linux (GNOME accessibility) | --- ## 💡 Suggested Fix Reverse the default and opt-in to smooth scrolling only when the user has not requested reduced motion: ```css /* core/base.css */ /* Default: instant scroll (safe for all users) */ html { font-size: 16px; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; } /* Opt-in smooth scroll only when the user has no motion preference */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { html { scroll-behavior: smooth; } } ``` This is the pattern recommended by MDN, WebAIM, and the W3C.

issues.body:
## 🐛 What's broken? `.ease-border-primary` only sets `border-color` and has **no effect** when used on its own. A developer who writes `
` will see no border at all — the class silently does nothing unless `.ease-border` or `.ease-border-2` is also present. --- ## 📋 Steps to Reproduce 1. Link EaseMotion CSS 2. Add this HTML: ```html
I should have a primary-colored border
``` 3. Inspect the element — no border is visible --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior `
` should render a visible border in the primary color, consistent with how every other `.ease-border-*` modifier works in the framework. --- ## ❌ Actual Behavior `core/utilities.css` line 238 reads: ```css .ease-border-primary { border-color: var(--ease-color-primary); } ``` `border-color` alone has no visual effect — CSS requires `border-style` (at minimum) to be set before `border-color` is rendered. The element's computed `border-style` defaults to `none`, so the color is applied to an invisible border. By contrast, `.ease-border` correctly uses the full shorthand: ```css .ease-border { border: 1px solid var(--ease-color-neutral-200); } ``` This inconsistency makes `.ease-border-primary` behave differently from every other border utility in the file. --- ## 🔗 Reproduction ```html
No border here (bug)
Border visible only with workaround
``` --- ## 🌍 Environment | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | EaseMotion CSS version | `1.0.0` | | Browser | All browsers | | OS | All platforms | --- ## 💡 Suggested Fix Change the declaration in `core/utilities.css` to include `border-style` and `border-width`: ```css /* Before */ .ease-border-primary { border-color: var(--ease-color-primary); } /* After */ .ease-border-primary { border: 1px solid var(--ease-color-primary); } ``` This makes it consistent with `.ease-border` and `.ease-border-2`, and eliminates the hidden dependency on a companion class.

issues.title: [BUG] Google Fonts loaded via render-blocking CSS @import in base.css

labels.name: accepted
labels.description: Contribution approved for integration into EaseMotion CSS

issues.body:
## 🐛 What's broken? `core/base.css` loads Google Fonts using a CSS `@import` rule at the top of the file. CSS `@import` is **synchronously render-blocking** — the browser must fully download and parse the remote stylesheet before it can continue rendering the page. This causes a measurable delay in First Contentful Paint (FCP) on every page that uses the framework. --- ## 📋 Steps to Reproduce 1. Link EaseMotion CSS via CDN or local file 2. Open Chrome DevTools → Performance tab → record a page load 3. Observe the network waterfall — the Google Fonts stylesheet blocks rendering until it resolves --- ## ✅ Expected Behavior Fonts should be loaded in a non-blocking manner. The framework should either: - Remove the `@import` from `base.css` and document the recommended `` approach in the README, or - At minimum, document that this `@import` has a performance cost and show the faster alternative --- ## ❌ Actual Behavior `core/base.css` line 6 contains: ```css @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@300;400;500;600;700&display=swap'); ``` This is placed inside a CSS file, which means the browser **cannot** discover and start downloading the font until it has already downloaded and begun parsing `base.css` itself. Google Lighthouse flags CSS `@import` for third-party resources as a critical performance issue. --- ## 🔗 Reproduction ```html

Hello

``` Run Lighthouse on this page — it will flag the Google Fonts `@import` under "Eliminate render-blocking resources". --- ## 🌍 Environment | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | EaseMotion CSS version | `1.0.0` | | Browser | All browsers (this is a CSS loading mechanism issue) | | OS | All platforms | --- ## 💡 Suggested Fix Remove the `@import` from `core/base.css` and update `docs/index.html` and all example files to use the recommended `` approach: ```html ``` Since `core/variables.css` already declares `system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif` as fallbacks in `--ease-font-sans`, the framework degrades gracefully without the `@import`. The README should document the recommended snippet for users who want Inter.

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
In \`client/src/components/RiskTrendChart.tsx\`, each data point's X-axis label is formatted using only the calendar date (month + day):

\`\`\`ts
// RiskTrendChart.tsx lines 47–56
date: isValid(new Date(a.createdAt))
  ? format(new Date(a.createdAt), "MMM d")  // e.g., "Jun 6"
  : "?",
\`\`\`

When a provider creates more than one assessment in a single calendar day (e.g., during a bulk import, a clinic session, or back-to-back assessments), every one of those assessments gets the exact same label (e.g., \`"Jun 6"\`). Recharts renders them at overlapping X positions, resulting in:

- Multiple data points stacked on top of each other — only the last one is visually accessible.
- Hovering the chart shows a tooltip for one point only, hiding the others.
- The trend line draws a horizontal segment with zero width, making it appear as if there is no variation between those assessments.
- Providers using the bulk import feature (which can create dozens of same-day records) see a chart that appears to have far fewer data points than expected.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create two or more assessments for the same patient within the same calendar day.
2. Navigate to Assessment History and find the patient's risk trend chart.
3. Observe: all same-day assessments share one label on the X-axis, and only one data point is visually distinct.

**Expected behavior**
Same-day assessments should be distinguishable on the chart. Options:
1. Include the time in the label: \`format(new Date(a.createdAt), "MMM d, HH:mm")\` (e.g., \`"Jun 6, 14:32"\`).
2. Use the raw ISO timestamp as the \`dataKey\` and apply a date-only format only to the axis tick labels via a \`tickFormatter\` prop — this preserves correct spacing while keeping labels readable.

**Relevant code**
- \`client/src/components/RiskTrendChart.tsx:47–56\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**
This issue is especially visible after using the Bulk Import feature, which typically processes all records in the same second and thus produces dozens of assessments with identical \`createdAt\` timestamps. A provider monitoring a high-risk patient could miss that two same-day assessments showed meaningfully different risk scores.

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The \`Assessment\` interface defined locally in \`client/src/components/RiskTrendChart.tsx\` types every clinical measurement field as \`any\`:

\`\`\`ts
// RiskTrendChart.tsx lines 14–22
interface Assessment {
  id: number;
  createdAt: any;           // should be string | Date
  riskScore: any;           // should be number
  bmi: any;                 // should be number
  hba1cLevel: any;          // should be number
  bloodGlucoseLevel: any;   // should be number
  riskCategory: string;
}
\`\`\`

TypeScript cannot catch any of the following bugs when these fields are \`any\`:
- A string (e.g. \`"28.5"\`) passed where a number is expected produces \`NaN\` after \`Number.toFixed()\`, which Recharts renders as a blank data point.
- A \`null\` or \`undefined\` value produces \`NaN\` chart values silently instead of being caught at compile time.
- Renaming a field in \`shared/schema.ts\` (e.g. \`hba1cLevel\` → \`hba1c\`) would cause the chart to silently display nothing — TypeScript would not flag the mismatch because the local interface accepts \`any\`.

The shared schema in \`shared/schema.ts\` already defines the correct types for all these fields via the Drizzle \`Assessment\` type.

**To Reproduce**
1. Run \`npm run check\` (TypeScript type check).
2. Notice no errors are raised even if you pass a string to \`riskScore\` in the component.

**Expected behavior**
The local \`Assessment\` interface should use proper types, or better, reuse the canonical \`Assessment\` type from \`@shared/schema\`:

\`\`\`ts
import type { Assessment } from "@shared/schema";

interface Props {
  assessments: Pick<Assessment, "id" | "createdAt" | "riskScore" | "bmi" | "hba1cLevel" | "bloodGlucoseLevel" | "riskCategory">[];
}
\`\`\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**
This is a type safety cleanup. The \`Assessment\` type from \`@shared/schema\` is already imported in other components (e.g., \`AssessmentResult.tsx\`) — \`RiskTrendChart.tsx\` should follow the same pattern. Fixing this will surface any latent type mismatches immediately in the TypeScript compiler.

issues.title: [BUG] RiskTrendChart metric toggle buttons missing aria-pressed state and type="button" attribute

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The metric toggle buttons in \`client/src/components/RiskTrendChart.tsx\` (Risk Score, BMI, HbA1c, Blood Glucose) are missing two important HTML/ARIA attributes:

\`\`\`tsx
// RiskTrendChart.tsx lines 81–93
<button
  key={key}
  onClick={() => toggleMetric(key)}
  className={...}
  style={...}
  // Missing: type="button"
  // Missing: aria-pressed={activeMetrics[key]}
  // Missing: aria-label describing the metric being toggled
>
  <span className="w-2 h-2 rounded-full" style={{ backgroundColor: color }} />
  {label}
</button>
\`\`\`

**Issue 1 — Missing \`type="button"\`**
HTML \`<button>\` elements default to \`type="submit"\`. If \`RiskTrendChart\` is ever rendered inside or adjacent to a \`<form>\` element, clicking a metric toggle will submit the form instead of (or in addition to) toggling the metric. This is an existing footgun that becomes a real bug as the codebase evolves.

**Issue 2 — Missing \`aria-pressed\`**
Toggle buttons that switch between on/off states must expose their current state via \`aria-pressed\` per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value). Without it, screen readers announce the button as a plain button with no state. A visually impaired provider cannot tell which metrics are currently displayed on the chart.

**To Reproduce (accessibility)**
1. Open the Assessment History page with a patient that has multiple assessments.
2. Navigate to the risk trend chart using a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA, JAWS).
3. Tab to the metric toggle buttons.
4. Observe: the reader announces "Risk Score (%)" with no indication of whether the metric is currently active or inactive.

**Expected behavior**
Each metric toggle button should have:
- \`type="button"\` to prevent accidental form submission.
- \`aria-pressed={activeMetrics[key]}\` to communicate toggle state to assistive technology.

\`\`\`tsx
<button
  key={key}
  type="button"
  aria-pressed={activeMetrics[key]}
  onClick={() => toggleMetric(key)}
  ...
>
\`\`\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any (accessibility issue affects all browsers)

**Additional context**
Healthcare applications frequently must comply with accessibility standards (Section 508, WCAG 2.1 AA). This fix requires adding two attributes to each button — no logic changes needed.

[BUG] ImportData.tsx shows "Max 5MB" label but performs no client-side file size validation

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Bulk Import page displays "Max file size: 5MB" in the upload area, but the \`processFile\` function does **not check \`file.size\`** before handing the file to PapaParse:

\`\`\`ts
// client/src/pages/ImportData.tsx
const processFile = (file: File) => {
  if (file.type !== "text/csv" && !file.name.endsWith('.csv')) {
    // only type check — no size check
    return;
  }
  Papa.parse(file, { ... });  // parses the entire file in the browser thread
\`\`\`

PapaParse processes the file synchronously in the browser's main thread. Uploading a file significantly larger than 5MB (e.g., 50MB or 200MB) will:
1. Block the browser UI thread while PapaParse reads the entire file into memory.
2. Potentially freeze or crash the tab before the HTTP POST is even sent.
3. The server's multer limit (5MB, configured in \`server/routes/upload.routes.ts:13\`) only triggers after the full file is already parsed client-side — too late to prevent the client-side freeze.

The "Max 5MB" label is therefore misleading — it is not enforced.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a CSV file larger than 5MB (e.g., 20MB).
2. Navigate to the Bulk Import page.
3. Drop or select the oversized file.
4. Observe: PapaParse begins parsing immediately, the tab may become unresponsive, and no size validation error is shown.

**Expected behavior**
Before calling \`Papa.parse\`, \`processFile\` should check \`file.size\` and show a toast error if it exceeds 5MB:

\`\`\`ts
const MAX_FILE_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024; // 5MB
if (file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE) {
  toast({ title: "File too large", description: "Please upload a CSV under 5MB.", variant: "destructive" });
  return;
}
\`\`\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Chrome, Firefox, Safari

**Additional context**
This is a simple one-line guard that keeps the advertised limit consistent with actual behaviour and prevents accidental tab crashes on large exports from EHR systems.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
In \`client/src/pages/ImportData.tsx\`, when a CSV row has no \`patientName\` or \`name\` column (or the values are empty), the import silently substitutes the string literal \`"Unknown Patient"\`:

\`\`\`ts
// ImportData.tsx line 42
patientName: row.patientName || row.name || "Unknown Patient",
\`\`\`

This means:
- A CSV with 500 rows lacking patient names creates 500 real database records all named \`"Unknown Patient"\`.
- These records appear in the assessment history, search results, and analytics (total patient count, risk distribution, critical alerts feed) — corrupting population health metrics.
- The provider receives a success toast with no indication that patient names were fabricated.
- There is no way to distinguish these synthetic records from real assessments after the fact.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create a CSV with valid clinical columns but omit the \`patientName\` and \`name\` columns (or leave them blank).
2. Navigate to the Bulk Import page and upload the CSV.
3. Observe: the import succeeds and the results table shows all records named "Unknown Patient".
4. Check the Assessment History — "Unknown Patient" records now appear permanently.

**Expected behavior**
Rows with a missing or empty patient name should be rejected with a per-row validation error. The import response should return a partial-success report listing which rows were skipped and why, rather than silently substituting a placeholder.

**Relevant code**
- \`client/src/pages/ImportData.tsx:42\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**
In a HIPAA-adjacent clinical tool, fabricating patient identifiers is a data integrity violation. The fix should validate that \`patientName\` is a non-empty string on the client before submitting rows, and the bulk API endpoint should also enforce this at the schema level (the Zod schema in \`shared/schema.ts\` already marks \`patientName\` as required). Skipped rows should be surfaced to the user in the import results table.

issues.title: [BUG] Preview endpoint silently uses fallback rule-based model with no disclosure to the provider
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
When the Python ML model is unavailable (timeout, missing venv, subprocess error), \`MLService.runAssessmentInference\` falls back to a simple 5-rule heuristic (\`calculateClinicalFallback\`). In the **full assessment creation flow**, this is correctly disclosed via a \`disclaimer\` field appended to the prediction. However, in the **preview endpoint** (\`POST /api/assessments/preview\`), the \`isFallback\` return value is silently discarded:

\`\`\`ts
// server/routes/assessments.routes.ts — preview handler
const { prediction } = await MLService.runAssessmentInference(input);
// isFallback is never read here — no disclosure in the response
return res.json({
  riskScore: prediction.riskScore,
  riskCategory: prediction.riskCategory,
  factors: prediction.factors ?? [],
  confidenceInterval: prediction.confidenceInterval ?? null,
  modelConfidence: prediction.modelConfidence ?? null,
});
\`\`\`

A provider watching the live preview panel while filling out the form sees a risk score that appears to be ML-generated, but may be produced by a simple point-scoring heuristic with no indication of degraded accuracy.

**To Reproduce**
1. Ensure the Python venv is not active or \`analyze.py\` is unreachable so the ML model fails.
2. Open the Dashboard and begin filling in patient vitals.
3. Observe the preview panel update in real time with a risk score.
4. Note: there is no warning, badge, or disclaimer indicating the result is from a fallback model.

**Expected behavior**
The preview response should include an \`isFallback\` flag (or equivalent) when the rule-based fallback is used. The client should display a visible warning such as:
> ⚠️ Live preview is using a rule-based estimate — ML model unavailable.

**Relevant code**
- \`server/routes/assessments.routes.ts\` — preview route (~line 49–68)
- \`server/services/mlService.ts\` — \`runAssessmentInference\` returns \`{ prediction, isFallback }\`
- \`shared/routes.ts\` — preview response schema does not include \`isFallback\`

**Screenshots**
N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**
The full assessment flow already handles this correctly with a disclaimer string. The fix is to propagate the same disclosure to the preview: add \`isFallback: boolean\` to the preview response schema and render a warning toast or badge on the client when it is \`true\`. This is a **clinical safety** concern — providers should always know the provenance and reliability of a risk estimate they are viewing.

The website package should run real quality checks.

### Description

`server/package.json` defines duplicate `test` and `test:watch` script keys. In JSON, later keys overwrite earlier keys, so only the last `test` and `test:watch` entries are actually used by npm.

Affected file:
- `server/package.json`, lines 9-13

Current impact:
- Several backend test suites listed in the earlier `test` scripts are silently excluded.
- Contributors and CI can get a passing backend test run while important tests are never executed.
- The script section is harder to maintain because it is not obvious which command npm will keep.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `server/package.json`.
2. Inspect the `scripts` object.
3. Notice that `test` is declared multiple times and `test:watch` is declared multiple times.
4. Run `npm run test` from `server/`.
5. Observe that npm only executes the final `test` command, not all listed test suites.

### Expected Behavior

`server/package.json` should define each npm script key only once. The backend test command should run the intended test coverage explicitly, for example through one consolidated `test` script or separate scripts such as `test:unit`, `test:integration`, and `test:all`.

Suggested fix:
- Remove duplicate script keys.
- Consolidate backend tests into one reliable command.
- Add separate named scripts if different test subsets are needed.
- Verify with `npm run test` from the `server/` directory.

### Screenshots

Not applicable.

- OS: All
- Browser: Not applicable
- Version: Current `main` branch

issues.title: [BUG] Auth forms missing autoComplete attributes — password managers auto-fill incorrectly and WCAG 1.3.5 violated
issues.body:
## Description

The Login, Register, and ResetPassword forms do not set `autoComplete` (HTML `autocomplete`) attributes on their email and password fields. The shared `Input` component forwards `...rest` props to the underlying `<input>`, so it fully supports `autoComplete` — but the page-level usage omits it entirely.

**Affected files and fields:**

| File | Field | Missing value |
|------|-------|---------------|
| `client/src/modules/auth/Login.jsx:109` | email input | `autoComplete="email"` |
| `client/src/modules/auth/Login.jsx:120` | password input | `autoComplete="current-password"` |
| `client/src/modules/auth/Register.jsx:205` | password input | `autoComplete="new-password"` |
| `client/src/modules/auth/Register.jsx:250` | confirm password input | `autoComplete="new-password"` |
| `client/src/modules/auth/ResetPassword.jsx:210` | new password input | `autoComplete="new-password"` |
| `client/src/modules/auth/ResetPassword.jsx:222` | confirm password input | `autoComplete="new-password"` |

Without these attributes:
- Password managers cannot distinguish between a **login** field and a **new password** field, causing wrong auto-fill (e.g. filling the register form with the saved current password instead of prompting to save a new one).
- Browsers may display "not secure" or "autocomplete disabled" warnings.
- Screen readers and assistive technologies cannot announce the purpose of each field to users (violates **WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.3.5 — Identify Input Purpose**).

## Reproduction Steps

1. Open the Register page (`/register`).
2. Use a password manager (1Password, Bitwarden, browser built-in, etc.) or inspect the `<input>` elements.
3. The password field has no `autocomplete` attribute — the password manager cannot offer to save or suggest a new strong password.
4. Repeat on the Login page — the password field has no `autocomplete="current-password"`, so password managers may not auto-fill.

## Expected Behavior

- Login email field: `autocomplete="email"`
- Login password field: `autocomplete="current-password"`
- Register / ResetPassword password fields: `autocomplete="new-password"`

Password managers should auto-fill the login form and offer to save/generate a new password on the register and reset forms.

## Screenshots / Logs

Inspect element on any auth form input — `autocomplete` attribute is absent.

## Environment Details

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any
- Affected files: `client/src/modules/auth/Login.jsx`, `Register.jsx`, `ResetPassword.jsx`

## Additional Context

**Fix** — add `autoComplete` to each `<Input>` call:

```jsx
// Login.jsx
<Input id="email"    type="email"    autoComplete="email"            ... />
<Input id="password" type="password" autoComplete="current-password" ... />

// Register.jsx
<Input id="password"        type="password" autoComplete="new-password" ... />
<Input id="confirmPassword" type="password" autoComplete="new-password" ... />

// ResetPassword.jsx
<Input type="password" autoComplete="new-password" ... />  // both fields
```

No component changes are needed — `Input` already passes through `...rest` to the underlying `<input>`.

Reference: [WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/identify-input-purpose.html)
