There is a typo in `backend/constants/permissions.js` at line 39 where the `USER_DELETE` permission constant uses a **space** instead of a **colon**, inconsistent with every other permission in the file:

```js
// backend/constants/permissions.js

// All other permissions follow the correct pattern:
USER_READ:   'user:read',
USER_UPDATE: 'user:update',

// Line 39 — TYPO: space instead of colon
USER_DELETE: 'user delete',  // ← Should be 'user:delete'
```

This `USER_DELETE` constant is then used in RBAC checks at line 147:

```js
PERMISSIONS.USER_DELETE  // resolves to 'user delete' (broken string)
```

Since roles are stored and compared using the colon-separated format (`'user:delete'`), this broken string **never matches** any stored permission, meaning:

- Admin users trying to delete other users may be silently denied (if roles check for `'user:delete'`)
- Or the RBAC guard passes unexpectedly depending on the deny/allow default — either way the behaviour is incorrect

## Environment / Wallet

- Backend: Node.js / Express
- File: `backend/constants/permissions.js`, line 39
- Also used at: `backend/constants/permissions.js`, line 147

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Log in as an admin user
2. Attempt to delete a user via the admin panel or API (`DELETE /api/users/:id`)
3. Observe: request is rejected or behaves unexpectedly due to permission mismatch

## Relevant Logs/Error Messages

No explicit error — the failure is silent because the string comparison simply never matches.

## Suggested Fix

```js
// Line 39 — fix the typo
USER_DELETE: 'user:delete',
```

Also verify that the role definition that grants this permission also uses `'user:delete'` so both sides match.

## Impact

- Admins cannot delete users (RBAC silently broken for this specific action)
- Or the permission check is bypassed entirely — both outcomes are incorrect
- Difficult to catch in manual testing because there is no error, just wrong behaviour

## Additional Context

- Difficulty: Beginner-friendly (one character change)
- Area: Backend / RBAC / Authorization
- Estimated fix time: ~10 minutes

issues.title: [Security] Open Redirect Vulnerability in Login Page via Unvalidated 'from' Query Parameter

labels.name: level:advanced
labels.description: 55 pts for contributors 30 pts for mentors

issues.body:
## Bug Description

The login page reads the `from` query parameter directly from the URL and passes it to `router.replace()` without any validation. This allows an attacker to craft a malicious link like:

```
https://cropchain.app/login?from=https://evil.com
```

After a legitimate login, the user is silently redirected to the attacker-controlled domain. This is a classic **Open Redirect** vulnerability commonly used in phishing campaigns — victims see a trustworthy login URL but end up on a malicious site post-authentication.

**Affected file:** `frontend/src/app/login/page.tsx` lines 20–24

```ts
// Current vulnerable code
const redirectPath = searchParams.get('from') || '/';
// ...
router.replace(redirectPath); // No validation — accepts any URL including external ones
```

## Environment / Wallet

- Frontend: Next.js (React 19)
- Affected: All browsers, all environments

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `https://<app-url>/login?from=https://evil.com`
2. Enter valid credentials and log in
3. Observe: user is redirected to `https://evil.com` instead of the app

## Relevant Logs/Error Messages

No error is thrown — the redirect succeeds silently, which is what makes this dangerous.

## Suggested Fix

Validate that the redirect path is an internal relative path only:

```ts
const raw = searchParams.get('from') || '/';
const redirectPath = raw.startsWith('/') && !raw.startsWith('//') ? raw : '/';
router.replace(redirectPath);
```

This ensures external URLs (anything with `://` or `//`) are rejected and the user falls back to `/`.

## Impact

- Enables phishing attacks using the legitimate app domain as the entry point
- OWASP lists Open Redirect as a well-known web vulnerability class (CWE-601)
- Attackers can steal credentials by redirecting to a lookalike page after login

## Additional Context

- Difficulty: Beginner-friendly (single-line fix)
- Area: Frontend security
- Related OWASP: [CWE-601 – URL Redirection to Untrusted Site](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html)

issues.title: [Bug]: CI workflow references non-existent tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py — E2E tests never run, giving false green
issues.body:
## Bug Summary

The CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) references `tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py` in a test step, but this file does not exist in the repository. As a result, E2E tests either silently produce a false-green pass (no tests collected = no failures) or crash the test runner, depending on pytest configuration.

## Describe the bug

In `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (~line 93), a CI step runs:

```yaml
- name: Run E2E API tests
  run: pytest tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py
```

The file `tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py` does not exist anywhere in the repository. This means:

- **Scenario A (most common):** pytest exits with `ERROR: not found: tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py` — the entire CI job fails or is skipped, blocking other tests.
- **Scenario B:** If `--ignore-glob` or similar config is set, pytest collects 0 tests and exits 0 — contributors see green CI with zero E2E coverage, creating false confidence.

Either way, **no E2E tests are ever executed**, and the CI status does not accurately reflect the health of the API.

## To Reproduce

1. Open `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and locate the E2E test step (~line 93)
2. Confirm that `tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py` does not exist: `ls tests/`
3. Push any change and observe the CI E2E step output

## Expected behavior

The CI step either:
- Runs a real `tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py` that exercises core API endpoints, OR
- Is removed / updated to reference the correct test file if it was renamed

## Actual behavior

The referenced test file does not exist. CI reports a missing-file error or silently collects 0 tests.

## Screenshots / Error Logs

```
ERROR: not found: /path/to/tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py
(no name '/path/to/tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py' in any of [<Dir hybrid-recommender>])
```

## OS

Ubuntu (GitHub Actions runner)

## Python version

As configured in CI (3.10+)

## Additional context

**Fix options (pick one):**

1. **Create a minimal E2E test file** with basic smoke tests for key API endpoints (recommended):
```python
# tests/test_e2e_api_suite.py
import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from backend.main import app

client = TestClient(app)

def test_health_endpoint():
    response = client.get("/api/health")
    assert response.status_code == 200

def test_search_endpoint_returns_results():
    response = client.get("/api/search?q=laptop")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert isinstance(response.json(), list)
```

2. **Update the CI step** to point to an existing test file if `test_e2e_api_suite.py` was renamed.

3. **Remove the step** until proper E2E tests are authored, so CI doesn't silently skip coverage.

**File:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` ~line 93  
**Impact:** Medium — E2E coverage gap; contributors have false confidence that API integration is tested.  
**Difficulty:** S–M depending on whether a full test file is written or just the CI reference is fixed.  
**Beginner-friendly:** Yes — excellent first contribution.

> Note: distinct from issue #831 (CI pipeline masking failures generally). This is a specific missing-file reference causing a concrete test gap.

issues.title: [Bug]: get_supabase_admin() declares return type -> Client but silently returns None on misconfiguration
issues.body:
## Bug Summary

`get_supabase_admin()` in `src/data/db.py` has a return type annotation of `-> Client` but returns `None` when environment variables are missing. Any caller that calls methods on the result gets an `AttributeError` at runtime.

## Describe the bug

```python
# src/data/db.py ~line 44
def get_supabase_admin() -> Client:   # ← promises a Client
    url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_URL")
    key = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")
    if not url or not key:
        return None               # ← silently returns None
    # ...
    if not client:
        return None               # ← another None return path
```

The function has **two early-return `None` paths** despite advertising `-> Client`. Downstream callers (e.g. `backend/main.py` lines ~1349, ~1441) do:

```python
client = get_supabase_admin()
client.table("products").select("*").execute()  # AttributeError if client is None
```

This silently explodes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'table'` instead of a clear, actionable error.

The incorrect annotation also misleads static type checkers (mypy, pyright) into thinking the return value is always a valid `Client`, suppressing warnings at call sites.

## To Reproduce

1. Unset or rename `SUPABASE_URL` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` environment variables
2. Start the backend and call any endpoint that uses `get_supabase_admin()`
3. Observe `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'table'` instead of a clear config error

## Expected behavior

Either:
- The function raises a descriptive `RuntimeError` / `EnvironmentError` when required env vars are missing, OR
- The return type is corrected to `Optional[Client]` and every call site adds a `None` guard

## Actual behavior

The function returns `None` silently, and callers crash with a confusing `AttributeError`.

## Screenshots / Error Logs

```
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'table'
```

## OS

Any

## Python version

Any (3.9+)

## Additional context

**Option A — fail loudly (preferred):**
```python
def get_supabase_admin() -> Client:
    url = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_URL")
    key = os.environ.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY")
    if not url or not key:
        raise EnvironmentError(
            "SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set"
        )
    # ...
```

**Option B — honest annotation:**
```python
from typing import Optional
def get_supabase_admin() -> Optional[Client]:
    ...
```
Then add `None` guards at every call site.

**File:** `src/data/db.py` lines ~44–67  
**Impact:** Medium — silent `AttributeError` in production when env vars are misconfigured; misleads static analysis.  
**Difficulty:** S — annotation fix + call-site guards or a single `raise` statement.  
**Beginner-friendly:** Yes — good first contribution.

> Note: distinct from issue #553 (duplicate function definitions in db.py). This issue is specifically about the incorrect return type contract.

issues.title: [Bug]: Search endpoint contains a duplicated ~70-line result-formatting block — dead code and maintenance trap
issues.body:
## Bug Summary

The result-processing loop in the search endpoint (`backend/main.py`) appears **twice** in the same function body. The second copy is unreachable dead code that inflates the function by ~70 lines and creates a maintenance trap.

## Describe the bug

Inside the search handler, the block that iterates over `products`, computes per-product sentiment, and appends dicts to `results` is copy-pasted in full at two separate locations (~lines 1010–1052 and ~lines 1084–1126). Both copies are structurally identical:

```python
# First occurrence (~line 1010)
results = []
for p in products:
    raw_sentiment = p.get('avg_sentiment', 0.0)
    reviews = p.get('reviews', [])
    # ... sentiment computation ...
    results.append({...})

# ... ~30 lines of unrelated code ...

# Second occurrence (~line 1084) — exact duplicate
results = []
for p in products:
    raw_sentiment = p.get('avg_sentiment', 0.0)
    reviews = p.get('reviews', [])
    # ... same sentiment computation ...
    results.append({...})
```

Because `results` is reassigned at the start of each block, the first block's output is thrown away. Only the second block's output is ever returned.

## To Reproduce

1. Open `backend/main.py`
2. Search for `results = []` inside the search endpoint handler
3. Observe two identical loops within the same function

## Expected behavior

The result-formatting logic appears exactly once, either inline or extracted into a helper function.

## Actual behavior

The logic is duplicated. Any bug fix or enhancement applied to one copy must be manually mirrored to the other — and reviewers have no way to know which copy is "authoritative."

## Screenshots / Error Logs

N/A — no runtime crash, but a silent correctness risk if the two copies ever diverge.

## OS

Any

## Python version

Any (3.9+)

## Additional context

**Fix:** Extract the block into a helper function and call it once:

```python
def _format_product_results(products: list) -> list:
    results = []
    for p in products:
        raw_sentiment = p.get('avg_sentiment', 0.0)
        # ... rest of logic ...
        results.append({...})
    return results
```

Then replace both occurrences with a single call.

**File:** `backend/main.py` lines ~1010–1052 and ~1084–1126  
**Impact:** Medium — maintenance risk; current output is only from the second copy.  
**Difficulty:** S — pure refactor, no logic changes required.  
**Beginner-friendly:** Yes — good first contribution.

issues.title: [Bug]: _admin_access_dep used in Depends() on 5 admin endpoints but never defined — NameError at startup
issues.body:
## Bug Summary

`_admin_access_dep` is referenced as a FastAPI dependency (`Depends(_admin_access_dep)`) on 5 admin endpoints in `backend/main.py` but is never defined or imported, causing a `NameError` when those routes are registered.

## Describe the bug

Five admin endpoints in `backend/main.py` use:

```python
_admin: None = Depends(_admin_access_dep)
```

But `_admin_access_dep` does not exist anywhere in `main.py` and is never imported. FastAPI evaluates `Depends()` arguments at route-registration time (application startup), so these 5 endpoints fail to register with:

```
NameError: name '_admin_access_dep' is not defined
```

**Affected endpoints:**
| Endpoint | Approx. line |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/build` | ~1345 |
| `POST /api/train/federated` | ~1439 |
| `POST /api/models/{version}/promote` | ~1901 |
| `POST /api/models/{version}/shadow` | ~1944 |
| `PUT /api/weights` | ~1975 |

Meanwhile, `backend/auth.py` defines `_require_admin_access` (different name) which appears to be the intended function but is never imported into `main.py`.

## To Reproduce

1. Start the FastAPI backend: `uvicorn backend.main:app`
2. Observe startup crash or that the 5 endpoints listed above are unreachable (return 404 / 500)

## Expected behavior

Admin endpoints register correctly at startup and enforce authentication via the admin dependency.

## Actual behavior

`NameError: name '_admin_access_dep' is not defined` — all 5 admin endpoints are broken.

## Screenshots / Error Logs

```
NameError: name '_admin_access_dep' is not defined
```

## OS

Any

## Python version

Any (3.9+)

## Additional context

**Fix:** Import the existing auth function under the expected name at the top of `main.py`:

```python
from backend.auth import _require_admin_access as _admin_access_dep
```

Then verify the function signature is compatible with FastAPI's `Depends()` pattern.

**File:** `backend/main.py` lines ~1345, 1439, 1901, 1944, 1975; `backend/auth.py`  
**Impact:** High — entire admin API surface is non-functional.  
**Difficulty:** S — import fix + signature compatibility check.

> Note: this is distinct from issue #593 (which is a security concern about CSRF not being real auth). This issue is about a hard crash — the function literally does not exist.

issues.title: [Bug]: products = MOCK_PRODUCTS placed outside except block silently discards all real search results
issues.body:
## Bug Summary

`products = MOCK_PRODUCTS` is placed **outside** the `except` block in the search endpoint, so it unconditionally overwrites whatever the Supabase query returned. Every search call returns the same 3 hardcoded products.

## Describe the bug

In `backend/main.py` the search handler runs a Supabase query inside a `try` block, assigns `products = result.data or []`, and then — outside the `except` — immediately reassigns `products = MOCK_PRODUCTS`. Because the reassignment is at the same indentation level as `try/except` (not inside `except`), it runs on **every** request, including completely successful ones.

```python
try:
    # ... Supabase query (lines ~935–992)
    products = result.data or []
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning("Search fallback to mock products: %s", e)

products = MOCK_PRODUCTS   # ← outside except, always executes — overwrites real results
```

## To Reproduce

1. Start the backend server
2. Send `GET /api/search?q=<any query>`
3. Observe that the response always contains the same 3 hardcoded items from `MOCK_PRODUCTS`, regardless of the query or database contents

## Expected behavior

The endpoint returns real products fetched from Supabase that match the search query. `MOCK_PRODUCTS` should only be used as a fallback when the database query fails.

## Actual behavior

All search responses return the hardcoded `MOCK_PRODUCTS` list. The Supabase query runs and succeeds, but its result is immediately discarded.

## Screenshots / Error Logs

No exception is raised — the bug is silent. The only observable symptom is that search results never change.

## OS

Any

## Python version

Any (3.9+)

## Additional context

**Fix:** Move the assignment inside the `except` block:

```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning("Search fallback to mock products: %s", e)
    products = MOCK_PRODUCTS   # ← correct placement
```

**File:** `backend/main.py` ~line 993  
**Impact:** High — the entire search feature is non-functional; real data is never surfaced to users.  
**Difficulty:** XS — single-line indentation change.

issues.title: [BUG] Processed images never deleted from Python AI service disk — unbounded storage growth
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Every call to the `/remove-bg` endpoint saves the processed PNG file to `config.UPLOAD_DIR` on disk and **never deletes it**. Similarly, `/generate-sheet` writes a JPEG to `outputs/` and never cleans it up. There is no cleanup code anywhere in the Python AI service — confirmed by the complete absence of `os.unlink`, `os.remove`, `shutil.rmtree`, or any scheduled cleanup.

Under normal production usage, this means processed passport photos — which contain recognizable faces — accumulate indefinitely on the server's filesystem. In a Docker container with a fixed volume, this will eventually exhaust disk space and crash the service.

**Relevant code**

`python-ai-service/app/routes/process_routes.py` (lines 38–47):
```python
save_path = os.path.join(config.UPLOAD_DIR, filename)
with open(save_path, "wb") as f:
    f.write(final_image)

return send_file(save_path, mimetype="image/png", ...)
# ← file remains on disk permanently; no cleanup
```

`python-ai-service/main.py` (lines 41–55):
```python
output_path = os.path.join(output_dir, f"sheet_{preset_id}.jpg")
saved = generate_a4_sheet(..., output_path=output_path)
return send_file(saved, mimetype="image/jpeg")
# ← output file never deleted
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Run the Python AI service.
2. Send multiple `/remove-bg` requests.
3. Inspect the `uploads/` directory — each request leaves a new PNG file. No files are ever deleted.

**Expected behavior**
Processed output files should be deleted from disk immediately after the HTTP response is sent (or not written to disk at all for in-memory processing). Uploaded input files that are no longer needed should also be cleaned up.

**Comparison**
The Node.js backend already handles this correctly for Cloudinary uploads:
```js
// backend/src/controllers/upload.controller.js
fs.unlinkSync(localPath);  // ← deletes local file after successful Cloudinary upload
```
The Python service has no equivalent.

**Suggested Fix**

**Option A — Delete after send using Flask's `after_this_request` hook:**
```python
from flask import after_this_request

@after_this_request
def cleanup(response):
    try:
        os.unlink(save_path)
    except OSError:
        pass
    return response

return send_file(save_path, ...)
```

**Option B — Stream from memory, skip disk entirely:**
```python
from io import BytesIO

buf = BytesIO(final_image)
buf.seek(0)
return send_file(buf, mimetype="image/png", download_name=f"{uuid.uuid4().hex}.png")
# No file written to disk at all
```
Option B is preferred as it eliminates the disk I/O entirely and avoids any race conditions in cleanup.

**Desktop:**
- OS: All (Linux in Docker, macOS locally)
- Not browser-specific — server-side resource leak

**Additional context**
- This is also a **privacy concern**: processed passport photos (with face data) sit on the server indefinitely with no data retention policy.
- Issue #351 addresses memory exhaustion via `rembg` model loading — a different resource. No existing issue covers disk accumulation from undeleted output files.

issues.title: [BUG] Internal exception details leaked to clients in Python AI service 500 error responses
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Python AI service returns raw Python exception messages directly to HTTP clients in 500 error responses. The `str(e)` of unhandled exceptions can expose internal filesystem paths, library names, model file locations, and server configuration details — giving attackers a detailed map of the server internals.

**Relevant code**

`python-ai-service/app/routes/process_routes.py` (line 51):
```python
except Exception as e:
    return jsonify({
        "success": False,
        "message": "Background removal failed.",
        "detail": str(e)   # ← full exception string sent to client
    }), 500
```

`python-ai-service/main.py` (line 58):
```python
except (ValueError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
    return jsonify({"error": str(e)}), 400  # ← exception string sent to client
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Send a POST to `/remove-bg` with a deliberately malformed or oversized image that causes an internal error.
2. Observe the response body — it will contain the full Python exception string, e.g.:
   - `"detail": "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/app/uploads/xyz.png'"` → reveals filesystem path
   - `"detail": "cannot identify image file <_io.BytesIO object at 0x7f...>"` → reveals memory layout
   - `"detail": "ONNX model not found at /root/.u2net/u2net.onnx"` → reveals model storage path

**Expected behavior**
- 500 error responses to clients must only contain a generic, user-friendly message (e.g., `"Processing failed. Please try again."`).
- Full exception details must be logged **server-side only** using Python's `logging` module.

**Suggested Fix**
```python
import logging
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

except Exception as e:
    logger.exception("Background removal failed")  # full traceback logged server-side
    return jsonify({"success": False, "message": "Background removal failed. Please try again."}), 500
```
Apply the same pattern to `main.py` and any other route that currently returns `str(e)` to the client.

**Desktop:**
- Affects all environments where the Python AI service is reachable
- Not browser-specific — server-side information disclosure

**Additional context**
- This is a well-known OWASP category: **A05:2021 – Security Misconfiguration** (verbose error messages).
- Issues #403 (CSRF/CSP), #351 (DoS), #347 (HPP), #345 (NoSQL injection) cover other security concerns — none address information leakage via error responses.
- Fix is straightforward: replace `str(e)` in responses with a static string and log using `logger.exception()`. Good first contribution.

issues.title: [BUG] Blob URLs stored in localStorage cause silently broken image preview on session restore in HistoryPage
issues.body: **Describe the bug** `saveSession()` and `saveSessionToHistory()` in `sessionManager.js` persist the `localUrl` field to `localStorage`. This `localUrl` is a `blob:http://...` URL created by `URL.createObjectURL(file)` in `usePhotoUpload.jsx`. Blob URLs are **only valid within the current browser page lifecycle** — after a page refresh, new tab, or browser restart, the browser releases the blob and the URL becomes dead. When a user navigates to `HistoryPage`, selects a past session, and clicks "Restore", `handleRestore()` calls `saveSession(session)` (writing the stale blob URL back to storage) and navigates to `/editor`. `EditorPage` reads `savedSession?.localUrl`, receives the dead blob URL, and the `` renders a broken image with **no error message shown to the user**. **To Reproduce** 1. Go to the Upload page and upload a photo. 2. Proceed to the Editor page (session is now saved to history). 3. Refresh the page or open a new tab and navigate to `/history`. 4. Click "Restore" on the saved session. 5. Observe: the Editor page loads with a broken/invisible image — no feedback is shown. **Expected behavior** Session restore should either: - Use the durable `fileUrl` (Cloudinary/backend URL) as a fallback when `localUrl` is unavailable, **or** - Not persist `localUrl` to `localStorage` at all (strip it before saving), and show a clear message prompting the user to re-upload if the file is unavailable. **Relevant code** `frontend/src/utils/sessionManager.js`: ```js // localUrl (blob: URL) is persisted as-is — invalid after page reload localStorage.setItem(SESSION_KEY, JSON.stringify({ ...data, updatedAt: Date.now() })); ``` `frontend/src/pages/EditorPage.jsx`: ```js const savedSession = getSession(); const [photoData, setPhotoData] = useState({ localUrl: state?.localUrl || savedSession?.localUrl, // ← dead blob URL ... }); ``` **Suggested Fix** Strip `localUrl` before writing to `localStorage` in `saveSessionToHistory`, since blob URLs are ephemeral: ```js export const saveSessionToHistory = (session) => { const { localUrl, ...persistable } = session; // drop ephemeral blob URL const newSession = { ...persistable, id: Date.now().toString(), savedAt: Date.now(), ... }; // save newSession }; ``` In `EditorPage`, fall back to `fileUrl` and show an `EmptyState` with a re-upload prompt if neither URL is valid. **Desktop:** - OS: All - Browser: All (blob URL lifecycle is browser-standard behaviour) **Additional context** - The `HistoryPage` "Restore" feature is entirely non-functional for photo preview across page loads, making the History feature misleading to users. - No existing issue covers blob URL lifecycle or localStorage session restore failure. This is distinct from dark mode and navbar issues.

issues.title: [BUG] POST /api/upload has no authentication — anonymous users can upload files freely
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The `POST /api/upload` route in the Express backend has **no `authMiddleware`**, allowing any unauthenticated user or bot to upload files to the server without being logged in. This leads to unbounded Cloudinary API usage, storage quota consumption, and disk usage — all with no identity tied to the upload.

Compare this to `GET /api/upload/:fileId` which correctly requires `authMiddleware`.

**Relevant code**

`backend/src/routes/upload.routes.js`:
```js
router.post("/", uploadMiddleware.single("photo"), uploadPhoto);  // ← no auth
router.get("/:fileId", authMiddleware, getUploadedPhoto);          // ← auth required
```

`backend/src/controllers/upload.controller.js` (lines ~40–44):
```js
if (req.user?.id) {
  await Upload.create({ ... });  // only logged for authenticated users
}
// anonymous uploads go through silently — consuming Cloudinary quota
```

**To Reproduce**
1. Start the backend locally.
2. Send a POST without any authentication cookie:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/upload \
  -F "photo=@/path/to/any/image.jpg"
```
3. The upload succeeds, the image is sent to Cloudinary, and no DB record is created.

**Expected behavior**
The upload endpoint should require the user to be authenticated. Anonymous upload attempts should return `401 Unauthorized`.

**Suggested Fix**
Add `authMiddleware` (and optionally a stricter upload-specific rate limiter) to the POST route:
```js
import { uploadRateLimiter } from "../middleware/rateLimit.middleware.js";

router.post("/", authMiddleware, uploadMiddleware.single("photo"), uploadPhoto);
```

**Desktop:**
- Affects all environments (local, staging, production)
- Not browser-specific — backend API vulnerability

**Additional context**
- The global `apiLimiter` (100 req / 15 min per IP) is trivially bypassed with IP rotation, providing no real protection.
- Issues #57, #192, and #324 address preprocessing/validation — none address missing authentication on the upload endpoint.
- This is a good first-contribution fix: a targeted, one-line route change with high security impact.

issues.title: [BUG] Path Traversal via caller-controlled photo_path in /generate-sheet endpoint
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The `/generate-sheet` endpoint in the Python AI service accepts a `photo_path` field from the JSON request body and passes it **directly and unsanitized** to `Image.open(photo_path)` inside `sheet_generator.py`. This allows an attacker to supply an arbitrary filesystem path (e.g., `../../etc/passwd`) and read any file accessible to the server process.

Additionally, the `preset_id` field from the same request body is embedded unsanitized into the output filename: `f"sheet_{preset_id}.jpg"`, enabling output path manipulation if `preset_id` contains `../`.

**To Reproduce**
1. Start the Python AI service locally.
2. Send a POST request to `/generate-sheet` with a crafted `photo_path`:
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/generate-sheet \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"photo_path": "../../etc/passwd", "preset_id": "35x45"}'
```
3. The service will attempt to open the specified path. If the file is parseable by Pillow, it reads it; otherwise the error response confirms the path exists.

**Expected behavior**
The `photo_path` parameter should be validated and restricted to files within the designated upload directory (`config.UPLOAD_DIR`). Arbitrary filesystem paths must be rejected with a 400 error.

**Relevant code**

`python-ai-service/main.py` (lines 32–55):
```python
data = request.get_json()
photo_path = data.get("photo_path")   # ← no sanitization
...
saved = generate_a4_sheet(photo_path=photo_path, ...)  # passed raw to Image.open()
```

`python-ai-service/app/services/sheet_generator.py` (line 124):
```python
img = Image.open(photo_path)  # ← opens caller-supplied path directly
```

**Suggested Fix**
Resolve the path and confirm it is within the allowed upload directory before use:
```python
import pathlib, re

ALLOWED_DIR = pathlib.Path(config.UPLOAD_DIR).resolve()

def safe_photo_path(raw: str) -> str:
    resolved = (ALLOWED_DIR / pathlib.Path(raw).name).resolve()
    if not str(resolved).startswith(str(ALLOWED_DIR)):
        raise ValueError("Invalid photo_path: outside of allowed directory")
    return str(resolved)

photo_path = safe_photo_path(data.get("photo_path", ""))
preset_id  = re.sub(r'[^a-zA-Z0-9_\-]', '', data.get("preset_id", "35x45"))
```

**Desktop:**
- Affects all OS / environments where the Python AI service is exposed
- Not browser-specific — server-side vulnerability

**Additional context**
- The Node.js upload controller already handles this correctly by using `fs.unlinkSync` after Cloudinary upload and never accepting raw paths from clients.
- Issues #347, #345, #351, #403 cover other attack surfaces (HPP, NoSQL injection, DoS, CSRF) — this path traversal issue is a distinct, unaddressed vulnerability.

issues.title: [BUG] Newsletter form handler uses querySelector — silently ignores all but the first matching form on any page
[BUG] Newsletter subscription shows success toast for invalid or malformed email inputs — no format validation in JS
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

The newsletter form submit handler in `app.js` performs only a truthy check on the email value before displaying a success toast:

```js
const email = this.querySelector('input[type="email"]').value.trim();
if (email) showToast('Thanks for subscribing!', 'success');
```

The `<input type="email">` HTML5 attribute provides basic browser-level validation, but this can be bypassed in several real-world scenarios:
- Autofill or programmatic form population
- Browsers with lenient validation (some accept `a@b` as valid)
- Any value that is truthy but not a real email (e.g., a single character `a`, or `@`, or `notanemail`)

When bypassed, the handler fires the success toast for garbage input, giving the user false confirmation that they have subscribed — while no actual subscription occurs.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `index.html` or `shop.html`
2. Open DevTools → Console
3. Run: `document.querySelector('.newsletter-form input[type="email"]').value = 'notanemail'`
4. Run: `document.querySelector('.newsletter-form').dispatchEvent(new Event('submit', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))`
5. Observe the "Thanks for subscribing!" success toast appears for a clearly invalid email

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

The handler should validate the email format using a regex before accepting the input. Invalid emails should trigger a warning toast (e.g., "Please enter a valid email address.") and not show a success message.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

Any non-empty string passes the `if (email)` check, resulting in a false success notification being shown to the user for invalid inputs.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

**Affected file:** `app.js`, lines 1047–1059

```js
// Current code — only truthy check
const email = this.querySelector('input[type="email"]').value.trim();
if (email) showToast('Thanks for subscribing!', 'success');  // ← no format check
```

**Suggested fix:**
```js
const email = this.querySelector('input[type="email"]').value.trim();
const emailRegex = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/;
if (email && emailRegex.test(email)) {
    showToast('Thanks for subscribing!', 'success');
} else {
    showToast('Please enter a valid email address.', 'warning');
}
```

---

## 🧩 Environment

- OS: Any  
- Browser: Any (reproducible programmatically in all browsers)  
- Node.js version: N/A (static site)  
- Framework/Library version: Vanilla JS

---

- [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

issues.title: [BUG] Logged-in user's display name never shown — auth state only stores email, user's name is ignored post-login
issues.body: ## 🐞 Description During registration, the user's name is collected and saved: `users.push({ name, email, password })`. However, at login (`login.js:44`) only the email address is persisted as the auth state: ```js localStorage.setItem('loggedInUser', email); ``` The `updateAuthUI()` function in `app.js` reads this value and only checks for its existence — it never retrieves or displays the user's name anywhere in the UI. The navbar simply swaps the login icon for a logout icon, but there is no personalized greeting (e.g., "Welcome, Alice") shown anywhere on the site after logging in. The user's name is effectively thrown away after registration, never surfacing in the authenticated experience. --- ## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce 1. Register a new account at `register.html` with a display name (e.g., "Alice") 2. Get redirected to `index.html` — observe the navbar shows only a logout icon, no name 3. Refresh the page and check any part of the UI for a greeting or username display 4. Observe that the name "Alice" is nowhere visible despite being stored in `localStorage` --- ## 💻 Expected Behavior After login, the authenticated user's display name should be shown in the navbar — e.g., a greeting chip like "Hi, Alice" or an account dropdown with the user's name — providing a personalized, professional e-commerce experience. --- ## 🧠 Actual Behavior The navbar only shows a generic logout icon. The user's name stored in the `users` array is never queried or rendered post-login. The app treats all logged-in users identically, with no personalization. --- ## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable) **`login.js:44–48` — only email is saved:** ```js if (user) { localStorage.setItem('loggedInUser', email); // ← name is discarded window.location.href = 'index.html'; } ``` **`app.js:51–77` — updateAuthUI never reads the name:** ```js const loggedInUser = localStorage.getItem('loggedInUser'); // just the email string if (loggedInUser) { link.innerHTML = ''; // generic icon, no name } ``` **Suggested fix:** On login success, also store the user's display name: ```js localStorage.setItem('loggedInUser', email); localStorage.setItem('loggedInUserName', user.name); // ← add this ``` In `updateAuthUI()`, render a personalized greeting: ```js const userName = localStorage.getItem('loggedInUserName'); if (loggedInUser && userName) { // e.g., insert a greeting element into the navbar const greeting = document.createElement('span'); greeting.className = 'nav-greeting'; greeting.textContent = `Hi, ${userName}`; } ``` Also clear `loggedInUserName` on logout alongside `loggedInUser`. --- ## 🧩 Environment - OS: Any - Browser: Any - Node.js version: N/A (static site) - Framework/Library version: Vanilla JS --- ## ✅ Checklist - [x] I have searched for existing issues before creating this one. - [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

issues.title: [BUG] Discount coupon codes CARA20 and WELCOME10 hardcoded in plaintext client-side JS — exploitable by any user
[BUG] User passwords stored as plaintext in localStorage — critical security vulnerability
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

`register.js` stores the full user object — including the **raw plaintext password** — directly in `localStorage`:

```js
users.push({ name, email, password });
localStorage.setItem('users', JSON.stringify(users));
```

Any script running on the page, any browser extension, any XSS payload, or any person with physical access to the device can retrieve every registered user's password in one line:

```js
JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('users'))
// → [{ name: 'Alice', email: 'alice@example.com', password: 'MySecret@1' }, ...]
```

This is distinct from issue #1798, which addresses hashing the session token (the `loggedInUser` key). This issue is about the **actual user passwords** stored in the `users` array.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a new account at `register.html` with any credentials
2. Open DevTools → Application → Local Storage
3. Click the entry for `users`
4. Observe the full plaintext password is visible in the stored JSON

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

Passwords should never be stored in plaintext. Before storing, passwords must be hashed with a one-way function so the original value cannot be recovered. Login comparison must then hash the input and compare hashes.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

Passwords are stored as-is in plaintext inside `localStorage`, readable by anyone with DevTools access or via an XSS attack.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

**Affected files and lines:**

| File | Line | Issue |
|------|------|-------|
| `register.js:39` | `users.push({ name, email, password })` | Plaintext stored |
| `login.js:44` | `u.password === password` | Plaintext compared |
| `forgotPassword.js:67` | `users[userIndex].password = newPass` | Plaintext overwritten |

**Suggested fix using Web Crypto API (no dependencies):**
```js
async function hashPassword(password) {
  const encoder = new TextEncoder();
  const data = encoder.encode(password);
  const hashBuffer = await crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', data);
  return Array.from(new Uint8Array(hashBuffer))
    .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join('');
}

// On register:
const hashed = await hashPassword(password);
users.push({ name, email, password: hashed });

// On login:
const hashed = await hashPassword(inputPassword);
const user = users.find(u => u.email === email && u.password === hashed);
```

> Note: For a production app, password hashing must happen server-side. Client-side hashing is an improvement over plaintext but is not a substitute for a secure backend authentication system.

---

## 🧩 Environment

- OS: Any  
- Browser: Any  
- Node.js version: N/A (static site)  
- Framework/Library version: Vanilla JS

---

issues.title: [BUG] Products 17–32 reuse the same 16 product images — wrong photos displayed on product cards
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

The `products` array in `products.js` defines 32 products but only 16 unique image files exist (`f1.jpg`–`f8.jpg` and `n1.jpg`–`n8.jpg`). Products 17–32 are assigned the exact same image paths as products 1–16, causing entirely different products to show the same photo.

- Product id:4 "Sakura Blossom Floral Shirt" and Product id:20 "Indigo Denim Jacket" both use `images/products/f4.jpg`

Each product should display a unique image that visually corresponds to its name and description. "Indigo Denim Jacket" should show a denim jacket, not a floral shirt.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

Products 17–32 display recycled images from products 1–16. The visual mismatch confuses users and breaks trust in the catalog.

issues.title: [BUG] forgotPassword.js allows resetting to a weaker password (6 chars) than registration requires (8+ chars with complexity)
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

The password validation rules are **inconsistent** between the registration and forgot-password flows:

- **`register.js:15`** enforces a strong policy: 8+ characters, at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one special character (`@$!%*?&`)
- **`forgotPassword.js:33`** only checks that the new password is **6 or more characters** — no complexity requirements at all

This means a user can bypass the intended password security policy by using the "Forgot Password" flow to reset their account password to something like `abc123`, which would be rejected at registration.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Register a new account at `register.html` — observe that weak passwords like `abc123` are rejected
2. Navigate to `forgotPassword.html`
3. Enter your registered email and set a new password of `abc123` (6 chars, no complexity)
4. Observe that the password is accepted and the account is updated with the weak password

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

The forgot-password form should enforce the **same password complexity rules** as the registration form. A password that would be rejected during signup should also be rejected during password reset.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

`forgotPassword.js` only validates minimum length of 6 characters, allowing users to reset to a password far weaker than what registration requires, silently downgrading account security.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

**`register.js:15` — strict validation:**
```js
const passwordRegex = /^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&]).{8,}$/;
if (!passwordRegex.test(password)) {
    showToast('Password must have 8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 number, and 1 special character.', 'warning');
    return;
}
```

**`forgotPassword.js:33` — weak validation:**
```js
if (!newPass || newPass.length < 6) {
    showToast('Password must be at least 6 characters!', 'warning');
    return;
}
```

**Suggested fix — reuse the same regex in `forgotPassword.js`:**
```js
const passwordRegex = /^(?=.*[a-z])(?=.*[A-Z])(?=.*\d)(?=.*[@$!%*?&]).{8,}$/;
if (!newPass || !passwordRegex.test(newPass)) {
    showToast('Password must have 8+ chars, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 number, and 1 special character.', 'warning');
    return;
}
```

Ideally, extract the regex into a shared utility (e.g., `utils.js`) so both files stay in sync.

---

## 🧩 Environment

- OS: Any  
- Browser: Any  
- Node.js version: N/A (static site)  
- Framework/Library version: Vanilla JS

issues.title: [BUG] Toast notification container missing aria-live region — screen readers never announce cart, error, or success messages
issues.body:
## 🐞 Description

The `showToast()` function in `app.js` dynamically creates a `#toast-container` div but never assigns an `aria-live` attribute or a `role="status"` to it. As a result, screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) are never notified when a toast notification appears. 

This means assistive-technology users receive **zero feedback** for critical user interactions such as:
- Adding an item to the cart
- Applying a promo code (success or failure)
- Login/signup errors or successes
- Newsletter subscription confirmation
- Order-related notifications

This is a **WCAG 2.1 SC 4.1.3 (Status Messages, Level AA)** violation.

---

## 🔁 Steps to Reproduce

1. Enable a screen reader (e.g., VoiceOver on macOS: ⌘ + F5)
2. Open `index.html` or `shop.html`
3. Add any product to the cart
4. Observe that the toast notification "Item added to cart!" appears visually but the screen reader announces **nothing**

---

## 💻 Expected Behavior

When a toast notification appears, the screen reader should automatically announce its message (e.g., "Tropical Hibiscus Summer Shirt added to cart!") without requiring the user to navigate to it.

---

## 🧠 Actual Behavior

The toast container is appended to `document.body` with no live-region role. Screen readers only announce elements in their reading order or elements explicitly marked as live regions. Users relying on screen readers get no feedback from any toast in the app.

---

## 🖼️ Screenshots / Logs (if applicable)

**Affected file:** `app.js`, lines 299–315

```js
// Current code — no aria-live, no role
var container = document.getElementById('toast-container');
if (!container) {
    container = document.createElement('div');
    container.id = 'toast-container';
    document.body.appendChild(container);  // ← missing aria attributes
}
```

**Suggested fix (2-line change):**
```js
if (!container) {
    container = document.createElement('div');
    container.id = 'toast-container';
    container.setAttribute('role', 'status');           // ← add this
    container.setAttribute('aria-live', 'polite');      // ← add this
    container.setAttribute('aria-atomic', 'false');     // ← add this
    document.body.appendChild(container);
}
```

---

## 🧩 Environment

- OS: Any  
- Browser: Any  
- Node.js version: N/A (static site)  
- Framework/Library version: Vanilla JS

---

- [x] I have included all relevant details and reproduction steps.

[BUG] Expired verification and password-reset tokens are never purged — no TTL index on User token fields
issues.body:
## Description

`server/src/database/models/User.js` lines 64–67 define four time-limited token fields on the User schema:

```js
verificationToken: { type: String, default: null },
verificationTokenExpires: { type: Date, default: null },
resetPasswordToken: { type: String, default: null },
resetPasswordExpires: { type: Date, default: null },
```

None of these fields have a **MongoDB TTL (Time-To-Live) index**. The application correctly checks expiry at read time, but expired tokens are **never nullified or removed** after they expire. Every failed email verification attempt and every expired password reset request permanently stores a token in the database.

## Reproduction Steps

1. Register an account but do not verify the email — let the OTP expire
2. Request a password reset but do not complete it — let the token expire
3. Run: `db.users.find({ verificationTokenExpires: { $lt: new Date() } })` or `db.users.find({ resetPasswordExpires: { $lt: new Date() } })`
4. Observe: Users with expired tokens appear, and the token fields still contain stale non-null values

## Expected Behavior

Expired token fields should be automatically nullified either via:
- A MongoDB TTL index that removes documents (not applicable here since we want to keep the User doc), OR
- Nullifying the token fields immediately after successful verification/reset (partially done for `otpAttempts` but inconsistently for token fields), OR
- A periodic cleanup job that nulls out fields where `*Expires < now()`

## Screenshots / Logs

Compare with `server/src/database/models/SemanticCache.js` line 45, which correctly uses TTL:
```js
semanticCacheSchema.index({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 604800 });
```
The User model does not have a similar mechanism for token cleanup.

## Environment Details

- OS: Any
- Database: MongoDB
- Affected: All users who have unverified registrations or initiated (but not completed) password resets

## Additional Context

**Why this matters:**

1. **Storage growth** — at scale, millions of stale token fields waste disk space in the users collection
2. **Security hygiene** — expired tokens that linger can obscure audit trails and make it harder to detect token replay attempts
3. **Data quality** — querying users by token state returns misleading results if expired tokens look "active" in the raw document

**Suggested Fix:**

Option A — Null out tokens after successful verification/reset in the service layer (simple, targeted):
```js
// After successful email verification in auth/service.js
user.verificationToken = null;
user.verificationTokenExpires = null;
await user.save();
```

Option B — Add a Mongoose virtual or scheduled cleanup (more robust):
```js
// In a scheduled job (e.g., using node-cron):
await User.updateMany(
  { verificationTokenExpires: { $lt: new Date() } },
  { $set: { verificationToken: null, verificationTokenExpires: null } }
);
```

issues.title: [BUG] cascadeDeleteUser leaves orphaned RoadmapComment documents and does not remove user from ClassroomSession participants
issues.body:
## Description

`server/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js` — the `cascadeDeleteUser()` function is missing two cleanup operations:

1. **`RoadmapComment` documents are never deleted.** The model `server/src/database/models/RoadmapComment.js` exists and stores comments authored by users, but `RoadmapComment` is never imported or deleted in `cascadeDelete.js`. After account deletion, all of a user's roadmap comments remain in MongoDB referencing a non-existent `userId`.

2. **User is not removed from `ClassroomSession.participants`.** Line 70 deletes sessions where `host: userId`, but when a user joined someone else's classroom session as a *participant*, their ID remains in the `participants` array of those sessions forever. The `ClassroomSession` schema defines a `participants` array field (line 65).

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create a user account and post one or more Roadmap comments
2. Also join another user's classroom session as a participant
3. Delete the account via the delete-account flow
4. Query `db.roadmapcomments.find({ user: <deletedUserId> })` — documents still exist
5. Query `db.classroomsessions.find({ participants: <deletedUserId> })` — ID still in array

## Expected Behavior

All documents authored by or referencing a deleted user should be cleaned up atomically within the same MongoDB transaction in `cascadeDeleteUser()`.

## Screenshots / Logs

```js
// server/src/utils/cascadeDelete.js — current state (missing lines)
// RoadmapComment is NOT imported
// ClassroomSession only cleans up where user is host:
await ClassroomSession.deleteMany({ host: userId }, { session });  // line 70
// participants array is never purged
```

## Environment Details

- OS: Any
- Backend: Node.js + MongoDB + Mongoose

## Additional Context

**Why this matters:**

- **GDPR Article 17 (Right to Erasure):** The delete-account feature must remove ALL user-identifying data. Roadmap comments contain user-written content that can be personally identifying.
- **Data integrity:** Querying roadmap comments for a deleted user could throw NullPointerErrors or return ghost entries in the UI
- **Storage bloat:** Orphaned documents accumulate silently over time

**Suggested Fix** (add inside the transaction block in `cascadeDelete.js`):

```js
import RoadmapComment from "../database/models/RoadmapComment.js";

// Inside the transaction:
await RoadmapComment.deleteMany({ user: userId }, { session });

await ClassroomSession.updateMany(
```

## Issue Summary

Backend API tests duplicate route logic instead of testing the real Express server implementation.

## Issue Description

The backend test file creates a new Express app inside `server/tests/api.test.js` and reimplements the route handlers being tested. This means the tests can pass even if the real routes in `server/server.js` are changed, broken, missing middleware, or wired differently.

The current tests are useful, but they validate duplicated logic rather than the real app module. This can create false confidence and allow regressions in `server/server.js` to go unnoticed.

## Proposed Solution (Optional)

Suggested approach:

- Refactor the backend so the Express app can be imported by tests without automatically starting the server.
- For example, move app creation into `createApp()` or `app.js`, then keep `app.listen()` in a separate startup file.
- Update `server/tests/api.test.js` to start the real exported app on the test port.
- Add regression tests for validation failures, unknown quiz IDs, leaderboard aggregation, and any middleware that should apply to production routes.

Medium - Should be addressed soon

## Category

- Refactor
- Enhancement

- Future contributors may update `server/server.js` while the duplicated test routes continue to pass.

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Indicates that the pull request or issue is currently under review.

issues.body:
## Issue Summary

Secure the backend code execution endpoint used by the playground.

## Issue Description

The backend exposes `POST /api/execute-code` in `server/server.js`, which accepts user-submitted Python, C++, and Java source code, writes it into the host temp directory, and runs it with `child_process.exec`.

Relevant locations:

- `server/server.js`: `app.use(cors())` enables unrestricted CORS for the backend.
- `server/server.js`: `/api/execute-code` accepts and executes submitted code.
- `server/server.js`: Python/C++/Java commands are assembled and executed on the host.
- `src/pages/playground/index.tsx`: the playground calls `/api/execute-code` for non-JavaScript languages.

There is a timeout and output buffer limit, but the endpoint does not currently provide a real execution sandbox. It also does not appear to enforce CPU/memory isolation, filesystem/network restrictions, request body limits, or endpoint-specific rate limiting.

This is different from the existing issue about deployed playground requests using a hardcoded localhost API URL. This issue focuses on the security model of executing untrusted code on the backend host.

## Proposed Solution (Optional)

Suggested approach:

- Gate server-side execution behind an explicit environment flag so it cannot be accidentally enabled in production.
- Add strict request body limits and endpoint-specific rate limiting for `/api/execute-code`.
- Restrict CORS origins through configuration instead of allowing all origins.
- Run submitted code in an isolated sandbox or external judge service rather than directly on the backend host.
- Use per-run isolated temp directories and robust cleanup for source, binary, and class files.
- Add tests that confirm execution is disabled or safely rejected when sandboxing is not configured.

## Priority

High - Requires urgent attention

## Category

- Security
- Refactor

## Additional Context (Optional)

Why this matters:

- Public code execution endpoints are high-risk unless isolated.
- Timeout alone does not prevent filesystem access, network access, resource abuse, or host compromise.
- A safer execution boundary would improve the playground's production readiness.

This is not beginner-friendly. It is better suited for an intermediate or advanced contributor familiar with backend security and process isolation.

issues.title: [Cleanup] analyze.py first DATA_FILE declaration is dead code — silently overwritten 18 lines later

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

labels.name: type:performance
labels.description: Speed, memory efficiency, or loading time optimizations.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`analyze.py` declares the `DATA_FILE` variable **twice** at module level. The first declaration (a bare relative path) is immediately and silently overwritten by a second declaration (a robust absolute path) 18 lines later, making the first assignment unreachable dead code.

**First declaration (analyze.py line 6) — dead code:**
```python
DATA_FILE = "diabetes_dataset.csv"   # ← this value is never used
```

**Second declaration (analyze.py line ~24-28) — the one that actually applies:**
```python
SCRIPT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DATA_FILE = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "attached_assets", "diabetes_dataset.csv")
if not os.path.exists(DATA_FILE):
    DATA_FILE = os.path.join(SCRIPT_DIR, "diabetes_dataset.csv")
```

The relative path `"diabetes_dataset.csv"` at line 6 is assigned to `DATA_FILE` and then unconditionally replaced before any function ever reads it.

**Why this matters:**
1. **Misleads readers**: A developer reading the top of the file sees `DATA_FILE = "diabetes_dataset.csv"` and incorrectly concludes this is the active path. This has caused confusion in past PRs that attempted to use the relative path.
2. **False fallback impression**: It may look like the relative path is a fallback, but it is NOT — the second block completely overwrites it without reading the first value.
3. **Tool confusion**: Linters and static analysis tools may flag the unused first assignment, and grep-based searches for `DATA_FILE` return a misleading result at line 6.

**To Reproduce**
1. Read lines 1-30 of `analyze.py`
2. Note that line 6 assigns `DATA_FILE` and lines 24-28 reassign it unconditionally
3. Verify: the value `"diabetes_dataset.csv"` from line 6 is never used

**Expected behavior**
`DATA_FILE` should be declared exactly once, with the robust absolute path that already handles path resolution correctly.

**Suggested fix**
Delete line 6:
```python
# Remove this line entirely:
DATA_FILE = "diabetes_dataset.csv"
```

The correct definition already exists at lines ~24-28 and handles both the `attached_assets/` path and the legacy fallback.

**Additional context**
This is a beginner-friendly one-line cleanup. It has zero functional impact (the code already works correctly using the second declaration) but removes confusion and cleans up the module's top-level state. A comment explaining the path resolution logic at the second declaration site would be a welcome addition to the PR.

issues.title: [BUG] users table updatedAt column is never updated after email verification or other profile changes

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The `users` table has an `updatedAt` column, but no UPDATE query in the codebase ever sets it. PostgreSQL does not have an implicit `ON UPDATE CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` — the column only gets a value at INSERT time via `defaultNow()`. After that, it is permanently frozen at the account creation timestamp.

**Schema definition (shared/schema.ts line ~60):**
```ts
export const users = pgTable("users", {
  // ...
  updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at").defaultNow().notNull(),  // ← only set at INSERT
});
```

**Example: email verification update (server/auth.ts line ~531):**
```ts
await db
  .update(users)
  .set({ emailVerified: true, emailVerifiedAt: new Date() })  // ← updatedAt missing
  .where(eq(users.id, user.id));
```

Every `.set({...})` call on the `users` table omits `updatedAt`. This means after email verification, role changes, or any future profile update, `updatedAt` will continue to report the original account creation time.

**Impact:**
- Audit queries like "users whose profiles changed in the last 30 days" return wrong results
- Cache invalidation strategies based on `updatedAt` will never trigger
- Admin dashboards or future analytics using `updatedAt` will silently show stale data

**To Reproduce**
1. Register a new account and note the `updatedAt` value in the database
2. Verify the account's email
3. Query the database: `SELECT updated_at FROM users WHERE email = '...'`
4. `updated_at` still shows the original registration timestamp, not the verification time

**Expected behavior**
`updatedAt` should be set to `new Date()` in every UPDATE query on the `users` table.

**Suggested fix**
Add `updatedAt: new Date()` to every `.set({...})` block that modifies a user record:
```ts
await db
  .update(users)
  .set({ emailVerified: true, emailVerifiedAt: new Date(), updatedAt: new Date() })
  .where(eq(users.id, user.id));
```

Alternatively, consider using a Drizzle `$onUpdate` helper if supported by the version in use, to enforce this automatically at the ORM layer.

**Additional context**
This is a beginner-friendly contribution — the fix is to add `updatedAt: new Date()` to each update query in `server/auth.ts`. There is currently only one user UPDATE query (email verification), making the scope of the fix small and well-defined.

issues.title: [Cleanup] server/middleware/rateLimiter.ts exports publicApiRateLimiter but it is never imported or used anywhere

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

labels.name: type:performance
labels.description: Speed, memory efficiency, or loading time optimizations.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`server/middleware/rateLimiter.ts` defines and exports a custom `publicApiRateLimiter` middleware, but this function is **never imported in any other file** in the codebase. The entire module is dead code.

**Verification:**
```bash
grep -rn "publicApiRateLimiter\|from.*rateLimiter" server/ --include="*.ts"
# Only result: the export declaration inside rateLimiter.ts itself
```

**The module has two problems:**

**Problem 1 — Dead code:**
The middleware is exported but never mounted on any route or registered in the Express app. The application already uses `express-rate-limit` for endpoint-specific rate limiting (`assessmentLimiter`, `authLimiter`, `otpLimiter` in `routes.ts` and `auth.ts`). This custom implementation is a parallel, disconnected implementation.

**Problem 2 — Security flaw in the dead code:**
Even though it is unused, the implementation has a vulnerability that would matter if it were ever enabled:
```ts
// rateLimiter.ts
const ip = req.ip || req.headers["x-forwarded-for"] || "unknown";
```
`req.headers["x-forwarded-for"]` is a client-controlled header. Without proper proxy trust configuration (`app.set("trust proxy", ...)`), this header can be forged by any client to bypass rate limiting entirely. The application already sets `trust proxy` correctly in `server/index.ts` for production, but the raw header read here bypasses that.

**To Reproduce**
1. Search for any `import` of `publicApiRateLimiter` across the codebase — none exist
2. Read `server/middleware/rateLimiter.ts` — the export is the only reference to itself

**Expected behavior**
Either:
- **Delete** `server/middleware/rateLimiter.ts` if public API rate limiting is already covered by `express-rate-limit` middleware on individual routes, OR
- **Wire it up** by importing it in `server/index.ts` and mounting it as global middleware: `app.use(publicApiRateLimiter)`, and fix the `x-forwarded-for` extraction to use only `req.ip` (which already respects the `trust proxy` setting).

**Additional context**
This is a good beginner-friendly contribution. The dead code creates confusion for new contributors who may assume the middleware is providing active protection when it is not.

2. Inspect the code demo card in the hero section
3. Locate the copy button (top-right of the card, shows a `Copy` or `Check` icon)
4. Use a screen reader (VoiceOver, NVDA, or browser accessibility inspector) to focus the button

### Expected behavior

The screen reader should announce something like **"Copy code, button"** when focused, and **"Copied to clipboard, button"** after clicking.

### Actual behavior

The screen reader announces **"button"** with no name — the user has no way to know what the button does.

### Affected area

Other

### Environment

All browsers / OS combinations. Testable with browser DevTools accessibility panel (no screen reader needed — the button will show "No accessible name" in the Accessibility tree).

**Relevant code:**
```tsx
// modules/home/hero-code.tsx:60-65  (current — missing aria-label)
<button
    onClick={onCopy}
    className="text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground transition-colors"
>
    {copied ? <Check className="w-4 h-4" /> : <Copy className="w-4 h-4" />}
</button>
```

**Fix:**
```tsx
<button
    onClick={onCopy}
    aria-label={copied ? "Copied to clipboard" : "Copy code"}
    className="text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground transition-colors"
>
    {copied ? <Check className="w-4 h-4" /> : <Copy className="w-4 h-4" />}
</button>
```

The dynamic `aria-label` also communicates the state change (copy → copied) to assistive technology without any additional ARIA needed.

**Note:** This is the same class of issue already fixed in other components via issues #283 (`env-manager.tsx`), #281 (`playground-explorer.tsx`), and #279 (`terminal.tsx`). The homepage hero section was missed in those passes.

### Screenshots, logs, or recordings

Affected file: `modules/home/hero-code.tsx` lines 60–65
