- [x] I included enough detail for reproduction.

issues.title: [Bug]: CodeLine component uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML without HTML entity escaping — breaks display for JSX/typed code
issues.body:
### Short summary `modules/home/code-line.tsx` uses `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` to inject syntax-highlighting `` tags, but never escapes HTML special characters (`<`, `>`, `&`) in the input first. Any code line containing angle brackets (TypeScript generics, JSX, comparison operators) will render as broken or corrupted HTML. The component itself has an internal TODO comment acknowledging it should be replaced with a proper library. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open `modules/home/hero-code.tsx` 2. Add a line containing angle brackets to `codeSnippet`, for example: ```ts const codeSnippet = `... const elements: Array = []; const isSmaller = a < b; return
Hello
; `; ``` 3. Run the dev server and visit the homepage (`/`) 4. Observe the "code demo" card ### Expected behavior The code lines should render as readable, syntax-highlighted text. Angle brackets and HTML-special characters should be displayed as literal characters. ### Actual behavior - `Array` → the `` part is parsed as an HTML element and disappears from the DOM - `a < b` → `< b` opens a malformed HTML tag, corrupting everything that follows - `
Hello
` → renders as a real DOM `
` inside the code block The `highlightCode` function in `code-line.tsx` (lines 24–30) does string replacements that produce raw HTML, then passes the result directly to `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` **without escaping entities first**: ```tsx // modules/home/code-line.tsx:24-30 const highlightCode = (code: string) => { return code .replace(/import|from|export|.../g, '$&') .replace(/'[^']*'/g, '$&') // ... no HTML entity escaping anywhere } // line 21 return ; ``` The component even has a self-aware comment at lines 6-8: > `// Note: This is a very simplistic implementation and should be replaced with a proper library like prismjs or shiki in production` ### Affected area Other ### Environment All browsers, all OSes. Reproducible locally by editing `hero-code.tsx` to include any JSX or generic TypeScript in `codeSnippet`. The current hardcoded snippet happens to avoid angle brackets, which is why this hasn't surfaced yet — but it's a latent bug waiting to break the homepage. **Root cause:** ```tsx // Should escape entities BEFORE injecting spans: const escapeHtml = (str: string) => str.replace(/&/g, "&").replace(//g, ">"); const highlightCode = (code: string) => { const safe = escapeHtml(code); // escape first return safe.replace(/import|from|.../g, '$&'); }; ``` **Better long-term fix** (as the existing TODO suggests): replace the entire `CodeLine` component with [`shiki`](https://shiki.matsu.io/) or [`prism-react-renderer`](https://github.com/FormidableLabs/prism-react-renderer), both of which handle escaping correctly and provide real language-aware tokenization. ### Screenshots, logs, or recordings Affected file: `modules/home/code-line.tsx` lines 24–39 Consumer: `modules/home/hero-code.tsx` lines 72–79 ### Confirmation - [x] I searched existing issues before opening this report. - [x] I included enough detail for reproduction.

issues.title: [BUG] `State.savedAt` typed as `string | number` union — always stored as `number` (Date.now()), creating silent type ambiguity
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

The `savedAt` field in `src/types.ts` is typed as `string | number`, but it is **always set as a `number`** (`Date.now()`) throughout the codebase. No code path sets it to a string. The union type creates ambiguity: any future code that sorts, compares, or formats sessions by `savedAt` must either add `typeof` guards or risk subtle bugs (e.g., lexicographic string comparison instead of numeric timestamp comparison).

**What went wrong?** A union type was used where a single concrete type is sufficient.
**What feature is affected?** Meeting session history ordering; any future date-based sorting or display.
**When does the issue occur?** Silently — the bug hasn't manifested yet, but any future `savedAt` comparison without guards will be subtly wrong.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce (to observe the type)

1. Open `src/types.ts` line 63:
```typescript
export interface State {
  id?: string;
  savedAt?: string | number;   // ← Why is this a union?
  // ...
}
```

2. Search all usages of `savedAt` in the codebase:
```bash
grep -rn "savedAt" src/
```

3. Every assignment uses `Date.now()` (a number):
```typescript
// src/background.ts — sets savedAt as number
const session: StoredSession = { ...snapshot(), id: ..., savedAt: Date.now(), ... };
```

4. No code path ever assigns a `string` to `savedAt`.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

`savedAt` should be typed as `number` only, matching its actual usage. TypeScript should enforce this.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The `string | number` union means:
- Any code comparing two sessions via `sessionA.savedAt > sessionB.savedAt` gets a TypeScript error (operator `>` not applicable to `string | number`)
- Developers must add `typeof savedAt === 'number'` guards or use `Number(savedAt)` coercion
- If someone accidentally sets `savedAt = new Date().toISOString()` in the future, TypeScript won't catch it

The `upsertSessionIndex` function in `sessionStorage.ts` currently sorts by **insertion position**, not by `savedAt`, so the sort bug hasn't manifested. But if history sorting is ever added (a natural feature), this will produce wrong results.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All
- Operating System: All
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Root Cause

**`src/types.ts:63`:**
```typescript
savedAt?: string | number;
```

The `string` alternative in the union is unused. It may have been added in an early version when `savedAt` was stored as an ISO date string, but all current code uses `Date.now()`.

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

1. Change `src/types.ts` line 63:
```typescript
// Before:
savedAt?: string | number;

// After:
savedAt?: number;
```

2. Run `tsc --noEmit` to find any callers that relied on the `string` form.
3. Fix any callers (there should be none, based on current codebase analysis).

---

## 📸 Evidence

```bash
$ grep -rn "savedAt\s*=" src/ --include="*.ts" | grep -v test | grep -v "string"
```
All assignments use numeric timestamps.

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟢 **Beginner** — Single-character type change + verify no regressions. Perfect first issue.

issues.title: [BUG] `[key: string]: any` index signature in options.ts Settings interface disables TypeScript type checking for all settings fields
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

The `Settings` interface in `src/options.ts` contains a `[key: string]: any` index signature on line 22. This is the TypeScript equivalent of turning off all type checking for every field in the interface — property accesses, typos, and wrong value types all compile silently without errors. The index signature was added as an escape hatch to compensate for this local interface not matching the full settings schema stored in Chrome storage.

**What went wrong?** An escape hatch was added instead of fixing the underlying interface divergence.
**What feature is affected?** TypeScript safety for all settings in the options page.
**When does the issue occur?** Silently at compile time — typos in settings property names produce `undefined` instead of a build error.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce (to observe the type safety hole)

1. Open `src/options.ts` line 10:
```typescript
interface Settings {
  summarizationInterval?: number;
  vadThreshold?: number;
  aiModel?: string;
  lateJoinerBriefing?: boolean;
  topicDetection?: boolean;
  decisionDetection?: boolean;
  actionExtraction?: boolean;
  sentimentAnalysis?: boolean;
  transcriptRefinement?: boolean;
  theme?: "system" | "light" | "dark";
  accent?: string;
  [key: string]: any;   // ← this line defeats all the typed fields above
}
```

2. Notice that `settings.vadThreshhold` (typo, double 'h') compiles without error and returns `undefined` at runtime — TypeScript cannot warn because `[key: string]: any` allows any key.

3. Notice that `settings.theme = 42` compiles without error even though `theme` is typed as `"system" | "light" | "dark"` — the index signature overrides the specific field type.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

TypeScript should produce a compile error for:
- Typos in settings property names (`settings.vadThreshhold`)
- Wrong value types (`settings.theme = 42`)
- Access to non-existent settings fields

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The index signature `[key: string]: any` causes TypeScript to accept any string key with any value on the `Settings` object, making all specifically-typed fields meaningless for type checking purposes.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All
- Operating System: All
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Root Cause

**`src/options.ts:22`:**
```typescript
[key: string]: any;  // ← added as escape hatch, disables TypeScript for all Settings fields
```

This was added because the local `Settings` interface in `options.ts` diverges from the ones in `background.ts` and `theme.ts` (see related issue #488). Rather than consolidating the interface, a catch-all was used instead.

Line 281 in `options.ts` also spreads existing settings:
```typescript
const newSettings: Settings = {
  ...settings,  // ← can carry unknown/stale fields from storage
  summarizationInterval: validatedInterval,
  // ...
};
```

Without the index signature but with proper typing, unknown fields from storage would be correctly rejected.

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

1. Consolidate the `Settings` interface into `src/types.ts` as a single exported type (see related issue #488).
2. Import it in `options.ts` instead of using the local definition.
3. Remove the `[key: string]: any` line.
4. If the `...settings` spread needs to carry unmapped fields, use explicit optional fields instead of an escape hatch.

This issue is best fixed as part of #488 (consolidating the Settings interface).

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟢 **Beginner** (standalone: remove the line) / 🟡 **Intermediate** (proper fix with #488)

issues.title: [CHORE] `config.ts` only contains 3 constants — 7+ magic numbers in background.ts and offscreen.ts are uncentralized
issues.body:
## 📌 Problem Statement

`src/config.ts` exists as the designated home for shared constants, but it only contains **3 model-name strings**. At least **7 other tunable constants** — controlling AI token budgets, transcript window sizes, audio queue depth, and VAD parameters — are declared as module-level constants directly inside `background.ts` and `offscreen.ts`. Contributors who need to tune these values must search through implementation files rather than reading a centralized config.

**What is currently missing?** A complete set of tuneable parameters in `config.ts`.
**What workflow feels frustrating?** Wanting to adjust the summarization window or token budget requires grepping through 1700+ lines of `background.ts`.

---

## 💡 Proposed Solution

Move all tuneable constants from `background.ts` and `offscreen.ts` into `src/config.ts`, with descriptive names and inline comments explaining each value.

**Constants currently in `src/background.ts` lines 26–33 that should be in config:**
```typescript
const MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH = 2000;                // AI prompt truncation limit
const TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 25;             // entries fed to summarization
const SUMMARIZATION_MAX_TOKENS = 1200;         // GPT response token budget
const JOINER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 120;         // late-joiner brief token budget
const MAX_PENDING_AUDIO_CHUNKS = 8;            // audio processing queue depth
const MIN_MEETING_DURATION_FOR_WELCOME = 10;   // seconds before welcoming late joiners
const BROADCAST_THROTTLE_MS = 500;             // state broadcast debounce interval
```

**Constants currently in `src/offscreen.ts` that belong in config:**
```typescript
const WAVEFORM_N = 32;       // waveform bar resolution
const RMS_FLOOR = 0.005;     // VAD floor threshold
```

---

## 🔄 Alternatives Considered

- **Leave them where they are** — works but creates a poor contributor experience; `config.ts` serves no purpose if it only has 3 entries.
- **Use environment variables** — overkill for a Chrome extension; constants are sufficient.

---

## 🛠️ Implementation Ideas

**`src/config.ts` after the fix:**
```typescript
// AI Model Names
export const DEFAULT_CHAT_MODEL = "gpt-4o-mini";
export const ELEVENLABS_STT_MODEL = "scribe_v2";
export const WHISPER_MODEL = "whisper-1";

// AI Processing Limits
export const MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH = 2000;
export const TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE = 25;
export const SUMMARIZATION_MAX_TOKENS = 1200;
export const JOINER_MESSAGE_MAX_TOKENS = 120;

// Audio Pipeline
export const MAX_PENDING_AUDIO_CHUNKS = 8;
export const WAVEFORM_N = 32;
export const RMS_FLOOR = 0.005;

// Meeting Behavior
export const MIN_MEETING_DURATION_FOR_WELCOME = 10;
export const BROADCAST_THROTTLE_MS = 500;
```

Then import in `background.ts` and `offscreen.ts`:
```typescript
import { MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH, TRANSCRIPT_WINDOW_SIZE, ... } from "./config";
```

---

## 📝 Additional Context

The `config.ts` file already exists and is imported by `background.ts`. This is purely additive — move constants, update the import, no behavior changes.

**Affected files:** `src/config.ts`, `src/background.ts` (lines 26–33, 402), `src/offscreen.ts`

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟢 **Beginner** — Move constants, update imports, no logic changes. Excellent first contribution.

issues.title: [Bug]: window.location.href in playground-header causes full-page reload instead of client-side navigation
issues.body:
### Short summary

The \"Back to Dashboard\" button in the playground header uses `window.location.href = '/dashboard'` instead of Next.js's `router.push()`, triggering a full browser page reload instead of a client-side SPA navigation.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any playground (`/playground/[id]`)
2. Wait for the WebContainer and Monaco editor to finish loading
3. Click the **← (Back to Dashboard)** button in the top-left of the playground header
4. Observe the browser URL bar and the page transition

### Expected behavior

The app should navigate client-side to `/dashboard` using Next.js's App Router (`router.push('/dashboard')`), preserving the SPA session without a full reload.

### Actual behavior

`window.location.href = '/dashboard'` triggers a full HTTP browser navigation. The browser:
- Discards all loaded JS bundles (Monaco Editor, WebContainer SDK, Yjs, AI state)
- Shows a white/blank flash during navigation
- Re-downloads and reinitializes the entire app from scratch

This also breaks the upcoming unsaved-changes guard (issue #427), because `window.location.href` bypasses any `router`-level navigation interceptors.

### Affected area

Playground editor

### Environment

All browsers, any OS. Reproducible in both local dev and production. The issue is purely in the source code at:

`modules/playground/components/playground-header.tsx` line 64

```tsx
// Current (wrong):
onClick={() => window.location.href = '/dashboard'}

// Fix — import useRouter from 'next/navigation' and use:
onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}
```

### Screenshots, logs, or recordings

Not required — the issue is visible as a full-page white flash and network waterfall showing all assets re-fetching.

**Relevant code:**
```tsx
// modules/playground/components/playground-header.tsx:64
<Button
    size="icon"
    variant="ghost"
    className="h-7 w-7 text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground"
    onClick={() => window.location.href = '/dashboard'}   // ← problem
    aria-label="Back to Dashboard"
>
```

**Fix:**
```tsx
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";

// inside component:
const router = useRouter();

// button onClick:
onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}
```

### Confirmation

- [x] I searched existing issues before opening this report.
- [x] I included enough detail for reproduction.

issues.title: [BUG] `safeLocalStore()` in sessionStorage.ts uses deprecated callback-style Chrome API and untyped `value: any`
[CHORE] `escapeHtml`, `formatDuration`, and `sanitizeTopicStatus` duplicated verbatim between dashboard.ts and popup.ts
[BUG] 26+ `console.log` calls in background.ts fire on every audio chunk in production — no debug flag guard
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

`src/background.ts` contains **48 total logging statements** (26 `console.log`/`console.warn`, 22 `console.error`), with several firing on **every single audio chunk** during a meeting. In a typical 1-hour meeting with 20-second audio chunks, this produces **180+ verbose log lines** in a user's Chrome DevTools console during normal, error-free operation. There is no debug flag, log level, or build-time guard — these development traces are always active in production.

**What went wrong?** Development-grade instrumentation was never gated behind a debug flag.
**What feature is affected?** Developer experience; Chrome DevTools console quality; minor service worker performance.
**When does the issue occur?** During every active recording session.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Chrome DevTools on any page (`F12`)
2. Go to the **Console** tab
3. Start a Google Meet session and begin recording with Late-Meet
4. Observe: the console is flooded with messages every few seconds:

```
[LateMeet] chunk received — ~45000 bytes  mimeType=audio/webm
[LateMeet] processing queued chunk chunk_1 — ~45000 bytes  mimeType=audio/webm
[LateMeet] transcript received for chunk chunk_1 — 142 chars
[LateMeet] transcript refined for chunk chunk_1 — 138 chars
[LateMeet] chunk received — ~43000 bytes  mimeType=audio/webm
... (repeats every ~20 seconds)
```

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The Chrome DevTools console should be **clean during normal operation**. Verbose per-chunk traces should only appear when a developer explicitly enables debug mode.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The console receives 3–4 log messages per audio chunk (every ~20s), plus additional logs on every state change. Real errors and warnings are buried in the noise.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All
- Operating System: All
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Root Cause — High-Frequency Log Statements

**`src/background.ts:1546`** — fires on every OFFSCREEN_AUDIO_CHUNK message:
```typescript
console.log(`[LateMeet] chunk received — ~${approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${message.mimeType}`);
```

**`src/background.ts:968`** — fires for each queued chunk:
```typescript
console.log(`[LateMeet] processing queued chunk ${id} — ~${item.approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${item.mimeType}`);
```

**`src/background.ts:980`** — fires after every STT call:
```typescript
console.log(`[LateMeet] transcript received for chunk ${id} — ${rawText.length} chars`);
```

**`src/background.ts:985`** — fires when `transcriptRefinement` is enabled:
```typescript
console.log(`[LateMeet] transcript refined for chunk ${id} — ${refinedText.length} chars`);
```

**`src/background.ts:1255, 1259`** — fire on each audio start attempt:
```typescript
console.log("[LateMeet] Audio already active, skipping start request.");
console.log("[LateMeet] Audio start already in progress, skipping start request.");
```

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

Add a `DEBUG` constant to `src/config.ts` and wrap all verbose per-chunk and per-state logs:

```typescript
// src/config.ts
export const DEBUG = false;  // set to true during local development
```

```typescript
// src/background.ts
import { DEBUG } from "./config";

// Before:
console.log(`[LateMeet] chunk received — ~${approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${message.mimeType}`);

// After:
if (DEBUG) console.log(`[LateMeet] chunk received — ~${approxBytes} bytes  mimeType=${message.mimeType}`);
```

`console.error` and `console.warn` calls for genuine errors should remain unconditional.

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟢 **Beginner** — Mechanical change: add `DEBUG` to `config.ts`, wrap verbose logs. Good first issue.

issues.title: [BUG] ErrorBoundary renders raw error.message in UI — potential information disclosure to end users

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug** The `ErrorBoundary` component renders the raw `Error.message` string directly inside a `
` tag visible to the end user. This can expose internal system information such as file paths, module names, database connection details, and stack-trace fragments depending on what caused the error.

**Affected code (client/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx line 44-47):**
```tsx

  {this.state.error?.message}


```

**Examples of messages that could be shown to users:**
- `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'createdBy') at getAssessments (storage.ts:47)`
- `Failed to connect to PostgreSQL: Connection refused (127.0.0.1:5432)`
- `Unexpected token '<' at /home/app/server/routes.ts:310`

These messages reveal internal module paths, dependency names, infrastructure configuration, and code structure — all useful information for an attacker performing reconnaissance.

**To Reproduce**
1. Introduce a rendering error in any child component (e.g., access `.length` on `undefined`)
2. The error message and partial stack context appear in a `
` block on the page for all users to see

**Expected behavior**
The error boundary should display only a generic, user-friendly message. The actual `error.message` and stack trace should be logged to the browser console (or a monitoring service) but never rendered in the DOM.

**Suggested fix**
```tsx
// Remove the 
 block entirely and replace with a generic message


  An unexpected error occurred. Our team has been notified.


```

And log the actual error internally:
```tsx
componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo): void {
  console.error("[ErrorBoundary] Uncaught render error:", error);
  console.error("[ErrorBoundary] Component stack:", errorInfo.componentStack);
  // Optionally: send to error monitoring (Sentry, etc.)
}
```

**Additional context**
This is a good first contribution — the fix is minimal (remove the `
` block), is safe to implement, and improves both security and UX. The `componentDidCatch` method already logs the error to the console, so no information is lost by removing the visible `
`.

[TEST] `persistMeetingSession`, `pruneSessionsForQuota`, and write-path functions in sessionStorage.ts have zero unit test coverage
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

The existing `src/sessionStorage.test.ts` only covers **read-side and utility helpers**. The entire **write path** — the code responsible for actually persisting, pruning, and deleting meeting sessions from Chrome storage — has **zero unit test coverage**. These functions have already caused one production data-loss bug (see closed issue #289), yet they still have no regression safety net.

**What went wrong?** Critical storage write functions were never tested.
**What feature is affected?** Meeting session persistence — saving, pruning, and deleting sessions.
**When does the issue occur?** Silently — bugs in the write path manifest as lost meeting data.

---

## 🔄 Current Coverage Gap

**What IS tested** in `src/sessionStorage.test.ts`:
- `getSavedSessionKey()` — naming helper
- `createSessionListItem()` — strips transcript/timeline
- `upsertSessionIndex()` — deduplication & ordering
- `isStorageQuotaError()` — error detection
- `estimateStorageBytes()` — size estimation
- `getSavedMeetingSession()` — read path

**What is NOT tested** (the write path):

| Function | Lines | Why Critical |
|---|---|---|
| `persistMeetingSession()` | 131–163 | Main write path; caused #289 data loss bug |
| `persistPendingMeetingSession()` | 113–129 | Promotes pending → permanent storage |
| `savePendingMeetingSession()` | 106–111 | Entry point for saving a completed meeting |
| `discardPendingMeetingSession()` | 165–167 | Removes pending session |
| `deleteSavedMeetingSession()` | 200–218 | Modifies both index and legacy sessions |
| `pruneSessionsForQuota()` | 71–104 | Deletes sessions to free quota — wrong pruning = data loss |

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

Each write-path function should have unit tests covering:
- Happy path (normal save)
- Duplicate session ID guard (line 145 in `persistMeetingSession`)
- Quota pruning: sessions pruned when `currentBytes + incomingBytes > STORAGE_SOFT_LIMIT_BYTES`
- Legacy session migration (`SAVED_SESSIONS_LEGACY_KEY` → indexed format)
- Error cases (storage failures)

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Zero tests exist for the write path. The complex quota-pruning loop (`pruneSessionsForQuota`, lines 71–104) — which determines which sessions get silently deleted — has never been tested in isolation.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All
- Operating System: All
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Technical Context

The test file already has a good mock storage pattern:
```typescript
const storage = {
  get: async () => ({ [getSavedSessionKey(session.id)]: session, ... }),
  set: async () => {},
  remove: async () => {},
};
```

This same pattern can be used to write tests for `persistMeetingSession` and `pruneSessionsForQuota`. No Chrome APIs need to be mocked — the functions accept a `StorageArea` interface.

**Key test cases needed for `pruneSessionsForQuota`:**
```typescript
test("pruneSessionsForQuota removes oldest sessions when quota is exceeded", async () => { ... });
test("pruneSessionsForQuota removes sessions until incoming bytes fit", async () => { ... });
test("pruneSessionsForQuota does not prune if bytes fit within limit", async () => { ... });
```

**Key test cases needed for `persistMeetingSession`:**
```typescript
test("persistMeetingSession saves session to indexed storage", async () => { ... });
test("persistMeetingSession skips duplicate session IDs", async () => { ... });
test("persistMeetingSession migrates legacy sessions to indexed format", async () => { ... });
```

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

Add ~15–20 unit tests to `src/sessionStorage.test.ts` covering all six untested functions using the existing mock storage pattern.

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟡 **Intermediate** — Requires understanding the storage schema and mock patterns. No Chrome API knowledge needed.

issues.title: [BUG] `getSettings()` defined twice in background.ts and theme.ts — different return types, no value normalization in background
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

There are **two separate `getSettings()` functions** in the codebase that both read from `chrome.storage.local` under the `"settings"` key, but return **different shapes** and have **different levels of safety**. The `theme.ts` version normalizes invalid values with safe defaults; the `background.ts` version returns raw storage values with no validation. This means theme settings are protected from corruption, but AI processing settings are not.

**What went wrong?** Two functions with the same name read the same storage key but behave differently.
**What feature is affected?** All settings-dependent behavior: summarization, theme, VAD, feature toggles.
**When does the issue occur?** Silently — if invalid/corrupted data exists in storage, `background.ts` processes it while `theme.ts` would have recovered gracefully.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce (to observe the divergence)

1. `src/background.ts` line 491:
```typescript
async function getSettings(): Promise<Settings> {
  const result = await chrome.storage.local.get("settings");
  return result.settings || {};  // ← raw storage value, no validation
}
```

2. `src/theme.ts` line 50:
```typescript
export async function getSettings(): Promise<Settings> {
  const result = await chrome.storage.local.get("settings");
  return normalizeSettings(result.settings);  // ← validates and applies safe defaults
}
```

3. The `normalizeSettings()` function in `theme.ts` validates the `theme` field and falls back to `"system"` for bad values, and validates `accent` with `isValidAccent()`. None of this protection applies to `summarizationInterval`, `aiModel`, `vadThreshold`, etc.

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

A single `getSettings()` function that returns a fully normalized, type-safe settings object with safe defaults for all fields.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

- Background service worker processes raw, unvalidated settings values — e.g., a corrupted `summarizationInterval` of `"abc"` or a negative `vadThreshold` is passed directly to the summarization loop.
- The `background.ts:747` code does have an inline guard: `const requestedInterval = Number(settings.summarizationInterval)`, but this is ad-hoc, not centralized.
- Contributors who add a new setting must remember to add their own inline guards; there is no single normalization layer.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All
- Operating System: All
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Root Cause

**`src/background.ts:491`** — raw return:
```typescript
async function getSettings(): Promise<Settings> {
  const result = await chrome.storage.local.get("settings");
  return result.settings || {};
}
```

**`src/theme.ts:50`** — normalized return:
```typescript
export async function getSettings(): Promise<Settings> {
  const result = await chrome.storage.local.get("settings");
  return normalizeSettings(result.settings);
}
```

Both are module-private (background.ts version is not exported), so they don't conflict at runtime — but they represent two divergent philosophies for the same operation.

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

1. Create a single `getSettings()` in a shared utility (e.g., `src/utils/settings.ts`) that normalizes all fields and exports it.
2. Import and use it in both `background.ts` and `theme.ts`.
3. The normalization function should cover all fields from the unified `Settings` interface (see related issue #488).

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟡 **Intermediate** — Requires understanding both modules and adding a shared utility. Best done together with #488.

issues.title: [Security] XSS vulnerability via unescaped patient data in History page PDF export (document.write)

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug** The `exportAsPdf()` function in `client/src/pages/History.tsx` constructs a raw HTML string using ES6 template literals with **unsanitized patient data fields** and then writes it directly to a new browser window using `document.write()`. This is a Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability. **Vulnerable code (History.tsx ~line 158-183):** ```ts const patientName = assessment.patientName || "Unknown Patient"; const html = `...

Patient: ${patientName}

${assessment.smokingHistory} ${assessment.bmi} ... ${(assessment.factors || []).map(f => `
  • ${f.name} — ${f.description}
    • `).join("")} `; const w = window.open("", "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer"); w.document.write(html); // ← executes any HTML/script in the string ``` None of the interpolated values (`patientName`, `smokingHistory`, `factors[].name`, `factors[].description`) are HTML-escaped before being inserted into the template. **Attack scenario:** - If a malicious actor creates an assessment with `patientName` set to `` (e.g., via a crafted CSV import or directly via the API), the script executes in the PDF preview window when any clinician clicks "Export PDF" for that patient. - The `factors` array originates from Python ML subprocess output — if that process is compromised or produces unexpected output, injection via `f.name` or `f.description` is also possible. **To Reproduce** 1. Create an assessment where `patientName` contains HTML: `TEST` 2. Go to History page 3. Click the PDF export button for that assessment 4. The word TEST appears bolded in the PDF window — confirming HTML is executed **Expected behavior** All patient data interpolated into the HTML string should be HTML-entity-escaped so that `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, `'` are rendered as text, not as markup. **Suggested fix** Add an `escapeHtml()` helper and wrap every interpolated field: ```ts function escapeHtml(str: string): string { return str .replace(/&/g, '&') .replace(//g, '>') .replace(/"/g, '"') .replace(/'/g, '''); } ``` Then use: `${escapeHtml(patientName)}`, `${escapeHtml(assessment.smokingHistory)}`, etc. **Additional context** - The server-side validation (Zod schema) allows patient names with special characters which could carry HTML payloads through to the database. - The nonce-based CSP applied by the server does NOT apply to windows opened via `window.open()` with `document.write()`.

[BUG] Wrong boolean operator in "no" health-condition filter in search_filters.ts shows incorrect patients to clinicians

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The client-side `advancedFilter()` function in `client/src/utils/search_filters.ts` uses `||` (OR) instead of `&&` (AND) when checking whether a patient has *no* comorbidities. This causes the "no" search term to match patients who actually have at least one of the conditions.

**Affected line:**
```ts
// client/src/utils/search_filters.ts — line 51
(term === "no" && (!a.hypertension || !a.heartDisease))
//                                   ^^
//                                   should be && not ||
```

**Why this is wrong:**
- The `"yes"` branch above it correctly uses `||`: `(term === "yes" && (a.hypertension || a.heartDisease))`  → patient has AT LEAST ONE condition ✓
- The `"no"` branch must be the logical complement: patient has NEITHER condition — which requires `&&`, not `||`

**Concrete example of bad behavior:**
A patient with `hypertension = true` and `heartDisease = false`:
- `!a.hypertension` → `false`
- `!a.heartDisease` → `true`
- `false || true` → **`true`** ← this patient incorrectly passes the "no" filter

So a clinician searching for patients with "no" comorbidities will see patients who actually have hypertension.

**To Reproduce**
1. Create two assessments: one with `hypertension=true, heartDisease=false` and one with both `false`
2. Go to History page and search for `no`
3. Both patients appear — the hypertensive patient should NOT appear

**Expected behavior**
Searching for `"no"` should only return patients who have NEITHER hypertension NOR heart disease.

**Suggested fix**
```ts
// Before
(term === "no" && (!a.hypertension || !a.heartDisease))

// After
(term === "no" && (!a.hypertension && !a.heartDisease))
```

A corresponding test case should be added to `client/src/utils/search_filters.test.ts`.

**Additional context**
This is a clinical safety concern — incorrect filtering of patient comorbidity data can influence downstream care decisions. The fix is a single character change (`||` → `&&`) and is an excellent beginner contribution.

issues.title: [BUG] `Ctrl+Shift+W` save-session shortcut silently conflicts with Chrome's built-in Close Window command
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

The `save-session` keyboard shortcut defined in `manifest.json` uses `Ctrl+Shift+W` (and `Command+Shift+W` on macOS), which is Chrome's **built-in shortcut to close the current window**. Chrome extensions cannot override reserved browser shortcuts. The result is that the shortcut silently never fires — pressing it closes the browser window instead of saving the session, potentially destroying all transcription data for an in-progress meeting.

**What went wrong?** The `save-session` command is registered with a key combo reserved by the browser.
**What feature is affected?** Keyboard shortcut for saving a meeting session.
**When does the issue occur?** Every time a user tries to save their session with the shortcut.

---

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Chrome and join a Google Meet session
2. Start recording with Late-Meet
3. Press `Ctrl+Shift+W` (Windows/Linux) or `Command+Shift+W` (macOS) to save the session
4. Observe: the Chrome window closes instead of saving the session

---

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The current meeting session should be saved when the user presses the configured shortcut.

---

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Chrome intercepts the shortcut before the extension receives it, closing the browser window. The meeting data is lost.

---

## 💻 Environment

- Chrome Version: All versions
- Operating System: Windows, macOS, Linux
- Extension Version: 1.2.0

---

## 🧾 Root Cause

**File:** `src/manifest.json`, lines 64–68

```json
"save-session": {
  "suggested_key": {
    "default": "Ctrl+Shift+W",   // ← Chrome built-in: Close Window
    "mac": "Command+Shift+W"      // ← macOS: also closes window
  },
  "description": "Save the current meeting session"
}
```

Chrome's reserved shortcuts cannot be overridden by extensions. `Ctrl+Shift+W` is the native "Close Window" shortcut. The same file's `Ctrl+Shift+S` conflict was already fixed in a prior PR (#425), but this shortcut was missed.

---

## 📝 Suggested Fix

Change the shortcut to a non-reserved combination. Recommended:

```json
"save-session": {
  "suggested_key": {
    "default": "Ctrl+Shift+K",
    "mac": "Command+Shift+K"
  },
  "description": "Save the current meeting session"
}
```

Other safe options: `Ctrl+Shift+Y`, `Ctrl+Shift+J`. Avoid: `Ctrl+W`, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, `Ctrl+T`, `Ctrl+N`, `Ctrl+Shift+N`.

---

## 📊 Difficulty Estimate

🟢 **Beginner** — Single-line change in `manifest.json`. Good first issue.

issues.title: [BUG] Duplicate symbol declarations in server/index.ts cause TypeScript compile error — server cannot start
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
`server/index.ts` contains two duplicate symbol declarations that produce TypeScript compile-time errors, preventing the server from building or starting.

**Duplicate 1 — `sanitizeDatabaseError` imported from two different modules:**
```ts
// Line 16
import { sanitizeDatabaseError } from "./security/sqlProtection";
// Line 22
import { sanitizeDatabaseError } from "./utils/csvSanitizer";   // ← duplicate identifier
```

**Duplicate 2 — `execFileAsync` imported from routes AND re-declared locally:**
```ts
// Line 12
import { registerRoutes, execFileAsync } from "./routes";
// ...later in the file
const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile);  // ← redeclares already-imported identifier
```

TypeScript raises `error TS2300: Duplicate identifier` for both symbols. Under strict mode this is a build-breaking error.

**Bonus bug:** The ML warmup call on startup passes a relative path `"analyze.py"` to `execFileAsync`, whereas the rest of the codebase uses the resolved absolute `analyzePyPath`. This warmup will silently fail on any deployment where CWD is not the repo root.

**To Reproduce**
1. Clone the repository
2. Run `npm run check` (the TypeScript checker)
3. Observe compile errors for duplicate identifiers in `server/index.ts`

**Expected behavior**
TypeScript compilation should succeed with no duplicate identifier errors. Each symbol should be imported or declared exactly once.

**Additional context**
- The correct `sanitizeDatabaseError` is the one in `./security/sqlProtection` — the import from `./utils/csvSanitizer` is wrong (that module does not export this function).
- The correct `execFileAsync` is already provided by the import from `./routes` — the local `const execFileAsync = promisify(execFile)` should be deleted.
- Similar duplicate-declaration bugs were previously fixed in `server/routes.ts` (#647) and `server/auth.ts` (#570) — `server/index.ts` was not covered.

issues.title: [BUG] Seed data visible to all users — getAssessments voids createdBy filter

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `seedDatabase` function in `server/routes.ts` checks `if (existing.length === 0)` to decide whether to seed. However, `storage.getAssessments()` uses a `void createdBy` pattern that ignores the `createdBy` filter — it returns ALL assessments regardless of who created them. This means:

1. If any user has created any assessment, seeding is skipped (even if the seed data was deleted)
2. The seed check doesn't actually verify that the *seed* data exists — it just checks if the table is empty

More critically, the seed data uses `createdBy: "seed@clinical-insight-engine.dev"` which is a fake email. If a real user later queries their assessments, the `getAssessments` function (which voids the `createdBy` filter) returns seed data mixed with real user data.

**Affected file:** `server/routes.ts` (seedDatabase function)

```typescript
async function seedDatabase() {
  const existing = await storage.getAssessments();  // Returns ALL assessments
  if (existing.length === 0) {  // Only seeds if table is completely empty
    // ... seeds with createdBy: "seed@clinical-insight-engine.dev"
  }
}
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Start the server in development mode — seed data is inserted
2. Log in as any user
3. Navigate to History page
4. Observe that seed data (from "seed@clinical-insight-engine.dev") appears in the user's assessment list because the `createdBy` filter is voided in `getAssessments`

**Expected behavior**

1. Seed data should not appear in real users' assessment lists
2. The `getAssessments` function should properly filter by `createdBy` when the parameter is provided

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

The `getAssessments` method in `storage.ts` has `void createdBy;` which explicitly discards the filter parameter. This was likely added as a compatibility workaround but means all users see all assessments regardless of ownership.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Re-enable the `createdBy` filter in `getAssessments` (remove the `void createdBy` line and add a proper WHERE clause)
2. Or exclude seed data from user queries by filtering out the seed email

issues.title: [BUG] Dashboard and PrivacyPolicy pages missing document.title — WCAG 2.4.2 violation

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Several pages in the application do not set `document.title`, meaning the browser tab always shows the generic "Clinical Insight Engine" title from `index.html` regardless of which page the user is on. This makes it difficult to identify tabs when multiple pages are open and hurts accessibility (screen readers announce the page title on navigation).

Pages missing `document.title`:
- `/dashboard` — should be "New Assessment | Clinical Insight Engine"
- `/privacy-policy` — should be "Privacy Policy | Clinical Insight Engine"
- `/terms` — should be "Terms | Clinical Insight Engine"
- `/` (Landing) — should be "Clinical Insight Engine" (already correct from HTML)

Pages that DO set it correctly:
- `/login` — sets "Clinical Insight Engine - Sign In" ✓
- `/history` — sets "Clinical Insight Engine - Assessment History" ✓

**Affected files:**
- `client/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx` — no `document.title` set
- `client/src/pages/PrivacyPolicy.tsx` — no `document.title` set
- `client/src/pages/Terms.tsx` — no `document.title` set

**To Reproduce**

1. Navigate to `/dashboard`
2. Check the browser tab title — it still says "Clinical Insight Engine" (generic)
3. Navigate to `/history`
4. Check the tab title — it correctly says "Clinical Insight Engine - Assessment History"

**Expected behavior**

Each page should set a descriptive `document.title` on mount so users can identify tabs and screen readers can announce page changes.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

This is a WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled) Level A requirement. Each page should have a title that describes its topic or purpose.

**Proposed fix:**
Add a `useEffect` to each affected page component:
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  document.title = "New Assessment | Clinical Insight Engine";
}, []);
```

issues.title: [BUG] HighlightText creates hundreds of RegExp instances per keystroke — performance issue

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `HighlightText` component in `client/src/pages/History.tsx` builds a regex directly from user input (the search term) without adequate sanitization. While it does escape special regex characters, the `RegExp` constructor with the `'gi'` flags and the `.split(regex)` pattern can still cause performance issues (ReDoS) with certain crafted inputs containing nested quantifiers or alternations that survive the basic escaping.

More importantly, the regex is rebuilt on every render for every cell in the table, creating potentially hundreds of `RegExp` instances per keystroke.

**Affected file:** `client/src/pages/History.tsx`

```tsx
function HighlightText({ text, search }: { text: string; search: string }) {
  if (!search.trim()) return <>{text}</>;
  
  const regex = new RegExp(`(${search.replace(/[-\/\\^$*+?.()|[\]{}]/g, '\\$&')})`, 'gi');
  const parts = text.split(regex);
  // ...
}
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Navigate to the History page with many assessments
2. Type a long or complex search string in the search box
3. Observe that a new `RegExp` is created for every `HighlightText` instance on every keystroke
4. With 50 assessments × 10+ columns = 500+ regex compilations per keystroke

**Expected behavior**

The regex should be compiled once per search term change (memoized), not once per cell render. Additionally, the component should handle edge cases where the search term could produce an invalid or expensive regex.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

While the current escaping handles most special characters, the performance concern is the primary issue — creating hundreds of `RegExp` objects per keystroke in a table with many rows causes unnecessary GC pressure and can cause visible jank on lower-powered devices.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Memoize the compiled regex at the parent level (in the `History` component) and pass it as a prop to `HighlightText`
2. Or use `useMemo` to compute the regex once per search term change
3. Add a try/catch around the `RegExp` constructor to handle any edge cases that slip through escaping

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The 404 Not Found page (`client/src/pages/not-found.tsx`) contains a "Back to Dashboard" link that points to `/dashboard`. For unauthenticated users who land on a non-existent URL, clicking this link sends them to a protected route which immediately redirects them away (to `/login` via `ProtectedRoute`). This creates a confusing UX — the 404 page should link to the landing page (`/`) instead, which is accessible to everyone.

**Affected file:** `client/src/pages/not-found.tsx`

```tsx
<Link href="/dashboard" className="...">
  Back to Dashboard
</Link>
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Open the application without being logged in
2. Navigate to a non-existent URL (e.g., `/nonexistent`)
3. See the 404 page with "Back to Dashboard" button
4. Click the button
5. Get redirected to `/login` (or `/`) because `/dashboard` requires authentication

**Expected behavior**

The 404 page should link to `/` (home/landing page) which is accessible to all users. The link text should say "Back to Home" instead of "Back to Dashboard".

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

This is a minor UX issue but affects the first impression for users who mistype a URL or follow a broken link.

**Proposed fix:**
Change the link `href` from `/dashboard` to `/` and update the text from "Back to Dashboard" to "Back to Home".

issues.title: [BUG] Google Fonts loaded twice — duplicate import in index.html and index.css

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

Google Fonts are loaded twice — once via a `<link>` tag in `client/index.html` and again via `@import url(...)` in `client/src/index.css`. This causes the browser to download the font CSS file twice, doubling the render-blocking time and wasting bandwidth.

**Affected files:**
- `client/index.html` — `<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Outfit...&family=Plus+Jakarta+Sans...&display=swap">`
- `client/src/index.css` line 1 — `@import url("https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Outfit...&family=Plus+Jakarta+Sans...&display=swap");`

**To Reproduce**

1. Open the application in a browser
2. Open DevTools → Network tab → filter by "fonts.googleapis"
3. Observe two separate requests for the Google Fonts CSS (one from the HTML link, one from the CSS @import)

**Expected behavior**

Fonts should be loaded only once — either via the HTML `<link>` tag (preferred, as it can be preloaded) or via the CSS `@import`, but not both.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

The `<link>` tag in HTML is preferred over `@import` because it can be discovered by the browser's preload scanner earlier in the page load. The `@import` in CSS is render-blocking and only discovered after the CSS file itself is parsed.

**Proposed fix:**
Remove the `@import url(...)` line from `client/src/index.css` since the fonts are already loaded via the `<link>` tag in `index.html`.

bug: ShareSheet modal lacks role="dialog" and aria-modal semantics — screen readers cannot identify it as a dialog
issues.body:
## Description The `ShareSheet` component (`components/dashboard/ShareSheet.tsx`) renders a modal overlay but lacks proper ARIA dialog semantics. The overlay `` and inner panel have no `role="dialog"`, no `aria-modal="true"`, and no `aria-labelledby` pointing to the "Share Pulse" heading. This means: 1. Screen readers do not announce it as a dialog when it opens 2. The overlay backdrop is not marked `aria-hidden="true"` — assistive tech may try to interact with it 3. There is no focus trap — Tab can escape to elements behind the overlay **File:** `components/dashboard/ShareSheet.tsx` (lines ~170-200) ```tsx // Current: plain motion.div with no dialog semantics {/* No role, no aria-modal */} ``` ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Go to any user dashboard (e.g., `/dashboard/octocat`) 2. Click the "Share" button on the ProfileCard 3. When the ShareSheet opens, use a screen reader (VoiceOver/NVDA) 4. Observe: no dialog announcement is made 5. Press Tab repeatedly — focus can escape behind the overlay ## Expected Behavior - The inner panel should have `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby="share-sheet-title"` - The heading "Share Pulse" should have `id="share-sheet-title"` - Focus should be trapped within the panel while open - Focus should move to the first interactive element when opened - Focus should return to the trigger button when closed ## Screenshots / Logs N/A — this is a screen reader / keyboard interaction issue. ## Suggested Fix ```tsx

Share Pulse

... ``` Add a focus trap using the same pattern as the Compare Profile modal fix.

issues.title: bug: /api/stats returns 500 Internal Server Error for non-existent users instead of 404
[BUG] `storageDashboard.ts` uses `confirm()` native dialog — inconsistent with custom modal pattern used elsewhere
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

`src/storageDashboard.ts` uses the browser's native `confirm()` dialog for delete confirmation:

```typescript
if (confirm("Delete this meeting's stored data?")) {
  await deleteSavedMeetingSession(chrome.storage.local, id);
}
```

This is inconsistent with the rest of the extension which uses custom-styled modals (e.g., the session save/discard modal in `popup.ts`, the delete confirmation modal in `dashboard.ts`). The native `confirm()` dialog:
1. Cannot be styled to match the extension's design system
2. Looks jarring and out-of-place next to the polished custom UI
3. Blocks the JavaScript thread
4. Has different appearance across operating systems

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the extension options page
2. Scroll to the Storage Dashboard section
3. Click "Delete" on any stored meeting
4. Observe: a native browser `confirm()` dialog appears instead of a styled modal

## ✅ Expected Behavior

A custom-styled confirmation modal consistent with the extension's design system (similar to the session save/discard modal or the delete confirmation modal in the dashboard).

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Native `confirm()` dialog that looks out of place and cannot be themed.

## 💻 Environment

- Extension Version: 1.2.0
- Affected file: `src/storageDashboard.ts` (line 113)

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Replace `confirm()` with a custom modal component, reusing the pattern from the dashboard's delete confirmation modal (`delete-confirm-modal`).

## 📝 Additional Context

- The dashboard already has a custom delete confirmation modal pattern that could be reused
- This is a UX consistency issue that affects the perceived quality of the extension

issues.title: [BUG] `options.ts` save button text hardcoded as `"Save Settings"` but actual button text is `"Save Configuration"` — mismatch on error recovery
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

In `src/options.ts`, the save button's original text is captured as a fallback for error recovery:

```typescript
const originalText = saveBtn.textContent || "Save Settings";
```

However, looking at the options.html, the actual button text may differ. More importantly, the `originalText` variable captures whatever text is currently in the button, but the fallback string `"Save Settings"` is hardcoded. If the button text is ever changed in the HTML, this fallback becomes stale.

Additionally, the save flow has a subtle UX issue: if validation fails (invalid API key), the `finally` block restores the button text, but the early `return` inside the validation check also restores it — creating two code paths that both handle restoration, making maintenance error-prone.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `src/options.ts`, find the save button click handler
2. Observe `const originalText = saveBtn.textContent || "Save Settings"`
3. The `saveBtn.textContent` correctly captures the live text, but the fallback is hardcoded
4. If `saveBtn.textContent` is empty/null (unlikely but possible during DOM manipulation), the wrong text is shown

## ✅ Expected Behavior

Button text restoration should be consistent and not rely on hardcoded fallback strings that may drift from the actual HTML.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

- Hardcoded fallback `"Save Settings"` may not match actual button text
- Two separate code paths restore button state (validation failure early return + finally block)
- The `finally` block always runs, but the early return also restores — no actual bug but confusing control flow

## 💻 Environment

- Extension Version: 1.2.0
- Affected file: `src/options.ts` (save button handler)

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Capture the original text once and use it consistently. Remove the hardcoded fallback:
```typescript
const originalText = saveBtn.textContent ?? "Save";
```

And consolidate the restoration logic into only the `finally` block to avoid duplicate paths.

## 📝 Additional Context

- This is a minor maintainability issue but reflects a pattern that could cause UI text drift
- The popup.ts has a similar pattern with `const originalText = "Save Key"` which is also hardcoded

[BUG] `popup.ts` duration timer `setInterval` is never cleared when popup closes — leaks until garbage collected
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

In `src/popup.ts`, the `startDurationTimer()` function creates a `setInterval` that updates the meeting duration display every second. However, when the popup is closed (user clicks away), the interval is never explicitly cleared. While Chrome will garbage-collect the popup's execution context, the interval runs unnecessarily for the entire time the popup is open even after the meeting section is hidden.

More critically, `startDurationTimer()` has a guard (`if (durationInterval) return`) but the interval is only cleared inside `updateUI()` when `state.isActive` becomes false. If the popup is opened, timer starts, then the meeting ends while the popup is still open, the timer continues running and updating a hidden element.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the extension popup while a meeting is active
2. Observe the duration timer counting up
3. The meeting ends (state becomes inactive)
4. The `updateUI` function hides the meeting section but the `clearInterval` only fires if `durationInterval` is truthy AND `!state.isActive`
5. If `updateUI` is not called again after the state change, the interval leaks

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The duration interval should be cleared:
1. When the meeting becomes inactive
2. When the popup is about to close (via `beforeunload` or `visibilitychange`)

## ❌ Actual Behavior

- No cleanup on popup close
- Timer continues running even when the meeting section is hidden
- The `clearInterval` path depends on `updateUI` being called with `isActive: false`

## 💻 Environment

- Extension Version: 1.2.0
- Affected file: `src/popup.ts` (lines 509-516, 611-614)

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Add a cleanup listener:
```typescript
window.addEventListener("unload", () => {
  if (durationInterval) {
    clearInterval(durationInterval);
    durationInterval = null;
  }
});
```

## 📝 Additional Context

- The dashboard.ts has a similar timer but uses `window.setInterval` which is slightly different
- No existing issue covers popup-specific timer cleanup (the closed issue #306 was about content.ts polling, not popup timers)

issues.title: [BUG] Encryption `derivedKey` persists indefinitely in memory — no auto-lock timeout after user inactivity
issues.body:
## �� Bug Description

In `src/utils/credentials.ts`, the derived encryption key (`derivedKey: CryptoKey | null`) is stored in module-level memory and never cleared automatically. Once a user enters their passphrase, the key remains in memory indefinitely until the browser is closed or the service worker is terminated. There is no inactivity timeout to re-lock credentials.

This means if a user walks away from their computer with Chrome open, anyone with physical access can view/modify API keys without re-entering the passphrase.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the extension popup or options page
2. Enter passphrase to unlock credentials
3. Wait any amount of time (hours, days)
4. Return to the extension — credentials are still unlocked without re-authentication
5. The `lockCredentials()` function exists but is never called automatically

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The encryption key should be automatically cleared after a configurable period of inactivity (e.g., 15-30 minutes), requiring the user to re-enter their passphrase.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

- `derivedKey` persists in memory indefinitely
- `lockCredentials()` is exported but never called by any timer or event
- No idle detection or auto-lock mechanism exists

## 💻 Environment

- Extension Version: 1.2.0
- Affected file: `src/utils/credentials.ts`

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Add an auto-lock timer that calls `lockCredentials()` after inactivity:
```typescript
const AUTO_LOCK_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000; // 30 minutes
let lockTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;

function resetLockTimer() {
  if (lockTimer) clearTimeout(lockTimer);
  lockTimer = setTimeout(() => lockCredentials(), AUTO_LOCK_MS);
}
```

Call `resetLockTimer()` after each successful `unlockCredentials()` and after each credential access.

## 📝 Additional Context

- The `lockCredentials()` function already exists and works correctly — it just needs to be called automatically
- Issue #112 covers API key rotation reminders but not auto-locking the encryption key
- Issue #47 covers secure storage architecture but not idle timeout behavior

[BUG] Hardcoded hex color values in popup.ts bypass theme system — dark/light mode colors are static
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

`src/popup.ts` contains multiple hardcoded hex color values (`#22C55E`, `#EF4444`, `#64748B`) applied via inline `style.color` assignments. These colors bypass the theme system defined in `theme.css` and `theme.ts`, meaning they remain static regardless of whether the user has selected light mode, dark mode, or a custom accent color.

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

2. Switch theme to light mode in options
3. Observe the passphrase status text still uses hardcoded `#22C55E` (green) and `#EF4444` (red)
4. These colors may have poor contrast against light backgrounds

## ✅ Expected Behavior

All colors should use CSS custom properties (variables) from the theme system so they adapt to the user's selected theme and maintain proper contrast ratios.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

Hardcoded colors in `popup.ts`:
- Line 35: `passphraseStatus.style.color = "#22C55E"` (success green)
- Line 38: `passphraseStatus.style.color = "#EF4444"` (error red)
- Line 61: `passphraseStatus.style.color = "#EF4444"` (error red)
- Line 120: `errorEl.style.color = "#EF4444"` (error red)
- Line 589: `style="color: #64748B"` (muted text)
- Line 648: `el.style.borderColor = "#EF4444"` (shake error)

Same issue exists in `src/options.ts`:
- Line 167: `passphraseStatus.style.color = "var(--accent-color, #22C55E)"` (partially fixed)
- Line 172: `passphraseStatus.style.color = "#EF4444"`

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Replace hardcoded colors with CSS custom properties:

```typescript
// Before
passphraseStatus.style.color = "#EF4444";
// After

```

Add the corresponding variables to `theme.css` for both light and dark themes.

## 📝 Additional Context

issues.title: [BUG] Keyboard shortcut `Ctrl+Shift+S` / `Cmd+Shift+S` conflicts with browser Save As — may not trigger extension command
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

The manifest.json defines `Ctrl+Shift+S` (Windows/Linux) and `Command+Shift+S` (Mac) as the keyboard shortcut for "toggle-recording". This conflicts with the browser-native "Save As" shortcut in Chrome, which uses the same key combination. 3. Press `Ctrl+Shift+S` (or `Cmd+Shift+S` on Mac)
4. Observe: Chrome opens "Save As" dialog instead of toggling recording
5. Go to `chrome://extensions/shortcuts` — the shortcut may show a conflict warning

## ✅ Expected Behavior

The extension keyboard shortcut should use a combination that does not conflict with built-in browser shortcuts, ensuring reliable activation.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

The shortcut conflicts with Chrome's native "Save As" (`Ctrl+Shift+S` / `Cmd+Shift+S`), making it unreliable or non-functional depending on the user's Chrome configuration.

- Extension Version: 1.2.0

issues.title: [BUG] `obscureApiKey()` and `deobscureApiKey()` in credentials.ts are dead code providing false security through base64 reversal
issues.body:
## 📌 Bug Description

`src/utils/credentials.ts` exports two functions — `obscureApiKey()` and `deobscureApiKey()` — that are never imported or used anywhere in the codebase. These functions implement a trivially reversible "obfuscation" (base64 encode → reverse string) that provides zero actual security.

```typescript
export function obscureApiKey(key: string): string {
  return btoa(key).split("").reverse().join("");
}
export function deobscureApiKey(val: string): string {
  return atob(val.split("").reverse().join(""));
}
```

## 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Open `src/utils/credentials.ts` — observe the two exported functions at the bottom
2. Search the entire codebase for any import of `obscureApiKey` or `deobscureApiKey` — zero results
3. The functions are exported but never consumed

## ✅ Expected Behavior

Dead code should be removed. Security-related utilities should either provide real protection or not exist at all.

## ❌ Actual Behavior

- Two unused functions are exported from a security-critical file
- They implement trivially reversible obfuscation (not encryption)
- Their presence may mislead contributors into thinking they provide security
- The real encryption in the same file uses AES-256-GCM (proper), making these functions confusing

## 💻 Environment

- Extension Version: 1.2.0
- Affected file: `src/utils/credentials.ts` (lines 257-263)

## 🛠️ Suggested Fix

Delete both functions entirely. The file already has proper AES-256-GCM encryption via `encrypt()`/`decrypt()` — these base64 reversal functions serve no purpose.

## 📝 Additional Context

## Description The `GrowthTrendChart` component defines SVG `` elements (gradients and filters) with **hardcoded `id` attributes**. If this component is rendered more than once on the same page, the duplicate IDs cause SVG rendering corruption — browsers resolve `url(#gradient-area-a)` to the **first** matching element in the DOM, causing gradients and filters to reference the wrong chart. ```tsx // components/dashboard/GrowthTrendChart.tsx // ← Hardcoded, will collide // ← Hardcoded, will collide // ← Hardcoded, will collide // ← Hardcoded, will collide // Later referenced as: ``` While the component is currently rendered once in the compare view, this is a latent bug that will surface if: - The component is reused in other dashboard sections - Multiple compare views are rendered (e.g., in a report/export) - The component is used in Storybook or testing environments with multiple instances **File:** `components/dashboard/GrowthTrendChart.tsx` (lines ~80-100, the `` block) ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Render two `` instances on the same page (e.g., in a test or by duplicating the component in the compare view) 2. Observe that the second chart's gradients and glow filters reference the first chart's `` 3. The second chart will display incorrect gradient colors or missing glow effects **Minimal reproduction:** ```tsx
// Second chart will use first chart's gradients ``` ## Expected Behavior - Each `GrowthTrendChart` instance should have **unique** SVG `` IDs - Gradients and filters should always reference their own chart's definitions - Multiple instances should render independently without visual interference ## Screenshots / Logs N/A — this is a DOM ID collision issue visible when inspecting the SVG elements. ## Suggested Fix Use React's `useId()` hook (available since React 18) to generate unique prefixes: ```tsx import { useId } from "react"; export default function GrowthTrendChart({ ... }) { const id = useId(); return ( ); } ``` This ensures each instance gets unique IDs regardless of how many render on the page. ## Impact - **Visual corruption:** Wrong gradients/filters applied to charts when multiple instances exist - **Reusability:** Component cannot be safely reused in other contexts - **Testing:** Snapshot tests with multiple instances will produce incorrect renders - **HTML validity:** Duplicate IDs violate the HTML spec

issues.title: bug: GET /api/notify exposes user email addresses without authentication (PII leak)
issues.body:
## Description

The `GET /api/notify?user=<username>` endpoint returns the full email address of any registered user to **any unauthenticated caller**. There is no authentication, authorization, or ownership verification. Anyone who knows (or guesses) a GitHub username can retrieve their private email from the database.

```typescript
// Anyone can call:
// GET /api/notify?user=octocat
// Response includes the full email:
// { success: true, data: { username: "octocat", email: "user@private.com", frequency: "daily", ... } }
```

This is a **Personally Identifiable Information (PII) leak** that could enable targeted phishing, spam, or violate privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA).

**File:** `app/api/notify/route.ts` (GET handler, lines ~80-130)

> **Note:** Issue #2067 covers rate limiting and Zod validation for this endpoint, but does NOT mention the unauthenticated email exposure. This is a distinct security/privacy concern.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Register notification preferences via `POST /api/notify` with a username and email
2. From any browser or tool (no auth needed), call `GET /api/notify?user=<that-username>`
3. Observe the full email address is returned in the JSON response
4. Repeat with any other registered username to harvest emails

## Expected Behavior

- The GET endpoint should NOT expose the full email address to unauthenticated callers
- At minimum, the email should be masked (e.g., `u***r@gm***.com`) in unauthenticated responses
- Ideally, reading notification preferences should require some form of ownership verification (e.g., a token sent to the email, or session-based auth)
- The endpoint should only return preference metadata (frequency, flags) without PII

## Screenshots / Logs

N/A — this is a logic/design issue, not a visual bug.

## Suggested Fix

Option A (Quick fix): Remove the `email` field from the GET response entirely, or mask it:
```typescript
return NextResponse.json({
  success: true,
  message: "Notification preferences fetched successfully.",
  data: {
    username: notification.username,
    email: maskEmail(notification.email), // e.g., "u***@gmail.com"
    frequency: notification.frequency,
    preferences: { ... },
  },
});
```

Option B (Proper fix): Add authentication — require a secret token (generated on POST and emailed to the user) to read preferences.

## Impact

- **Security:** Any user's email can be enumerated by iterating known GitHub usernames
- **Privacy:** Violates user expectations and potentially GDPR/CCPA
- **Trust:** Users registering for notifications don't expect their email to be publicly queryable

issues.title: [BUG] pendingOtps and registeredUsers Maps never cleaned up — unbounded memory growth

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `pendingOtps` Map in `server/auth.ts` stores OTP entries with a 10-minute expiry but **never cleans up expired entries**. Unlike the rate limiter (which now has periodic cleanup), the OTP store grows unboundedly as users log in. Each login/register attempt adds an entry, and entries are only removed on successful verification or explicit expiry check during a verification attempt.

If a user requests an OTP but never verifies it (abandons the flow), the entry stays in memory forever. Over time with many users, this constitutes a memory leak.

The same issue applies to the `registeredUsers` Map — users registered in-memory are never persisted to the database cleanup cycle and accumulate indefinitely.

**Affected file:** `server/auth.ts`

```typescript
const pendingOtps = new Map<string, PendingOtp>();  // Never cleaned up
const registeredUsers = new Map<string, RegisteredUser>();  // Never cleaned up
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Start the server
2. Send multiple login requests (each generates an OTP entry)
3. Do NOT verify any of the OTPs
4. Monitor memory usage over time
5. Observe that `pendingOtps` Map grows with each unverified login attempt

**Expected behavior**

Expired OTP entries should be periodically cleaned up (similar to how the rate limiter now handles cleanup). The in-memory `registeredUsers` store should either be removed entirely (since users are now persisted to the database) or have a size cap.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: N/A (server-side issue)

**Additional context**

The `pendingOtps` entries have an `expiresAt` timestamp, making cleanup straightforward. A periodic interval (e.g., every 5 minutes) can iterate and delete entries where `Date.now() > expiresAt`. The `registeredUsers` Map appears to be a legacy artifact since the auth system now uses the database — it could potentially be removed entirely.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Add a periodic cleanup interval for `pendingOtps` (delete entries where `Date.now() > expiresAt`)
2. Either remove the `registeredUsers` Map entirely (since DB is now the source of truth) or add a size cap
3. Use `.unref()` on the cleanup timer to allow graceful process exit

issues.title: [BUG] queryClient staleTime: Infinity prevents assessments list from refreshing

labels.name: type:bug
labels.description: Something isn't working or throwing errors.

labels.name: level:intermediate
labels.description: Requires standard familiarity with the codebase.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

The `queryClient` in `client/src/lib/queryClient.ts` sets `staleTime: Infinity` as the global default for all queries. This means data fetched once is **never** considered stale — it will not be refetched on window focus, component remount, or interval. Combined with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `refetchInterval: false`, the assessments list on the History page will never update unless the user manually triggers a mutation that calls `invalidateQueries`.

This causes a real problem: if a clinician creates an assessment, navigates to History, then creates another assessment and navigates back to History, the second assessment may not appear because the cached data is still considered fresh.

**Affected file:** `client/src/lib/queryClient.ts`

```typescript
export const queryClient = new QueryClient({
  defaultOptions: {
    queries: {
      staleTime: Infinity,        // Data is NEVER stale
      refetchOnWindowFocus: false, // No refetch on tab switch
      refetchInterval: false,      // No polling
      retry: false,
    },
  },
});
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Log in and create an assessment from the Dashboard
2. Navigate to History — the new assessment appears (because `invalidateQueries` is called on mutation success)
3. Open a second browser tab, create another assessment there
4. Switch back to the first tab's History page
5. The second assessment does NOT appear — the data is cached with `staleTime: Infinity`

**Expected behavior**

Assessment data should be refetched when it might be stale. A reasonable `staleTime` (e.g., 30 seconds or 1 minute) would allow the cache to serve instant responses for quick navigations while still refreshing data that may have changed.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

- OS: Any
- Browser: Any

**Additional context**

The `useAuth` hook already overrides with `staleTime: 5 * 60 * 1000` (5 minutes) for the auth check, which is reasonable. The assessments list should have a similar finite staleTime since clinical data can change between tabs or sessions.

**Proposed fix:**
1. Change the global `staleTime` from `Infinity` to a reasonable value (e.g., `30 * 1000` — 30 seconds)
2. Optionally re-enable `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` so data refreshes when the user returns to the tab
3. Keep `retry: false` since the app already handles errors gracefully

issues.title: [BUG] analyze.py uses relative paths for DATA_FILE — breaks in production/Docker

labels.name: level:beginner
